`web/src/BoardMark.tsx`:

```tsx
// The door's board: an ORIGINAL drawing, and the one picture on the setup
// screens (M6.5c2, R-6.5c2.6; spec §2.2).
//
// **Never a crop of the card art.** `ASSETS.md` carves the card and tile
// images out as carrying no grant of any kind, and these screens must stand
// without them for a self-hoster or a public release. So the board is DRAWN,
// in the app icon's spirit (`web/public/icons/icon.svg`): the ten areas of a
// two-player board in its 4/3/2/1 pyramid, brick-offset by centring the way
// `board_gen` lays one out, with two presidents and five assistants on it.
//
// **Tinted by what each area trades, in the stylesheet's own trade colours**:
// the four goods at the four production areas, the yen at the bank, victory
// points at the port and imported goods at customs. The three areas that trade
// no good — the church, the laboratory and the employment agency — are the
// neutral greys. Chinatown is not on a two-player board, so it is not here.
// The hues are CLASSES (`styles.css`, "the board mark"), so a token changed
// there changes the drawing and no colour is restated in this file.

import { seatClass } from "./Cards";
import type { PlayerColor } from "./types";

/** What a tile trades: a class `styles.css` colours. */
export type Trade = "copper" | "silk" | "tea" | "seafood" | "yen" | "vp" | "imports" | "neutral" | "faint";

/** One tile: its row from the top, its place in the row, what it trades, and
 *  how strongly it is tinted (the approved mock's own weights). */
export interface Tile {
  row: number;
  col: number;
  trade: Trade;
  alpha: number;
}

/** The two-player board: rows of four, three, two and one. */
export const TILES: readonly Tile[] = [
  { row: 0, col: 0, trade: "neutral", alpha: 0.55 }, // the church
  { row: 0, col: 1, trade: "tea", alpha: 0.62 }, // the tea plantation
  { row: 0, col: 2, trade: "seafood", alpha: 0.55 }, // the fishing ground
  { row: 0, col: 3, trade: "silk", alpha: 0.45 }, // the silk mill
  { row: 1, col: 0, trade: "vp", alpha: 0.6 }, // the port
  { row: 1, col: 1, trade: "copper", alpha: 0.65 }, // the copper mine
  { row: 1, col: 2, trade: "yen", alpha: 0.85 }, // the bank
  { row: 2, col: 0, trade: "imports", alpha: 0.6 }, // customs
  { row: 2, col: 1, trade: "faint", alpha: 0.5 }, // the laboratory
  { row: 3, col: 0, trade: "neutral", alpha: 0.45 }, // the employment agency
];

/** The drawing's own units: a tile is 96 by 68, a row 76 below the last and
 *  half a step (54) further in, a column 108 along. */
const W = 96;
const H = 68;
const STEP = 108;
const ROW = 76;
const INDENT = [0, 54, 108, 162] as const;

const PRESIDENTS: readonly { x: number; y: number; seat: PlayerColor }[] = [
  { x: 176, y: 30, seat: "Blue" },
  { x: 336, y: 104, seat: "Red" },
];

const CUBES: readonly { x: number; y: number; seat: PlayerColor }[] = [
  { x: 182, y: 116, seat: "Red" },
  { x: 199, y: 116, seat: "Red" },
  { x: 244, y: 40, seat: "Blue" },
  { x: 128, y: 192, seat: "Red" },
  { x: 236, y: 192, seat: "Blue" },
];

export function BoardMark({ width }: { width: number }) {
  return (
    <svg
      className="board-mark"
      width={width}
      height={Math.round((width * 296) / 420)}
      viewBox="0 0 420 296"
      aria-hidden="true"
      focusable="false"
    >
      <g className="bm-tiles">
        {TILES.map((t) => (
          <rect
            key={`${t.row}-${t.col}`}
            className={`bm-tile ${t.trade}`}
            data-row={t.row}
            x={INDENT[t.row]! + t.col * STEP}
            y={t.row * ROW}
            width={W}
            height={H}
            rx={7}
            fillOpacity={t.alpha}
          />
        ))}
      </g>
      {PRESIDENTS.map((p) => (
        <g key={`${p.x}-${p.y}`} className={`bm-president ${seatClass(p.seat)}`}>
          <circle className="bm-disc" cx={p.x} cy={p.y} r={12} />
          <circle className="bm-hole" cx={p.x} cy={p.y} r={5} />
        </g>
      ))}
      {CUBES.map((c) => (
        <rect
          key={`${c.x}-${c.y}`}
          className={`bm-cube ${seatClass(c.seat)}`}
          x={c.x}
          y={c.y}
          width={13}
          height={13}
          rx={2}
        />
      ))}
    </svg>
  );
}
```

`web/src/Chips.tsx`:

```tsx
// The small marks the setup screens share (M6.5c2, spec §2.2): a seat, the
// password a table asks for, and the bot's version.
//
// **Colour means one thing each, as it does everywhere in this client**: a
// seat's dot is the seat's colour, gold is "to move", orange is the password,
// the yen gold outline is the bot. The hues are the stylesheet's.

import { seatClass } from "./Cards";
import type { PlayerColor } from "./types";

/** The padlock, DRAWN (spec §2.2: "not an emoji", which renders differently on
 *  every system and announces as nothing useful). Decoration wherever it is
 *  used — the tag and the action buttons each carry their own words. */
export function Padlock({ size = 11 }: { size?: number }) {
  return (
    <svg
      className="padlock"
      width={size}
      height={size}
      viewBox="0 0 16 16"
      aria-hidden="true"
      focusable="false"
    >
      <rect x="3" y="7" width="10" height="7.5" rx="1.5" />
      <path d="M5.2 7V5.2a2.8 2.8 0 0 1 5.6 0V7" />
    </svg>
  );
}

/** One seat at a table: a dot in its colour and who is there.
 *
 *  The colour is the dot's accessible NAME (`role="img"`), so a screen reader
 *  hears "Blue, Alice" and the chip's text is the label alone — which is what
 *  a row's words, and the cells that read them, are made of. An open seat has
 *  no dot: nobody's colour sits there yet. */
export function SeatChip({
  color,
  label,
  open = false,
  toMove = false,
}: {
  color: PlayerColor;
  label: string;
  open?: boolean;
  toMove?: boolean;
}) {
  const cls = ["seat-chip", open ? "open" : "", toMove ? "to-move" : ""].filter(Boolean).join(" ");
  return (
    <span className={cls}>
      {!open && <i className={`seat-dot ${seatClass(color)}`} role="img" aria-label={color} />}
      {label}
    </span>
  );
}

/** The table asks for a password (R-6.5c2.7). Named for what it MEANS: the
 *  word "Password" alone reads as a field label. */
export function PasswordTag() {
  return (
    <span className="password-tag" role="img" aria-label="password required">
      <Padlock />
      Password
    </span>
  );
}

/** The bot's version (R-6.5c2.10): a label, never a choice. */
export function VersionTag({ label }: { label: string }) {
  return (
    <span className="version-tag" title="the bot's version">
      {label}
    </span>
  );
}
```

`web/src/SeatCard.tsx`:

```tsx
// One seat at a table that is filling (M6.5c2, spec §2.2; mocks 08 and 09).
//
// The seat's colour is the card's `color` (its seat class), so the band and
// the caption take it from `currentColor` and nothing restates a hue. A card is
// a REGION named by its caption, which is what lets a screen reader — and a
// cell — find "Blue" among four seats.

import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { seatClass } from "./Cards";
import type { PlayerColor } from "./types";

export function SeatCard({
  color,
  caption,
  who,
  note,
  action,
  open = false,
}: {
  color: PlayerColor;
  /** "Red · first player", "Blue" — shown in small capitals, in the seat's colour. */
  caption: string;
  /** Who is there: a name, "You", "Open seat". */
  who: ReactNode;
  /** One quiet line under it: "seated", "yours if you join". */
  note?: string;
  /** A control for this seat — "Sit here" — or nothing. */
  action?: ReactNode;
  /** Nobody has taken it: drawn dashed, on no ground. */
  open?: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <section className={`seat-card ${seatClass(color)}${open ? " open" : ""}`} aria-label={caption}>
      <div className="seat-card-band" aria-hidden="true" />
      <div className="seat-card-in">
        <p className="seat-card-caption">{caption}</p>
        <p className="seat-card-who">{who}</p>
        {note && <p className="seat-card-note">{note}</p>}
        {action}
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}
```

`web/src/Band.tsx`:

```tsx
// The band across the top of every setup screen but the door, and the corner
// that says who is playing (M6.5c2, R-6.5c2.3 – .5; spec §2.1 and §2.2; mocks
// 02, 03, 05 and 11).
//
// **The corner answers "who am I here?" in the door's own terms** (spec §2.1).
// Under the OPEN door the name a player chose IS their identity — its key is
// what every seat of theirs is bound to — so the one thing to offer is to
// become somebody else: "switch player". Behind Cloudflare Access (the
// `cf-access` and `worker` doors) the identity is Access's and nothing this
// browser stores can change it, so what is offered is the name OTHERS see:
// "change name". Either way the identity shown is the SERVER's `me.user` —
// never what this browser happens to store under `yokohama.claimed_user`, which
// behind Access is a stale header the server ignores (Review Focus 3).

import { Fragment, useEffect, useId, useRef, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { clearDisplayName, displayName, setDisplayName } from "./api";
import type { Me } from "./types";

/** The app mark at band size: the icon's own pyramid and its two colours
 *  (`web/public/icons/icon.svg`, whose geometry this is), so the band and the
 *  installed icon are one object. `[x, y, lit, weight]`. */
const ICON_TILES = [
  [35, 113, false, 0.92],
  [149, 113, false, 0.92],
  [263, 113, false, 0.92],
  [377, 113, false, 0.92],
  [92, 213, false, 0.78],
  [206, 213, true, 1],
  [320, 213, false, 0.78],
  [149, 313, false, 0.62],
  [263, 313, false, 0.62],
] as const;

function BandMark() {
  return (
    <svg
      className="band-mark"
      width={30}
      height={22}
      viewBox="30 110 450 292"
      aria-hidden="true"
      focusable="false"
    >
      {ICON_TILES.map(([x, y, lit, weight]) => (
        <rect
          key={`${x}-${y}`}
          x={x}
          y={y}
          width={100}
          height={86}
          rx={14}
          className={lit ? "lit" : undefined}
          fillOpacity={weight}
        />
      ))}
    </svg>
  );
}

/** The band: the mark, the product, where you are, and the corner.
 *
 *  **The LAST crumb is the page's heading** (`<h2>`); the ones before it are
 *  the path to it, not headings. So the lobby's band is the lobby's heading,
 *  and a form under "Lobby / New table" is headed "New table" here — a card
 *  below the band titles itself at a lower level. */
export function LobbyBand({ crumbs, corner }: { crumbs: string[]; corner: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <header className="lobby-band">
      <div className="band-brand">
        <BandMark />
        <h1>Yokohama</h1>
        {crumbs.map((crumb, i) => (
          <Fragment key={`${i}-${crumb}`}>
            <span className="crumb-sep" aria-hidden="true">
              /
            </span>
            {i === crumbs.length - 1 ? (
              <h2 className="crumb">{crumb}</h2>
            ) : (
              <span className="crumb">{crumb}</span>
            )}
          </Fragment>
        ))}
      </div>
      <div className="band-corner">{corner}</div>
    </header>
  );
}

/** Who is playing, and the one thing the door lets them change.
 *
 *  **One set of controls, two layouts.** At desktop width the menu sits
 *  inline ("Playing as Ben · switch player"); at phone width the stylesheet
 *  hides it behind the pill ("Ben ▾"), which is a disclosure over the SAME
 *  element — so there is never a second "switch player" for anything to find.
 *
 *  `onChange` fires on switch player only, AFTER the display name is dropped:
 *  the host re-asks `/api/me` (App passes `signOut`, which drops the claimed
 *  name too). A display-name edit changes no identity and tells nobody. */
export function IdentityCorner({ me, onChange }: { me: Me; onChange: () => void }) {
  const menuId = useId();
  const fieldId = useId();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [editing, setEditing] = useState(false);
  const [shown, setShown] = useState<string | null>(() => displayName());
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState("");
  const field = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (editing) field.current?.focus();
  }, [editing]);
  if (me.user === null) return null;
  const name = shown ?? me.user;
  const edge = me.mode !== "open";
  const save = () => {
    const trimmed = draft.trim();
    if (trimmed) setDisplayName(trimmed);
    else clearDisplayName();
    setShown(trimmed || null);
    setEditing(false);
  };
  return (
    <div className="identity-corner" data-open={open ? "true" : "false"}>
      <button
        type="button"
        className="identity-pill"
        aria-expanded={open}
        aria-controls={menuId}
        onClick={() => setOpen((o) => !o)}
      >
        <i aria-hidden="true" />
        <span className="identity-pill-name">{name}</span>
        <span aria-hidden="true"> ▾</span>
      </button>
      <div className="identity-menu" id={menuId}>
        {editing ? (
          <form
            className="identity-edit"
            onSubmit={(e) => {
              e.preventDefault();
              save();
            }}
          >
            <label className="sr-only" htmlFor={fieldId}>
              Your name
            </label>
            <input
              ref={field}
              id={fieldId}
              value={draft}
              maxLength={64}
              onChange={(e) => setDraft(e.target.value)}
            />
            <button type="submit" className="ghost">
              save
            </button>
            <button type="button" className="ghost" onClick={() => setEditing(false)}>
              cancel
            </button>
          </form>
        ) : (
          <>
            <span className="identity-who">
              Playing as <b title={me.user}>{name}</b>
            </span>
            {edge && shown !== null && <span className="identity-address">{me.user}</span>}
            {edge ? (
              <button
                type="button"
                className="ghost"
                onClick={() => {
                  setDraft(shown ?? "");
                  setEditing(true);
                }}
              >
                change name
              </button>
            ) : (
              <button
                type="button"
                className="ghost"
                onClick={() => {
                  clearDisplayName();
                  onChange();
                }}
              >
                switch player
              </button>
            )}
          </>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

The 64-character cap on the field is the server's own seat-name rule (`tables.rs:466-476`, `check_name`), so the
corner never stores a name every create and join would then refuse.

Append at the end of the file:

```css
/* ---- M6.5c2: the setup screens' shared parts (R-6.5c2.6 – .9; spec §2.2) ----
 *
 * The approved mocks (`docs/plans/2026-09-26-web-frontend-m6.5c2-mocks/`),
 * built in this stylesheet's own tokens. No new colour role: the seats' dots
 * are the seats', gold is "yours" and "to move", orange is the password, the
 * yen gold is the bot and this device, the VP blue the server. Every rule is
 * scoped to a class this block introduces, so nothing the game screen draws is
 * restyled. */

/* Focus, visibly, on every control the setup screens draw. */
.front-door :focus-visible, .lobby :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--vp); outline-offset: 2px; }

/* A raised card with a coloured top band: the door's three, the state cards,
   the name step, the forms. */
.raised-card {
  background: var(--bg-raised); border: 1px solid var(--line-bright); border-radius: 8px;
  overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 0 10px 30px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45);
}
.raised-card > .card-band { height: 8px; background: var(--line-bright); }
.raised-card > .card-band.yen { background: var(--yen); }
.raised-card > .card-band.vp { background: var(--vp); }
.raised-card > .card-band.warn { background: var(--warn); }
.raised-card > .card-in { padding: 1rem 1.15rem 1.15rem; }
.raised-card h2 { font-size: 21px; font-weight: 600; margin: 0.25rem 0 0.4rem; }
.raised-card .lede { color: var(--fg-dim); margin: 0 0 0.9rem; }
/* Two selectors, because a cap can BE a card's heading (the device card's "On
   this device" is its `h2`), and `.raised-card h2` would otherwise out-rank it. */
.card-cap, .raised-card .card-cap {
  font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.14em;
  text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--fg-faint); margin: 0;
}

/* The two filled controls: the yen gold one is the bot's and this device's,
   and a LINK in `button.primary`'s box for a navigation (`/enter`). */
button.primary.yen { background: var(--yen); color: var(--bg); }
a.primary-link {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.45rem;
  background: var(--vp); color: var(--bg); border: 0; border-radius: var(--radius);
  padding: 0.5rem 1.05rem; font: inherit; font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none;
}

/* The board mark: the door's drawing (`BoardMark.tsx`). One class per trade. */
.board-mark { display: block; max-width: 100%; height: auto; }
.board-mark .bm-tiles { filter: drop-shadow(0 6px 6px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5)); }
.board-mark .bm-tile { stroke: var(--fg); stroke-opacity: 0.16; stroke-width: 1; }
.bm-tile.copper { fill: var(--copper); }
.bm-tile.silk { fill: var(--silk); }
.bm-tile.tea { fill: var(--tea); }
.bm-tile.seafood { fill: var(--seafood); }
.bm-tile.yen { fill: var(--yen); }
.bm-tile.vp { fill: var(--vp); }
.bm-tile.imports { fill: var(--imports); }
.bm-tile.neutral { fill: var(--fg-dim); }
.bm-tile.faint { fill: var(--fg-faint); }
.bm-president .bm-disc { fill: currentColor; stroke: var(--bg); stroke-width: 3; }
.bm-president .bm-hole { fill: var(--bg); fill-opacity: 0.35; }
.bm-cube { fill: currentColor; stroke: var(--bg); stroke-width: 2; }

/* The band. Its side padding lines its content up with the lobby body's
   68rem column (Task 11: `.lobby-body` is 72rem less 2rem a side). */
.lobby-band {
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem;
  min-height: 64px; padding: 0.6rem max(2rem, calc(50% - 34rem));
  background: radial-gradient(ellipse 50% 160% at 80% 0%, var(--ground-glow) 0%, var(--ground-deep) 50%, var(--bg) 100%);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);
}
.band-brand { display: flex; align-items: baseline; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.2rem 0.55rem; min-width: 0; }
.band-brand .band-mark { align-self: center; flex: 0 0 auto; }
.band-mark rect { fill: var(--vp); }
.band-mark rect.lit { fill: var(--yen); }
.band-brand h1 { font-size: 22px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0; }
.band-brand .crumb, .band-brand .crumb-sep {
  font-family: var(--display); font-size: 18px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--fg-dim); margin: 0;
}
.band-corner { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6rem; flex: 0 0 auto; font-size: 12px; color: var(--fg-dim); }
.band-corner a {
  color: var(--fg-dim); text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: var(--line-bright);
  text-underline-offset: 3px;
}

/* The identity corner: inline at desktop width, a pill on a phone. */
.identity-corner { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; }
.identity-menu { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: flex-end; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.6rem; }
.identity-who { color: var(--fg-dim); white-space: nowrap; }
.identity-who b { color: var(--fg); font-weight: 700; }
.identity-address { color: var(--fg-faint); overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.identity-menu button.ghost, .identity-edit button.ghost { padding: 0.15rem 0.5rem; font-size: 12px; }
.identity-edit { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.35rem; }
.identity-edit input {
  font: inherit; font-size: 12px; width: 11rem; background: var(--bg-sunken); color: var(--fg);
  border: 1px solid var(--line-bright); border-radius: var(--radius); padding: 0.2rem 0.4rem;
}
.identity-pill {
  display: none; align-items: center; gap: 0.4rem; max-width: 11rem; font: inherit; font-size: 12px;
  color: var(--fg); background: transparent; border: 1px solid var(--line-bright); border-radius: 99px;
  padding: 0.2rem 0.65rem; cursor: pointer;
}
.identity-pill i { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--vp); flex: 0 0 auto; }
.identity-pill-name { min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }

/* The seat chip, the password tag and the version tag. */
.seat-chip {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; max-width: 100%;
  border: 1px solid var(--line-bright); border-radius: 99px; padding: 2px 9px 2px 6px;
  font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--fg); overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
.seat-chip.open { border-style: dashed; color: var(--fg-faint); padding-left: 9px; }
.seat-chip.to-move { border-color: var(--yen); color: var(--yen); }
.seat-dot { width: 9px; height: 9px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; flex: 0 0 auto; }
.password-tag {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 10.5px;
  font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; line-height: 1.4;
  color: var(--warn); border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--warn) 55%, transparent);
  background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--warn) 8%, transparent); border-radius: 3px; padding: 1px 6px;
}
.padlock rect, .padlock path { fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.6; }
.version-tag {
  display: inline-block; margin-left: 0.2rem; vertical-align: 0.2em; font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.06em; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--yen);
  border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--yen) 45%, transparent); border-radius: 3px; padding: 0 5px;
}

/* The seat card: the card's own colour is its seat's (`seatClass`), so the band
   and the caption read it from `currentColor`. */
.seat-card {
  min-width: 0; background: var(--bg-raised); border: 1px solid var(--line-bright);
  border-radius: 8px; overflow: hidden;
}
.seat-card-band { height: 6px; background: currentColor; }
.seat-card-in { padding: 0.65rem 0.8rem 0.75rem; }
.seat-card-caption {
  margin: 0; font-size: 10.5px; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: currentColor;
}
.seat-card-who {
  margin: 0.2rem 0 0.1rem; font-family: var(--display); font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--fg); overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
.seat-card-note { margin: 0; font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--fg-faint); }
.seat-card.open { border-style: dashed; background: transparent; }
.seat-card.open .seat-card-band { opacity: 0.45; }
.seat-card.open .seat-card-who { color: var(--fg-dim); }

/* The phone (mock 11): the corner becomes a pill whose menu drops below it. */
@media (max-width: 600px) {
  .lobby-band { padding: 0.55rem 1rem; }
  .band-brand .band-mark { display: none; }
  .band-brand h1 { font-size: 19px; }
  .band-brand .crumb, .band-brand .crumb-sep { font-size: 16px; }
  .identity-pill { display: inline-flex; min-height: 36px; }
  .identity-menu {
    display: none; position: absolute; right: 0; top: calc(100% + 0.5rem); z-index: 20;
    flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-end; gap: 0.45rem;
    min-width: 12rem; max-width: calc(100vw - 2rem); padding: 0.65rem 0.75rem;
    background: var(--bg-raised); border: 1px solid var(--line-bright); border-radius: 8px;
    box-shadow: 0 10px 30px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45);
  }
  .identity-corner[data-open="true"] .identity-menu { display: flex; }
  .identity-who { white-space: normal; }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: The check and its declaration.** `web/scripts/project-url.mjs`:

```js
// The door's project link, checked where the BUILD reads it (M6.5c2,
// R-6.5c2.6; spec §2.3).
//
// `vite.config.ts` calls this with `process.env.YOKOHAMA_PROJECT_URL`, and a
// throw here fails `vite build` — the Worker's release build and the Docker
// image's `build:client` alike — naming the variable and the reason. The rule:
// unset or empty is no link; otherwise an absolute `https://` or `http://` URL
// with a host, no whitespace or control character, at most 200 characters.
//
// **Build time, never run time**: the release is precached under a digest of
// its own bytes, so a server that rewrote `index.html` at start-up would fail
// the service worker's install check. A plain module with a declaration beside
// it (`project-url.d.mts`), so the node project type-checks the config.

export const PROJECT_URL_VAR = "YOKOHAMA_PROJECT_URL";
export const PROJECT_URL_MAX = 200;

/**
 * @param {string | undefined} raw
 * @returns {string | null}
 */
export function checkProjectUrl(raw) {
  if (raw === undefined || raw === "") return null;
  /** @param {string} why @returns {never} */
  const refuse = (why) => {
    throw new Error(`${PROJECT_URL_VAR} ${why}: ${JSON.stringify(raw)}`);
  };
  if (raw.length > PROJECT_URL_MAX) refuse(`is longer than ${PROJECT_URL_MAX} characters`);
  if (/[\s\u0000-\u001f\u007f-\u009f]/u.test(raw)) refuse("holds whitespace or a control character");
  if (!/^https?:\/\//i.test(raw)) refuse("must begin with https:// or http://");
  let url;
  try {
    url = new URL(raw);
  } catch {
    refuse("is not a URL");
  }
  if (url.hostname === "") refuse("names no host");
  return raw;
}
```

```ts
/** `web/scripts/project-url.mjs`'s declaration, for the node project that
 *  type-checks `vite.config.ts` — TypeScript resolves `./project-url.mjs` to
 *  this file under `moduleResolution: "bundler"` (measured, TypeScript 5.7). */
export declare const PROJECT_URL_VAR: "YOKOHAMA_PROJECT_URL";
export declare const PROJECT_URL_MAX: number;
/** `null` for unset or empty; the value itself when it passes; a thrown
 *  `Error` naming `YOKOHAMA_PROJECT_URL` otherwise. */
export declare function checkProjectUrl(raw: string | undefined): string | null;
```

```ts
// The door's project link (M6.5c2, R-6.5c2.6; spec §2.3).
//
// **A build value, and never a request**: the door asks the server nothing
// (R-6.5b2.7), and a run-time value would mean rewriting `index.html` at
// start-up, which the precache's digest check refuses. `vite.config.ts` checks
// `YOKOHAMA_PROJECT_URL` (`web/scripts/project-url.mjs`) and defines it; this
// module is its one reader.

export type ProjectLink = { href: string; text: string };

/** A checked URL as the door draws it: the address, and its text without the
 *  scheme. Pure, so a cell needs no build. */
export function linkFor(url: string | null): ProjectLink | null {
  if (url === null || url === "") return null;
  return { href: url, text: url.replace(/^https?:\/\//i, "") };
}

/** The build's link, or `null`. */
export function projectLink(): ProjectLink | null {
  return linkFor(__YOKOHAMA_PROJECT_URL__);
}
```

```tsx
    expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "New game" })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(fetch).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

  it("opens the local form from New game, which needs no door", async () => {
    render(<FrontDoor multiplayer />);
    await userEvent.setup().click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "New game" }));
    expect(window.location.hash).toBe("#/new/local");

  // when it is stale — so a re-pointed production bot changes this card at the

  it("labels the bot with the version this build ships, from the contract file", () => {

    expect(productionBot.label).not.toBe("");

    render(<FrontDoor multiplayer notice="this game is no longer available" />);
    expect(screen.getByText("this game is no longer available")).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  // **The project link** (R-6.5c2.6, spec §2.3): only where the build names

  it("draws the project link only when the build names one, in a new tab", () => {

    const link = screen.getByRole("link", { name: "github.com/you/yokohama-assistant" });
    expect(link).toHaveAttribute("href", "https://github.com/you/yokohama-assistant");
    expect(link).toHaveAttribute("target", "_blank");
    expect(link).toHaveAttribute("rel", "noopener noreferrer");

  // **"How to play" opens the help in place, WITHOUT its screenshots**: they
  // are photographs of the card art (`ASSETS.md`, the `web/public/help/` row),
  // and no setup screen draws card art.
  it("opens the help in place, with its words and none of its pictures", async () => {
    const { container } = render(<FrontDoor multiplayer />);
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const toggle = screen.getByRole("button", { name: "How to play" });
    expect(toggle).toHaveAttribute("aria-expanded", "false");
    await user.click(toggle);
    expect(toggle).toHaveAttribute("aria-expanded", "true");
    const panel = screen.getByRole("region", { name: "How to play" });
    expect(within(panel).getByRole("heading", { name: "The three parts of the screen" })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(container.querySelectorAll("img, figure.shot")).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(within(panel).getByRole("heading", { name: "How to play" })).toHaveFocus();
    await user.click(within(panel).getByRole("button", { name: "Close" }));
    expect(screen.queryByRole("region", { name: "How to play" })).toBeNull();
  });

  // **The build value, read once and never asked for.** Absent is ON, so a
  // deployment that sets nothing serves both channels; the one string that
  // turns it off is the literal `"false"`.
  it("reads the multiplayer entry off the build and nothing else", () => {
    expect(multiplayerOffered()).toBe(true);
    vi.stubEnv("VITE_MULTIPLAYER", "false");
    expect(multiplayerOffered()).toBe(false);
    vi.stubEnv("VITE_MULTIPLAYER", "true");
    expect(multiplayerOffered()).toBe(true);
    vi.stubEnv("VITE_MULTIPLAYER", "0");
    expect(multiplayerOffered()).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 8: The words.** `web/src/tables.ts` — append:

```ts
/** What a game ON THIS DEVICE is waiting on, in the door's words (M6.5c2,
 *  mocks 01 and 10): the bot it is played against, then its state.
 *
 *  A local game is you and the bot, so its words are a player's rather than a
 *  lobby's: "your move", "you won", "the bot won". The version is the
 *  LISTING's (`TableView.bot`), never a parse of the record; a game dealt
 *  before its table recorded which bot names none (spec §2.4). */
export function deviceWord(t: TableView): string {
  const vs = t.bot ? `vs ${t.bot.label} · ` : "";
  if (t.over) {
    if (t.winner === null) return `${vs}over`;
    return `${vs}${t.my_seats.includes(t.winner) ? "you won" : `${holder(t, t.winner)} won`}`;
  }
  if (t.status === "dealing") {
    return `${vs}${t.my_seats.some((s) => !t.chosen[s]) ? "choose a card" : "dealing"}`;
  }
  if (t.status === "open") return `${vs}${tableWord(t)}`;
  if (t.to_move === null) return `${vs}playing`;
  return `${vs}${t.my_seats.includes(t.to_move) ? "your move" : `waiting on ${holder(t, t.to_move)}`}`;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 11: The door.** `web/src/FrontDoor.tsx`, whole:

```tsx
// The front door at `#/` (R-6.5b2.1, R-6.5c2.6; mocks 01, 06, 11): the product's
// name and its board, and three ways on — and everyone sees it.
//
// **This screen asks the server NOTHING, and that is a ruling rather than a
// tidiness** (R-6.5b2.7): a single-player visitor is meant to cost zero Worker
// invocations. Everything it draws comes from the BUILD or from this browser:
// whether the friends card is drawn (`VITE_MULTIPLAYER`), the project link
// (`YOKOHAMA_PROJECT_URL`, `projectLink.ts`), the bot's version (the committed
// contract file `wire/production_bot.json`, which `wire_fixtures` refuses when
// it is stale), and the games in this browser (the local host's own listing).
// The runtime switch (`YOKOHAMA_WEB_MULTIPLAYER`) is what ENFORCES; this only
// informs the door, and where a deployment builds the client one way and runs
// the server the other, the link lands on `/enter`'s own 404, whose body says
// so.
//
// **"Go to the lobby" is an `<a>` and never a `fetch`.** Access answers a
// navigation with a `302` to another origin, which a `fetch` follows and then
// fails opaquely; a navigation is what the browser already knows how to do,
// and passing `/enter` is what mints the token every later request carries.
//
// **No card art, here or on any setup screen** (`ASSETS.md`): the board is an
// original drawing (`BoardMark`), and "How to play" draws the help panel
// without its screenshots, which are photographs of the art.

import { useEffect, useId, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { BoardMark } from "./BoardMark";
import { VersionTag } from "./Chips";
import { Help } from "./Help";
import { OnThisDevice } from "./OnThisDevice";
import type { ProjectLink } from "./projectLink";
import { Refusal } from "./Refusal";
import { navigate } from "./route";
import type { ReadinessStatus } from "./swRegister";
import productionBot from "./wire/production_bot.json";

/** Whether this BUILD offers the other channel.
 *
 *  Absent is ON, so a deployment that sets nothing serves both — and the one
 *  string that shuts the door is the literal `"false"`, not any falsy value: a
 *  `VITE_MULTIPLAYER=0` is a deployment that has said nothing this client can
 *  act on, and guessing would draw a door for a server that serves one.
 *
 *  A function and not a module constant, so a cell can stub the environment and
 *  read it back; it is called once per render of one screen and costs nothing. */
export function multiplayerOffered(): boolean {
  return import.meta.env.VITE_MULTIPLAYER !== "false";
}

export function FrontDoor({
  multiplayer,
  notice,
  readiness,
  link,
}: {
  /** Whether to draw the friends card. `multiplayerOffered()`'s answer, passed
   *  as a prop so this component is a screen and not a reader of the build —
   *  which is also what lets both arms be rendered in a cell (state E). */
  multiplayer: boolean;
  /** A sentence from OUTSIDE the door, drawn above the cards: a local game that
   *  ends, is abandoned or refuses to open lands here, where its siblings are
   *  listed. The lobby carries the same sentence for a table of the server's. */
  notice?: string | null;
  /** What the release's service worker is doing, from `useReadiness()` —
   *  drawn in the device card's foot. OPTIONAL: "nothing to say" is a real
   *  answer (a development build, a browser with no service workers, a page
   *  the browser walk has flagged). */
  readiness?: ReadinessStatus;
  /** The project link, from the build (`projectLink()`): a prop for
   *  `multiplayer`'s reason. Absent or `null` draws nothing. */
  link?: ProjectLink | null;
}) {
  const [help, setHelp] = useState(false);
  const helpTitle = useRef<HTMLHeadingElement | null>(null);
  const ids = useId();
  // The heading a player lands on when the help opens — focus, and never
  // `scrollIntoView` (ruling R-F11: it scrolls every scrollable ancestor).
  useEffect(() => {
    if (help) helpTitle.current?.focus();
  }, [help]);
  return (
    <div className="front-door">
      {/* **The hero, and not `header.banner`**: that is the GAME's header, and
          the browser walk's "am I in a game" waits are scoped to it
          (`e2e/harness.ts`'s `atTheGame`). */}
      <header className="door-hero">
        <div className="door-hero-in">
          <div className="door-title">
            <h1>Yokohama</h1>
            {link && (
              <a className="project-link" href={link.href} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">
                {link.text}
                <span aria-hidden="true"> &#8599;</span>
              </a>
            )}
          </div>
          <BoardMark width={360} />
        </div>
      </header>
      <main className="door-main">
        {notice && <Refusal sentence={notice} className="error door-notice" />}
        {/* **The three ways on, the channel that needs nothing first** (Task 3
            review, Minor 3): the bot card's New game needs no server, the
            friends card needs a login, and the games already here close the
            row. Under `VITE_MULTIPLAYER=false` the friends card is absent and
            the other two widen (state E). */}
        <div className={multiplayer ? "door-cards" : "door-cards two-up"}>
          <section className="raised-card door-card bot-card" aria-labelledby={`${ids}-bot`}>
            <div className="card-band yen" aria-hidden="true" />
            <div className="card-in">
              <p className="card-cap">2 players</p>
              <h2 id={`${ids}-bot`}>
                You against the bot <VersionTag label={productionBot.label} />
              </h2>
              <p className="lede">Plays entirely on this device. No account needed, and it works offline.</p>
              <button
                type="button"
                className="primary yen"
                onClick={() => navigate({ kind: "new", local: true })}
              >
                New game
              </button>
            </div>
          </section>
          {multiplayer && (
            <section className="raised-card door-card friends-card" aria-labelledby={`${ids}-friends`}>
              <div className="card-band vp" aria-hidden="true" />
              <div className="card-in">
                <p className="card-cap">2 to 4 players</p>
                <h2 id={`${ids}-friends`}>Play with friends</h2>
                <p className="lede">
                  Open a table and send the link, or take a free seat at someone else&rsquo;s. You
                  can spectate games in progress, too.
                </p>
                <a className="primary-link enter" href="/enter">
                  Go to the lobby
                </a>
              </div>
            </section>
          )}
          <OnThisDevice readiness={readiness} />
        </div>
        <div className="door-foot">
          <button
            type="button"
            className="linkish"
            aria-expanded={help}
            aria-controls={`${ids}-help`}
            onClick={() => setHelp((h) => !h)}
          >
            How to play
          </button>
        </div>
        {help && (
          <section id={`${ids}-help`} className="raised-card door-help" aria-labelledby={`${ids}-help-title`}>
            <div className="card-in">
              <div className="help-head">
                <h2 id={`${ids}-help-title`} ref={helpTitle} tabIndex={-1}>
                  How to play
                </h2>
                <button type="button" className="ghost" onClick={() => setHelp(false)}>
                  Close
                </button>
              </div>
              <Help shots={false} />
            </div>
          </section>
        )}
      </main>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// local dispatch's own `GET /api/games?scope=mine` — the module in this tab's
```

```tsx
/** One game on this device: its name — the ONE link — and what it waits on,
 *  with its bot. The link's box covers the row (`styles.css`), so the whole
 *  row opens the game while the link's name stays the game's name, which is
 *  what the cells and the browser walk find it by. */
function DeviceRow({ table }: { table: TableView }): React.ReactNode {
  return (
    <li className="device-row">
      <a className="device-name" href={hashOf({ kind: "table", id: table.id })}>
        {table.name ?? table.id}
      </a>
      <span className="device-state">
        {deviceWord(table)}
        <span aria-hidden="true"> &rsaquo;</span>
      </span>
    </li>
  );
}
```

```css
/* ---- M6.5c2: the front door (R-6.5c2.6; spec §2.2; mocks 01, 06, 11) ------- */
/* The hero: the name and the board on the navy glow, full bleed, its content
```

Create `web/e2e/setup_screens.spec.ts`:

```ts
// The setup screens in a real browser (M6.5c2, spec §2.2 and §3).
//
// What only a browser can say about the rebuilt screens, which jsdom — no
// stylesheet, no layout — structurally cannot: each is laid out at desktop
// width and at 390px, nothing on it scrolls sideways, its primary controls are
// thumb-sized on a phone, and no picture on it is an `<img>` (card art is never
// anything else in this client, so zero is the claim `ASSETS.md` asks of a
// setup screen). Every cell leaves its screenshots under the gitignored
// `test-results/` for the headed look spec §3 requires; the task's report names
// them beside the approved mocks.
//
// One spec for every screen this cycle rebuilds, so the width rule is written
// once: the door (Task 10), the name step (Task 11), the lobby (Task 12).

import type { Page } from "@playwright/test";
// **`test` comes from `./sw`, not from `@playwright/test`** (M6.5b2, spec §2.3):
// the fixture flags every page in the context so the release's service worker is
// NOT registered during the walk. `every_spec_declares_its_worker.spec.ts` is what
// keeps that from being a convention anybody has to remember.
import { expect, test } from "./sw";
import { BASE_URL, haveBrowser } from "../playwright.config";
import { blame, readOverflow, watchForBreakage } from "./harness";

// No browser, and `YOKOHAMA_WEB_E2E_OPTIONAL=1`: SKIP, visibly.
test.skip(!haveBrowser, "no Chromium — YOKOHAMA_WEB_E2E_OPTIONAL=1; this run tested NOTHING");

const DESKTOP = { width: 1440, height: 900 };
const PHONE = { width: 390, height: 844 };

/** Nothing on the page is wider than its window — read once the layout is DONE
 *  (the width gate's own note, `harness.ts`). */
async function noSidewaysScroll(page: Page, what: string): Promise<void> {
  await page.evaluate(() => new Promise((r) => requestAnimationFrame(() => r(null))));
  const read = await readOverflow(page);
  expect(
    read.docScrollWidth - read.docClientWidth,
    `${what} scrolls sideways: ${blame(read)}`,
  ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0);
}

/** A picture for the headed look, under this run's own output directory. */
async function look(page: Page, name: string): Promise<void> {
  await page.screenshot({ path: test.info().outputPath(`${name}.png`), fullPage: true });
}

/** How many `<img>` the page draws. */
const images = (page: Page): Promise<number> => page.evaluate(() => document.images.length);

/** A control's rendered height — "thumb-sized" is 44px, the platforms' own floor. */
async function height(page: Page, role: "button" | "link", name: string): Promise<number> {
  return (await page.getByRole(role, { name, exact: true }).boundingBox())!.height;
}

test("the door: three cards side by side at 1440 and one column at 390, no card art, nothing asked of the API", async ({
  page,
}) => {
  const watch = watchForBreakage(page);
  const asked: string[] = [];
  page.on("request", (r) => {
    const url = new URL(r.url());
    if (url.origin === new URL(BASE_URL).origin) asked.push(url.pathname);
  });

  for (const size of [DESKTOP, PHONE]) {
    await page.setViewportSize(size);
    await page.goto("/");
    const title = page.locator(".door-hero").getByRole("heading", { level: 1, name: "Yokohama" });
    await expect(title).toBeVisible();
    const cards = page.locator(".door-cards > .door-card");
    await expect(cards).toHaveCount(3);
    await expect(page.getByRole("link", { name: "Go to the lobby" })).toHaveAttribute("href", "/enter");
    await noSidewaysScroll(page, `the door at ${size.width}px`);
    expect(await images(page), `the door draws no <img> at ${size.width}px`).toBe(0);

    const boxes = await cards.evaluateAll((els) =>
      els.map((e) => {
        const r = e.getBoundingClientRect();
        return { left: Math.round(r.left), top: Math.round(r.top) };
      }),
    );
    const board = (await page.locator(".door-hero .board-mark").boundingBox())!;
    const heading = (await title.boundingBox())!;
    if (size === DESKTOP) {
      expect(new Set(boxes.map((b) => b.top)).size, `one row of cards: ${JSON.stringify(boxes)}`).toBe(1);
      expect(boxes.map((b) => b.left)).toEqual([...boxes.map((b) => b.left)].sort((a, b) => a - b));
      expect(board.x, "the board sits right of the title").toBeGreaterThan(heading.x + heading.width);
    } else {
      expect(new Set(boxes.map((b) => b.left)).size, `one column of cards: ${JSON.stringify(boxes)}`).toBe(1);
      expect(boxes.map((b) => b.top)).toEqual([...boxes.map((b) => b.top)].sort((a, b) => a - b));
      expect(board.y + board.height, "the board sits above the title").toBeLessThanOrEqual(heading.y + 1);
      expect(await height(page, "button", "New game"), "New game, thumb-sized").toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(44);
      expect(await height(page, "link", "Go to the lobby"), "Go to the lobby, thumb-sized").toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(44);
    }
    await look(page, `door-${size.width}`);
  }

  // The help opens in place, and brings none of its screenshots.
  await page.setViewportSize(DESKTOP);
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "How to play" }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "The three parts of the screen" })).toBeVisible();
  expect(await images(page), "the help on the door draws none of its screenshots").toBe(0);
  await look(page, "door-help-1440");

  // **R-6.5b2.7 in a real browser, for the rebuilt door**: the art manifest is
  // a static file and the words are the local host's; nothing is `/api/`.
  expect(asked.filter((p) => p.startsWith("/api/")), "the door asks the API for nothing").toEqual([]);
  expect(watch.failures).toEqual([]);
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: The rule.** `web/src/nameRule.ts`:

```ts
// The key grammar, as the server applies it (M6.5c2, R-6.5c2.3; spec §2.1).
//
// **A restatement, pinned.** `User::parse` (`crates/yokohama-web/src/identity.rs`)
// is the authority — it keys every seat, every watcher and every archive
// directory — and the name step normalizes exactly as it does, so the header
// this browser sends IS the key the server writes seats under.
// `nameRule.test.ts` holds this file to the layer's own verdicts over
// `web/src/wire/identity_cases.json`, which `wire_fixtures` emits and refuses
// when it is stale — so the two rules cannot drift apart in silence.
//
// **Rust's rules, character for character, and not JavaScript's** (measured
// against rustc when this plan was drafted):
// - `str::trim` strips the Unicode White_Space property, which is NOT what
//   `String.prototype.trim` strips: Rust trims U+0085 and keeps U+FEFF,
//   JavaScript the reverse;
// - `to_ascii_lowercase` folds A–Z only, where `toLowerCase` folds the Kelvin
//   sign U+212A into a `k` and would admit a name the server refuses;
// - `char::is_control` is the Cc category, U+0000–U+001F and U+007F–U+009F.
// A client built on the JavaScript built-ins would accept names the server
// refuses and send keys the server never writes.
//
// **The name as TYPED is kept too**, as the display name: "  Ben   Castle " is
// the key `ben castle`, shown `Ben Castle` (Review Focus 4).

/** `char::is_whitespace` — the Unicode White_Space property — as a class body. */
const WHITE = "\t\n\u000b\f\r \u0085\u00a0\u1680\u2000-\u200a\u2028\u2029\u202f\u205f\u3000";
const IS_WHITE = new RegExp(`[${WHITE}]`);
const EDGES = new RegExp(`^[${WHITE}]+|[${WHITE}]+$`, "g");
/** `char::is_control`: the Unicode Cc category. */
const IS_CONTROL = /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f-\u009f]/;

/** The longest plain name, in characters — all ASCII, so also in bytes. */
export const NAME_MAX = 32;
/** The longest address, in UTF-8 bytes (`User::parse`'s `s.len()`). */
const ADDRESS_MAX_BYTES = 254;

export type NameVerdict = { ok: true; key: string; display: string } | { ok: false; reason: string };

const asciiLower = (s: string): string => s.replace(/[A-Z]/g, (c) => c.toLowerCase());

/** The key a raw input is, and how it is shown — or why the server would
 *  refuse it. An `@` decides which half of the grammar applies: a plain name
 *  can never hold one, and an address always does. */
export function normalizeName(raw: string): NameVerdict {
  const typed = raw.replace(EDGES, "");
  if (typed === "") return { ok: false, reason: "Type a name to play under." };
  return typed.includes("@") ? address(typed) : plainName(typed);
}

/** The email shape `User::parse` has always taken: exactly one `@` with
 *  something on both sides, no whitespace or control character, at most 254
 *  bytes. */
function address(typed: string): NameVerdict {
  const key = asciiLower(typed);
  if (new TextEncoder().encode(key).length > ADDRESS_MAX_BYTES) {
    return { ok: false, reason: "An address is at most 254 bytes." };
  }
  if (IS_WHITE.test(key) || IS_CONTROL.test(key)) {
    return { ok: false, reason: "An address has no spaces or control characters in it." };
  }
  const parts = key.split("@");
  if (parts.length !== 2 || parts[0] === "" || parts[1] === "") {
    return { ok: false, reason: "An address has exactly one @, with something on both sides of it." };
  }
  return { ok: true, key, display: typed };
}

/** A plain name: 1–32 of ASCII letters, digits, space, `.`, `-` and `_`,
 *  beginning with a letter or a digit, internal runs of spaces collapsed to
 *  one, and never `anonymous`. The leading letter or digit is what keeps a
 *  name's archive directory from ever being `.` or `..` (spec §2.1, review H1). */
function plainName(typed: string): NameVerdict {
  const display = typed.replace(/ {2,}/g, " ");
  const key = asciiLower(display);
  if (!/^[a-z0-9 ._-]*$/.test(key)) {
    return { ok: false, reason: "A name uses letters, numbers, spaces, dots, dashes and underscores — nothing else." };
  }
  if (!/^[a-z0-9]/.test(key)) return { ok: false, reason: "A name begins with a letter or a digit." };
  if (key.length > NAME_MAX) return { ok: false, reason: `A name is at most ${NAME_MAX} characters.` };
  if (key === "anonymous") {
    return { ok: false, reason: "“anonymous” means nobody on this server — choose another name." };
  }
  return { ok: true, key, display };
}
```

```ts
/** How the door's own read failed (M6.5c2, spec §2.1's discriminators):
 *  `challenge` — the EDGE refused with Access's challenge (state A);
 *  `network` — nothing answered at all, a network error or offline (state C);
 *  `refused` — the server answered with a refusal of its own. */
export type DoorFailure = "challenge" | "network" | "refused";

/** What a failed `/api/me` was. An `ApiError` is an answer — the server's or
 *  the edge's — and anything else is `fetch` failing with none: `api.ts`'s
 *  `call` turns every HTTP status into an `ApiError`. */
export function failureOf(e: unknown): DoorFailure {
  if (!(e instanceof ApiError)) return "network";
  return isSessionExpired(e) ? "challenge" : "refused";
}
```

```ts
/** What the OPERATOR reads when the server names nobody under a door set in
 *  front of it (state B, spec §2.1): which header was expected, and how a
 *  player was meant to arrive. It sits in the card's "For the operator" fold,
 *  so a player reads the sentence meant for them first. The open door never
 *  reaches here: it has the name step. */
export function doorSentence(mode: Exclude<Me["mode"], "open">): string {
  return mode === "cf-access"
    ? "This server expects Cloudflare Access to name each player (Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email), and nothing arrived. Open it through its public hostname, or see the self-host guide on identity."
    : "This server expects the edge Worker to name each player (X-Yokohama-User), and nothing arrived. Open it through its public hostname.";
}
```

```tsx
// The door's states (M6.5c2, R-6.5c2.4; spec §2.1; mocks 03 and 05): A–D, the
// name step and the server's own refusal, each drawn from what `useMe` and the
// health read say — the discriminators spec §2.1 names.
//
// `me` is a payload, so it comes from the corpus (`wire.me`, `wire.meSignedOut`,
// and the Access door as the one field moved — `App.test.tsx`'s precedent). The
// `Door` object around it is the CLIENT's own hook state, not a payload.

import { render, screen, within } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { ACCESS_CHALLENGE } from "./api";
import { Door } from "./Door";
import type { Door as DoorState } from "./whoami";
import { wire } from "./wire/contract";

const state = (over: Partial<DoorState> = {}): DoorState => ({
  me: null,
  error: null,
  failure: null,
  notice: null,
  refresh: vi.fn(),
  signOut: vi.fn(),
  signedOut: vi.fn(),
  ...over,
});

const draw = (door: DoorState, serverUp: boolean | null = true, onRetry = vi.fn()) =>
  render(<Door door={door} serverUp={serverUp} onSignedIn={vi.fn()} onRetry={onRetry} />);

describe("the door's states", () => {
  // **A, and before C**: the Access application fronts `/api/health` too, so an
  // expired session fails BOTH reads — and "can't reach the server" would send
  // a player looking at their network when one click through the turnstile
  // fixes it.
  it("A: an expired Access session is one card, with the turnstile its one way through", () => {
    draw(state({ failure: "challenge", error: ACCESS_CHALLENGE }), false);
    expect(screen.getByRole("heading", { name: "Your sign-in has run out" })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: "Sign in again" })).toHaveAttribute("href", "/enter");
    expect(screen.queryByRole("heading", { name: "Can't reach the server" })).toBeNull();
  });

  it("C: no answer at all — from the door's own read, or from health with the door unanswered", async () => {
    const retry = vi.fn();
    const { unmount } = draw(state({ failure: "network", error: "TypeError: Failed to fetch" }), null, retry);
    expect(screen.getByRole("heading", { name: "Can't reach the server" })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: "Games on this device" })).toHaveAttribute("href", "#/");
    await userEvent.setup().click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Try again" }));
    expect(retry).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    // The platform's words are not the player's.
    expect(screen.queryByText(/TypeError/)).toBeNull();
    unmount();
    draw(state(), false);
    expect(screen.getByRole("heading", { name: "Can't reach the server" })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  // "Any other refusal of `/api/me` keeps today's `Refusal` rendering inside the
  // new card" (spec §2.1): the server's own words, and no turnstile.
  it("keeps the server's own refusal, in its own words, inside a card", () => {
    draw(state({ failure: "refused", error: wire.error.error }));
    expect(screen.getByRole("heading", { name: "The server refused" })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText(wire.error.error)).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByRole("link", { name: "Sign in again" })).toBeNull();
  });

  it("D: nothing answered yet reads as connecting, over skeleton rows", () => {
    const { container } = draw(state(), null);
    expect(screen.getByRole("status")).toHaveTextContent("Connecting to the server…");
    expect(container.querySelectorAll(".skeleton-rows > div")).toHaveLength(3);
  });

  it("the open door with no name is the name step", () => {
    expect(wire.meSignedOut.mode).toBe("open");
    draw(state({ me: wire.meSignedOut }));
    expect(screen.getByRole("heading", { name: "Choose a name" })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  // **B: the server answered and nobody reached it** — a player's sentence on
  // the card, and the header the edge was meant to set in a fold for whoever
  // runs the server.
  it("B: a door in front of the server that named nobody — a card for the player, a fold for the operator", () => {
    draw(state({ me: { ...wire.meSignedOut, mode: "cf-access" } }));
    expect(screen.getByRole("heading", { name: "This server couldn't tell who you are" })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: "Sign in again" })).toHaveAttribute("href", "/enter");
    const fold = screen.getByText("For the operator").closest("details")!;
    expect(fold).not.toHaveAttribute("open");
    expect(within(fold).getByText(/Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email/)).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByLabelText("Name")).toBeNull();
  });

  it("draws nothing once the server names the caller", () => {
    const { container } = draw(state({ me: wire.me }));
    expect(container).toBeEmptyDOMElement();
  });
});
```

```tsx
// The name step: the open door's one question (M6.5c2, spec §2.1; mock 03).
//
// The KEY is the contract, not the component. `api.ts` reads
// `CLAIMED_USER_KEY` on every call and sends it as the header, so the screen
// must store what the SERVER will key — `nameRule.ts`'s key, pinned to
// `User::parse` — and keep what was typed for display on its own key. The
// cells import both keys from `api.ts` rather than restating them.

import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { CLAIMED_USER_KEY, DISPLAY_NAME_KEY } from "./api";
import { SignIn } from "./SignIn";

describe("the name step", () => {
  // **Review Focus 4, on the screen**: one key, shown as typed.
  it("stores the key the server will use, keeps the name as typed, and hands the key up (Review Focus 4)", async () => {
    const onSignedIn = vi.fn();
    render(<SignIn onSignedIn={onSignedIn} />);
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText("Name"), "  Ben   Castle ");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Continue" }));
    expect(localStorage.getItem(CLAIMED_USER_KEY)).toBe("ben castle");
    expect(localStorage.getItem(DISPLAY_NAME_KEY)).toBe("Ben Castle");
    expect(onSignedIn).toHaveBeenCalledWith("ben castle");
  });

  it("takes an address too, keyed exactly as the server keys it", async () => {
    const onSignedIn = vi.fn();
    render(<SignIn onSignedIn={onSignedIn} />);
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText("Name"), " Red@Wire.TEST ");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Continue" }));
    expect(localStorage.getItem(CLAIMED_USER_KEY)).toBe("red@wire.test");
    expect(onSignedIn).toHaveBeenCalledWith("red@wire.test");
  });

  // Refused BEFORE a request: a name the server would refuse is never stored and
  // never handed up — every request would then be a 401.
  it("refuses what the server refuses, says why, and stores nothing", async () => {
    const onSignedIn = vi.fn();
    render(<SignIn onSignedIn={onSignedIn} />);
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText("Name"), "..");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Continue" }));
    expect(screen.getByText("A name begins with a letter or a digit.")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(localStorage.getItem(CLAIMED_USER_KEY)).toBeNull();
    expect(localStorage.getItem(DISPLAY_NAME_KEY)).toBeNull();
    expect(onSignedIn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("asks for something rather than refusing an empty field", async () => {
    render(<SignIn onSignedIn={vi.fn()} />);
    await userEvent.setup().click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Continue" }));
    expect(screen.getByText("Type a name to play under.")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(localStorage.getItem(CLAIMED_USER_KEY)).toBeNull();
  });

  // §7.1's last bullet: the player is returned here WITH the sentence. Without
  // it a game vanishes and a bare form appears, and nothing connects the two.
  it("shows the sentence that sent the player back, above the form", () => {
    render(<SignIn onSignedIn={vi.fn()} notice="no signed-in user: send X-Yokohama-Claimed-User" />);
    const said = screen.getByRole("status");
    expect(said).toHaveTextContent("no signed-in user: send X-Yokohama-Claimed-User");
    expect(said.compareDocumentPosition(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Continue" }))).toBe(
      Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_FOLLOWING,
    );
```

```tsx
// The name step: the open door's one question (M6.5c2, R-6.5c2.3; spec §2.1;
// mock 03).
//
// **It exists under ONE door.** `open` is the mode where the server believes
// the `X-Yokohama-Claimed-User` header — a self-host with no identity provider,
// and this project's own browser walk — and behind Cloudflare Access or the
// edge Worker the identity arrives from in front of the server and this screen
// is never drawn (`Door.tsx`).
//
// **The rule is the server's, and so is the key.** `normalizeName` is pinned
// to `User::parse` over one committed table (`nameRule.ts`), so the header this
// browser sends is exactly the key the server writes seats under. The name as
// TYPED is stored too, as the display name the lobby corner and every seat show.

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { setClaimedUser, setDisplayName } from "./api";
import { normalizeName } from "./nameRule";
import { Refusal } from "./Refusal";

export function SignIn({
  onSignedIn,
  notice,
}: {
  onSignedIn: (key: string) => void;
  /** Why the player is here, in the server's own words, when they did not
   *  choose to be (spec §7.1). A 401 unmounts the screen that caught it, so the
   *  sentence has to arrive with them or it is lost. */
  notice?: string;
}) {
  const field = useId();
  const rule = useId();
  const [value, setValue] = useState("");
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const submit = () => {
    const name = normalizeName(value);
    if (!name.ok) {
      setError(name.reason);
      return;
    }
    // **Stored BEFORE the callback, because the callback is what re-reads
    // `/api/me`.** `api.ts` attaches the header from storage on every call, so a
    // refresh that ran first would ask the server who we are while the browser
    // was still holding nobody, and the answer would send us straight back here.
    setClaimedUser(name.key);
    setDisplayName(name.display);
    setError(null);
    onSignedIn(name.key);
  };
  return (
    <section className="raised-card state-card name-step">
      <div className="card-band vp" aria-hidden="true" />
      <div className="card-in">
        <h2>Choose a name</h2>
        {/* Above the form: the reason you are here is read before the thing it
            asks you to do. `role="status"` because it appears without the player
            having done anything on this screen. */}
        {notice && (
          <p className="error door-notice" role="status">
            {notice}
          </p>
        )}
        <p className="lede">Other players see it at your tables and in chat.</p>
        {/* A real form, so Enter in the field continues. The default is
            prevented because there is nothing to submit TO — the name goes to
            storage and the next request carries it as a header. */}
        <form
          onSubmit={(e) => {
            e.preventDefault();
            submit();
          }}
        >
          <label className="sr-only" htmlFor={field}>
            Name
          </label>
          <input
            id={field}
            type="text"
            autoComplete="nickname"
            aria-describedby={rule}
            value={value}
            onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)}
          />
          <p className="hint" id={rule}>
            Letters, numbers, spaces, dots, dashes and underscores. Up to 32 characters.
          </p>
          <button type="submit" className="primary">
            Continue
          </button>
        </form>
        {error && <Refusal sentence={error} />}
        <p className="fine">
          This server doesn&rsquo;t check who anyone is, so anyone who can reach it can use any name.
          Play here with people you know. Your tables stay with the name you sat down as, so
          switching names later leaves them behind.
        </p>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 8: The door's states.** `web/src/Door.tsx`, whole:

```tsx
// What the server says about WHO IS ASKING, drawn as the lobby's content (M6.5b,
// spec §2.5; M6.5c2, R-6.5c2.4, spec §2.1; mocks 03 and 05).
//
// **The door's answers are STATES, each a card with one thing to do** — they
// were sentences until M6.5c2 (R-6.5c2.4). What decides each, in the order it
// is tested, and the order is the rule:
//
//   A. `/api/me` met the EDGE's challenge: Cloudflare Access saying the session
//      in front of the server has expired (`WWW-Authenticate:
//      Cloudflare-Access`, `ACCESS_CHALLENGE`). FIRST, because the Access
//      application covers the whole hostname, `/api/health` included — an
//      expired session fails both reads, and the test below would otherwise
//      call a door the player can walk through "can't reach".
//   C. Nothing answered: `/api/me` failed with no HTTP answer at all, or the
//      health read failed while `/api/me` has not answered (the `unreachable`
//      rule `App.tsx` held until M6.5c2, moved here whole).
//   —  The server REFUSED `/api/me` in words of its own: those words, through
//      `Refusal`, inside a card.
//   D. Nothing has answered yet: "Connecting to the server…" over skeleton rows.
//   —  The OPEN door, and no name yet: the name step (`SignIn`).
//   B. The server answered, and no identity reached it, under a door set in
//      front of it (`cf-access`, `worker`) — a non-email header included, which
//      the mode rule reads as absent (spec §2.1).
//
// State E — multiplayer off — is the front door's (`FrontDoor.tsx`).

import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { Refusal } from "./Refusal";
import { SignIn } from "./SignIn";
import { doorSentence, type Door as DoorState } from "./whoami";

/** A state's card: its coloured band, its title, and what to do. */
function StateCard({ band, title, children }: { band: "vp" | "warn" | "plain"; title: string; children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <section className="raised-card state-card">
      <div className={band === "plain" ? "card-band" : `card-band ${band}`} aria-hidden="true" />
      <div className="card-in">
        <h2>{title}</h2>
        {children}
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}

/** State C: nothing answered. Exported because the SIGNED-IN lobby draws it
 *  too, when its own health read fails (`Lobby.tsx`). */
export function Unreachable({ onRetry }: { onRetry: () => void }) {
  return (
    <StateCard band="plain" title="Can't reach the server">
      <p className="lede">
        The lobby needs a connection. Your games on this device still work, including new games against
        the bot.
      </p>
      <div className="state-actions">
        <button type="button" className="ghost" onClick={onRetry}>
          Try again
        </button>
        <a href="#/">Games on this device</a>
      </div>
    </StateCard>
  );
}

/** State D: nothing has answered yet — the one true sentence, over skeleton
 *  rows where the lists will be. */
function Connecting() {
  return (
    <div className="connecting-state">
      <p className="connecting-line" role="status">
        <span className="connecting-dots" aria-hidden="true">
          <i />
          <i />
          <i />
        </span>
        Connecting to the server&hellip;
      </p>
      <div className="skeleton-rows" aria-hidden="true">
        <div />
        <div />
        <div />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

export function Door({
  door,
  serverUp,
  onSignedIn,
  onRetry,
}: {
  door: DoorState;
  /** Whether `GET /api/health` landed — `null` until it answers (App's own). */
  serverUp: boolean | null;
  /** The name was typed and stored: ask `/api/me` again rather than deciding
   *  here that this browser is now that person. */
  onSignedIn: () => void;
  /** "Try again": both reads, again (App's `retry`). */
  onRetry: () => void;
}) {
  if (door.failure === "challenge") {
    return (
      <StateCard band="vp" title="Your sign-in has run out">
        <p className="lede">Sign in again to get back to your tables. Games on this device are unaffected.</p>
        {/* A LINK and never a fetch (`Refusal.tsx`'s reason): passing `/enter`
            is what mints the cookie every later request carries. */}
        <a className="primary-link" href="/enter">
          Sign in again
        </a>
      </StateCard>
    );
  }
  if (door.failure === "network" || (serverUp === false && door.me === null)) {
    return <Unreachable onRetry={onRetry} />;
  }
  if (door.failure === "refused" && door.error !== null) {
    return (
      <StateCard band="warn" title="The server refused">
        <Refusal sentence={door.error} className="error door-error" />
      </StateCard>
    );
  }
  if (door.me === null) return <Connecting />;
  if (door.me.user !== null) return null;
  if (door.me.mode === "open") {
    return <SignIn onSignedIn={onSignedIn} notice={door.notice ?? undefined} />;
  }
  return (
    <StateCard band="warn" title="This server couldn't tell who you are">
      <p className="lede">Try signing in again. If this keeps happening, tell whoever runs the server.</p>
      <a className="primary-link" href="/enter">
        Sign in again
      </a>
      <details className="operator-note">
        <summary>For the operator</summary>
        <p>{doorSentence(door.me.mode)}</p>
      </details>
    </StateCard>
  );
}
```

```tsx
  // **Review Focus 3.** A browser that typed an address under the OPEN door
  // still holds it when it visits a door set in front of the server — the NAS
  // after its redeploy onto `cf-access`. The stale header rides every request,
  // the server ignores it, and the corner says who ACCESS says this is. Nothing
  // asks the player to "switch player": the name is not theirs to switch there.
  it("names the Access identity, never a stale stored name, and offers no switch player (Review Focus 3)", async () => {
    localStorage.setItem(CLAIMED_USER_KEY, "stale@old.test");
    const stub = stubApi((call) => {
      // The corpus's user behind Access: one field moved off a real payload,
      // the precedent of the non-claimed cell above.
      if (call.path.endsWith("/api/me")) return { ...wire.me, mode: "cf-access" };
      if (call.path.endsWith("/api/health")) return { ...wire.health, identity: "cf-access" };
      if (call.path.endsWith("/api/labels")) return wire.labels;
      if (call.path.endsWith("/art/manifest.json")) return wire.artManifest;
      if (call.path.endsWith("/stream")) return openStream();
      if (call.method === "GET" && call.path.startsWith("/api/chat"))
        return { ...wire.houseChat, messages: [], last: 0 };
      if (isGamesList(call)) return gamesNamed();
      throw new Error(`unexpected ${call.method} ${call.path}`);
    });
    window.location.hash = "#/lobby";
    render(<App />);
    await waitFor(() => expect(document.querySelector(".identity-corner")).not.toBeNull());
    const corner = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".identity-corner")!;
    expect(within(corner).getByTitle(wire.me.user!)).toHaveTextContent(wire.me.user!);
    expect(within(corner).getByRole("button", { name: "change name" })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(within(corner).queryByRole("button", { name: "switch player" })).toBeNull();
    expect(document.body.textContent).not.toContain("stale@old.test");
    // The premise, read off the wire: the stale header WAS sent, and ignored.
    expect(stub.matching("GET", "/api/me")[0]!.headers["x-yokohama-claimed-user"]).toBe("stale@old.test");
  });

  // **switch player, under the open door** (spec §2.1): the stored name goes —

  it("drops the stored name on switch player, and lands on the name step", async () => {
    localStorage.setItem(CLAIMED_USER_KEY, wire.me.user!);
    localStorage.setItem(DISPLAY_NAME_KEY, "Red");
    stubApi((call) => {
      if (call.path.endsWith("/api/me"))
        return localStorage.getItem(CLAIMED_USER_KEY) ? wire.me : wire.meSignedOut;
      if (call.path.endsWith("/api/health")) return wire.health;
      if (call.path.endsWith("/api/labels")) return wire.labels;
      if (call.path.endsWith("/art/manifest.json")) return wire.artManifest;
      if (call.path.endsWith("/stream")) return openStream();
      if (call.method === "GET" && call.path.startsWith("/api/chat"))
        return { ...wire.houseChat, messages: [], last: 0 };
      if (isGamesList(call)) return gamesNamed();
      throw new Error(`unexpected ${call.method} ${call.path}`);
    });
    window.location.hash = "#/lobby";
    render(<App />);
    await waitFor(() => expect(document.querySelector(".identity-corner")).not.toBeNull());
    const corner = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".identity-corner")!;
    expect(within(corner).getByTitle(wire.me.user!)).toHaveTextContent("Red");
    await userEvent.setup().click(within(corner).getByRole("button", { name: "switch player" }));
```

```tsx
  /** Bumped by "Try again" (state C), which re-runs the health read below —
   *  its latch is already released by the failure that drew the card. */
  const [healthTick, setHealthTick] = useState(0);
  /** "Try again" on a server that could not be reached (M6.5c2, state C): both
   *  reads again — the door's and the health — and the screen back to
   *  "connecting" until one answers. A health read that LANDED keeps its answer:
   *  only a failed one is forgotten. */
  const retry = useCallback(() => {
    setServerUp((up) => (up === false ? null : up));
    setHealthTick((n) => n + 1);
    refresh();
  }, [refresh]);
```

```ts
export async function signIn(page: Page, email: string = WALKER, url = "/#/lobby"): Promise<void> {
  await page.goto(url);
  const step = page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Choose a name" });
  // Signed in reads two ways: the lobby's corner, whose title is the identity
  // (M6.5c2), and the "You are …" strip every other screen still draws.
  const escaped = email.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
  const signedIn = page
    .locator(".identity-corner")
    .getByTitle(email, { exact: true })
    .or(page.getByText(new RegExp(`^You are ${escaped}$`)));
  await expect(step.or(signedIn).first()).toBeVisible();
  if (await step.count()) {
    await page.getByLabel("Name", { exact: true }).fill(email);
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Continue" }).click();
  }
  await expect(signedIn.first()).toBeVisible();
}
```

```ts
  // **The corner is a pill on a phone, and nothing on the lobby scrolls
  // sideways** (M6.5c2, spec §2.2). It replaces M6.4's who-strip measure, whose
  // "Your name" field the corner's own control replaced. At desktop width the
  // corner reads "Playing as …" beside its one action; at 390px the same corner
  // is a pill and the action is one tap away. Live the door is the Worker's, so
  // the action is "change name"; locally it is the open door's "switch player".
  {
    const desktop = a.viewportSize()!;
    const corner = a.locator(".identity-corner");
    const action = corner.getByRole("button", { name: LIVE ? "change name" : "switch player" });
    const pill = corner.locator(".identity-pill");
    await expect(corner.getByText("Playing as")).toBeVisible();
    await expect(action).toBeVisible();
    await expect(pill).toBeHidden();

    await a.setViewportSize({ width: 390, height: 844 });
    await a.evaluate(() => new Promise((r) => requestAnimationFrame(() => r(null))));
    await expect(pill).toBeVisible();
    await expect(action, "the action waits behind the pill").toBeHidden();
    const read = await readOverflow(a);
    expect(
      read.docScrollWidth - read.docClientWidth,
      `the lobby scrolls sideways at 390px: ${blame(read)}`,
    ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0);
    await pill.click();
    await expect(action, "one tap opens the corner").toBeVisible();
    const opened = await readOverflow(a);
    expect(
      opened.docScrollWidth - opened.docClientWidth,
      `the open corner pushes the lobby sideways at 390px: ${blame(opened)}`,
    ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0);
    await pill.click();

    await a.setViewportSize(desktop);
    await a.evaluate(() => new Promise((r) => requestAnimationFrame(() => r(null))));
  }
```

and whose bot this build does not run (`bot.runs_here === false`) offers no action and says "can't continue here" —
every game route refuses it (spec §2.4) — and its creator keeps Abandon. A table you sit at is listed under Your
tables only (`my_seats` non-empty). The creator's rows keep `Abandon` beside the action (R-13; the draft's "spec
gaps").
