```ts
// The lobby row's words (M6.5c2, R-6.5c2.7; mock 02): how long ago a table was
// opened, the line under its name, a chip per seat, and its one action.
describe("the lobby row", () => {
  /** Two days after the corpus's own tables were opened. */
  const NOW = (wire.table.created_at + 2 * 86_400) * 1000;

  it("says how long ago a table was opened", () => {
    const at = wire.table.created_at;
    expect(ago(at, (at + 30) * 1000)).toBe("just now");
    expect(ago(at, (at + 20 * 60) * 1000)).toBe("20 min ago");
    expect(ago(at, (at + 3600) * 1000)).toBe("an hour ago");
    expect(ago(at, (at + 5 * 3600) * 1000)).toBe("5 hours ago");
    expect(ago(at, (at + 86_400) * 1000)).toBe("a day ago");
    expect(ago(at, NOW)).toBe("2 days ago");
    // A device clock behind the table's reads "just now", never a negative age;
    // a stored time that is not a number still reads (`Chat.tsx`'s `when` rule).
    expect(ago(at, (at - 600) * 1000)).toBe("just now");
    expect(ago(Number.NaN, NOW)).toBe("a while ago");
  });

  it("says the table's size, then what matters from where it is read", () => {
    expect(rowMeta(wire.table, "mine", NOW)).toBe("2 players · opened 2 days ago");
    expect(rowMeta(wire.table, "playing", NOW)).toBe("2 players");
    expect(rowMeta(wire.tableDealing, "mine", NOW)).toBe("2 players · dealing");
    expect(rowMeta(wire.tableOpen, "mine", NOW)).toBe("2 players · waiting for 1 more");
    expect(rowMeta(wire.tableOpen, "open", NOW)).toBe("2 players · opened 2 days ago");
    expect(rowMeta({ ...wire.table, over: true, winner: 1 }, "mine", NOW)).toBe("2 players · over · Blue won");
  });

  // A chip per seat, in SEAT ORDER. The bot's seat is derived for `seatNames`'
  // reason (the corpus game is bot-free by construction), with the label the
  // build ships.
  it("draws a chip per seat: you, the bot with its version, an open seat, and the turn in gold", () => {
    const seats = [...wire.table.seats];
    seats[0] = { kind: "bot" };
    const vsBot: TableView = { ...wire.table, seats, bot: { label: productionBot.label, runs_here: true } };
    expect(seatChips(vsBot)).toEqual([
      { color: "Red", label: `the bot · ${productionBot.label} · to move`, open: false, toMove: true },
      { color: "Blue", label: "you", open: false, toMove: false },
    ]);
    // Dealt before its table recorded which bot: no version to show (spec §2.4).
    expect(seatChips({ ...vsBot, bot: null })[0]!.label).toBe("the bot · to move");
    expect(seatChips(wire.tableOpen)[1]).toEqual({ color: "Blue", label: "open seat", open: true, toMove: false });
    // A dealing table has no turn to mark, and a finished one none either.
    expect(seatChips(wire.tableDealing).some((c) => c.toMove)).toBe(false);
    expect(seatChips({ ...wire.table, over: true }).some((c) => c.toMove)).toBe(false);
  });

  it("offers one action per row, and nothing to open where this server cannot continue the game", () => {
    expect(rowAction(wire.tableOpen, "mine")).toEqual({ kind: "copy" });
    expect(rowAction({ ...wire.table, my_seats: [0] }, "mine")).toEqual({
      kind: "go",
      label: "Play",
      primary: true,
      padlock: false,
    });
    expect(rowAction(wire.table, "mine")).toEqual({ kind: "go", label: "Play", primary: false, padlock: false });
    expect(rowAction({ ...wire.table, over: true }, "mine")).toMatchObject({ kind: "go", label: "View" });
    expect(rowAction(wire.tableOpen, "open")).toEqual({ kind: "go", label: "Take a seat", primary: false, padlock: true });
    expect(rowAction(wire.tableWatchable, "playing")).toEqual({
      kind: "go",
      label: "Spectate",
      primary: false,
      padlock: true,
    });
    expect(rowAction({ ...wire.tableWatchable, can_watch: true }, "playing")).toMatchObject({ padlock: false });
    // A bot this build does not run: nothing to open while the game runs, and
    // the finished game opens as ever (spec §2.4, R-6.5c2.10).
    const foreign: TableView = { ...wire.table, bot: { label: "V3", runs_here: false } };
    expect(rowAction(foreign, "mine")).toEqual({ kind: "stranded" });
    expect(rowAction({ ...foreign, over: true }, "mine")).toMatchObject({ kind: "go", label: "View" });
  });
});
```

```ts
/** Which of the lobby's three lists a row is in (M6.5c2, R-6.5c2.7). */
export type Section = "mine" | "open" | "playing";

/** How long ago a table was opened, in a row's words (mock 02: "opened 2 days
 *  ago"). `createdAt` is the wire's Unix SECONDS and `now` milliseconds, the
 *  clock's own. A stored time is DATA, so a value that is not a number reads
 *  rather than throws (`Chat.tsx`'s `when` rule). */
export function ago(createdAt: number, now: number = Date.now()): string {
  const seconds = Math.floor(now / 1000) - createdAt;
  if (!Number.isFinite(seconds)) return "a while ago";
  if (seconds < 60) return "just now";
  const minutes = Math.floor(seconds / 60);
  if (minutes < 60) return `${minutes} min ago`;
  const hours = Math.floor(minutes / 60);
  if (hours < 24) return hours === 1 ? "an hour ago" : `${hours} hours ago`;
  const days = Math.floor(hours / 24);
  return days === 1 ? "a day ago" : `${days} days ago`;
}

/** The line under a row's name: the table's size, then what matters about it
 *  from the list it is read in (mock 02). Yours still filling says how many it
 *  waits for; somebody else's says how fresh it is; a game being played says
 *  its size alone, because its chips say who is moving. */
export function rowMeta(t: TableView, section: Section, now: number = Date.now()): string {
  const size = `${t.players} players`;
  if (t.over) return `${size} · ${tableWord(t)}`;
  if (t.status === "dealing") return `${size} · dealing`;
  if (t.status === "open") {
    const free = t.seats.filter((s) => s.kind === "open").length;
    return section === "mine" ? `${size} · waiting for ${free} more` : `${size} · opened ${ago(t.created_at, now)}`;
  }
  return section === "playing" ? size : `${size} · opened ${ago(t.created_at, now)}`;
}

/** One seat's chip, as a row draws it. */
export interface ChipModel {
  color: PlayerColor;
  label: string;
  open: boolean;
  toMove: boolean;
}

/** A chip per seat, in SEAT ORDER (mock 02): your own seats say "you", the bot
 *  says WHICH bot where the table records it (R-6.5c2.10: "the bot · V4", from
 *  `TableView.bot`), an empty seat says so, and the seat holding the turn says
 *  so in gold — "your move" when it is yours. */
export function seatChips(t: TableView): ChipModel[] {
  const turn = t.status === "playing" && !t.over ? t.to_move : null;
  return t.seats.map((seat, i) => {
    const mine = t.my_seats.includes(i);
    const who =
      seat.kind === "bot"
        ? t.bot
          ? `the bot · ${t.bot.label}`
          : "the bot"
        : seat.kind === "human" && mine
          ? "you"
          : seatName(seat);
    const toMove = turn === i;
    return {
      color: t.colors[i]!,
      label: toMove ? `${who} · ${mine ? "your move" : "to move"}` : who,
      open: seat.kind === "open",
      toMove,
    };
  });
}

/** A row's one control (R-6.5c2.7), or why it has none. */
export type RowAction =
  | { kind: "go"; label: "Play" | "View" | "Take a seat" | "Spectate"; primary: boolean; padlock: boolean }
  | { kind: "copy" }
  | { kind: "stranded" };

/** What a row's one control does.
 *
 *  **A game this server cannot continue** — its bot is one this build does not
 *  run, and it is not over — offers nothing to open: every game route refuses
 *  it (spec §2.4), and its creator still has Abandon beside the row. A finished
 *  one opens as ever. Yours: a card owed or your move is the gold Play; a table
 *  still filling is its link, to send. The padlock says a password is still
 *  wanted — at an open table whenever it is locked, at a game only until this
 *  caller has given it (`can_watch`). */
export function rowAction(t: TableView, section: Section): RowAction {
  if (t.bot && !t.bot.runs_here && !t.over) return { kind: "stranded" };
  if (section === "mine") {
    if (t.status === "open") return { kind: "copy" };
    if (t.over) return { kind: "go", label: "View", primary: false, padlock: false };
    const owed =
      t.status === "dealing"
        ? t.my_seats.some((s) => !t.chosen[s])
        : t.to_move !== null && t.my_seats.includes(t.to_move);
    return { kind: "go", label: "Play", primary: owed, padlock: false };
  }
  if (section === "open") return { kind: "go", label: "Take a seat", primary: false, padlock: t.locked };
  return { kind: "go", label: "Spectate", primary: false, padlock: t.locked && !t.can_watch };
}
```

```tsx
// The SERVER's first screen (spec §5.2; M6.5c2, R-6.5c2.7, mock 02): the band,
// then three lists as rows — the tables you sit at, the tables waiting for
// someone to sit down, and the games being played — with the lobby chat in a
// rail beside them, below them on a phone.
//
// **At `#/lobby` since M6.5b2, and no longer the screen a visitor lands on.**
// `#/` is the front door (R-6.5b2.1), which draws from this browser alone; the
// Access turnstile `/enter` redirects here, which is why the lobby needed an
// address of its own. What is left of "On this device" here is one link back.
//
// **Three scopes, ONE signal** (R-plan-4). `mine`, `open` and `playing` are
// three questions about the same store and a player reads them together, so
// one `usePolled` asks all three in one `Promise.all` and hands over one
// object — three hooks would be three connections and a screen where part of
// the lobby is older than the rest.
//
// **The stream it listens to is the HOUSE channel**, `/api/stream`, and a frame
// off it is two counters and never a table (M6.3 R-3.4, M6.4 R-6.4.7): a
// `watch` channel coalesces, so a frame naming a table would sometimes name the
// wrong one. The lobby re-reads ALL its lists on any bump instead, which is
// what `Source`'s default `frames: "wake"` mode does.
//
// **The first load is this component's, not the hook's.** The house stream says
// NOTHING on connect, so an unaided hook would show nothing until somebody else
// moved. The three headings are static and drawn at once; until the lists land,
// Your tables reads "loading…" over skeleton rows. That is the lobby's own wait
// and not the door's state D, which is over by the time the lists are asked for.
//
// **A row is the table's name and age, a chip per seat, and ONE action**
// (R-6.5c2.7; the words are `tables.ts`'s). The name is the row's one LINK
// (R-14) and the action is a button to the same address, so a table is never
// two links (`exit_game.spec.ts` counts one). The creator's own rows keep
// `Abandon` beside the action: the lobby is the only place a dealing or playing
// server table can be abandoned (R-13).
```

```tsx
  /** Put a table's address on the clipboard (mock 02's Copy link). A browser
   *  that refuses — an insecure origin has no clipboard — gets the address in
   *  the error strip instead, which a player can still copy by hand. */
  const copyLink = async (t: TableView) => {
    const url = new URL(hashOf({ kind: "table", id: t.id }), window.location.href).href;
    try {
      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(url);
      setCopied(t.id);
      setTimeout(() => setCopied((c) => (c === t.id ? null : c)), 2000);
    } catch {
      setError(`the link could not be copied — it is ${url}`);
    }
  };

  /** One row: the name — the row's one LINK — with the password tag, the line
   *  under it, a chip per seat, and the one action.
   *
   *  **Abandoning is the CREATOR's, on the Your-tables rows** (R-13), beside the
   *  action and quieter than it. The action and Abandon both NAME the table in
   *  their accessible names, so a control can never be about another row. */
  const row = (t: TableView, section: Section) => {
    const action = rowAction(t, section);
    const name = t.name ?? t.id;
    const yours = section === "mine" && t.created_by === me;
    return (
      <li key={t.id} className={section === "mine" ? "lobby-row mine" : "lobby-row"}>
        <div className="row-title">
          <div className="row-name">
            <a className="row-link" href={hashOf({ kind: "table", id: t.id })}>
              {name}
            </a>
            {t.locked && <PasswordTag />}
          </div>
          <div className="row-meta">{rowMeta(t, section)}</div>
        </div>
        <div className="row-seats">
          {seatChips(t).map((chip, i) => (
            <SeatChip key={i} color={chip.color} label={chip.label} open={chip.open} toMove={chip.toMove} />
          ))}
        </div>
        <div className="row-action">
          {action.kind === "go" && (
            <button
              type="button"
              className={action.primary ? "primary yen row-go" : "ghost row-go"}
              aria-label={`${action.label}: ${name}`}
              onClick={() => navigate({ kind: "table", id: t.id })}
            >
              {action.padlock && <Padlock />}
              {action.label}
            </button>
          )}
          {action.kind === "copy" && (
            <button
              type="button"
              className="ghost row-go"
              aria-label={`${copied === t.id ? "Copied" : "Copy link"}: ${name}`}
              onClick={() => void copyLink(t)}
            >
              {copied === t.id ? "Copied" : "Copy link"}
            </button>
          )}
          {action.kind === "stranded" && (
            <span
              className="stranded"
              title={t.bot ? `played against ${t.bot.label}, which this server no longer runs` : undefined}
            >
              can&rsquo;t continue here
            </span>
          )}
          {yours && <Abandon table={t} onDone={reread} onError={setError} />}
        </div>
      </li>
    );
  };

  const mine = lists ? unique([...lists.mine.games, ...(paged?.games ?? [])]) : [];
  const open = lists ? lists.open.games.filter(notMine) : [];
  const playing = lists ? lists.playing.games.filter(notMine) : [];
  const nextCursor = paged ? paged.next : (lists?.mine.next ?? null);
  /** Whether this deployment answers the house chat (R-6.4.6): the rail, or
   *  one column with no rail at all. */
  const rail = lobbyChat();
```

```ts
test("the lobby at 1440 and at 390: rows of name, seats and one action; the chat beside the lists, then below them; the corner a pill on the phone", async ({
  page,
  request,
}) => {
  const watch = watchForBreakage(page);
  const as = (who: string) => ({ "x-yokohama-claimed-user": who });
  /** A table, opened over the API as `who` (the open door reads the header;
   *  `it_explains.spec.ts`'s shape), and its id. */
  const create = async (who: string, data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<string> => {
    const res = await request.post("/api/games", { headers: as(who), data });
    expect(res.status(), await res.text()).toBe(201);
    return String(((await res.json()) as { id: string }).id);
  };
  const OTHER = "someone@e2e.test";
  const opened: [string, string][] = [
    [
      await create(WALKER, {
        players: 2,
        colors: ["Red", "Blue"],
        start_seat: 0,
        seats: [{ user: WALKER }, { open: true }],
        name: "Width check",
        password: "pw",
      }),
      WALKER,
    ],
    [
      await create(WALKER, {
        players: 2,
        colors: ["Red", "Blue"],
        start_seat: 0,
        seats: [{ user: WALKER }, { bot: true }],
        name: "Against the bot",
      }),
      WALKER,
    ],
    [
      await create(OTHER, {
        players: 3,
        colors: ["Red", "Blue", "Yellow"],
        start_seat: 0,
        seats: [{ user: OTHER }, { open: true }, { open: true }],
        name: "Someone else's",
      }),
      OTHER,
    ],
  ];
  try {
    await signIn(page, WALKER);
    for (const size of [DESKTOP, PHONE]) {
      await page.setViewportSize(size);
      await page.goto("/#/lobby");
      const mine = page.locator(".lobby .your-games");
      const rowOf = (name: string) =>
        mine.locator("li").filter({ has: page.getByRole("link", { name, exact: true }) });
      await expect(rowOf("Width check")).toBeVisible();
      await expect(rowOf("Width check").getByRole("img", { name: "password required" })).toBeVisible();
      // The bot's version, from the table's own `TableView.bot` (an undealt
      // table shows the production bot, spec §2.4).
      await expect(rowOf("Against the bot")).toContainText(`the bot · ${PRODUCTION_LABEL}`);
      await expect(
        page.locator(".lobby .open-tables").getByRole("button", { name: "Take a seat: Someone else's" }),
      ).toBeVisible();
      await noSidewaysScroll(page, `the lobby at ${size.width}px`);
      expect(await images(page), `the lobby draws no <img> at ${size.width}px`).toBe(0);

      const lists = (await page.locator(".lobby-lists").boundingBox())!;
      const rail = (await page.locator(".lobby section.lobby-chat").boundingBox())!;
      const pill = page.locator(".identity-pill");
      if (size === DESKTOP) {
        expect(rail.x, "the chat sits in a rail beside the lists").toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(lists.x + lists.width - 1);
        await expect(pill).toBeHidden();
        await expect(page.locator(".identity-corner").getByText("Playing as")).toBeVisible();
        // Name, seats and action on ONE line: the three share the row's middle.
        const middles = await rowOf("Width check").evaluate((li) =>
          [".row-title", ".row-seats", ".row-action"].map((s) => {
            const r = li.querySelector(s)!.getBoundingClientRect();
            return Math.round(r.top + r.height / 2);
          }),
        );
        expect(Math.max(...middles) - Math.min(...middles), `one line per row: ${middles}`).toBeLessThanOrEqual(12);
      } else {
        expect(rail.y, "the chat sits below the lists on a phone").toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(lists.y + lists.height - 1);
        await expect(pill).toBeVisible();
        await expect(page.getByRole("button", { name: "switch player" })).toBeHidden();
        await pill.click();
        await expect(page.getByRole("button", { name: "switch player" })).toBeVisible();
        await noSidewaysScroll(page, "the lobby at 390px with the corner open");
        await pill.click();
        expect(await height(page, "button", "Copy link: Width check"), "a row's action, thumb-sized").toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(44);
        expect(await height(page, "button", "New table"), "New table, thumb-sized").toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(44);
      }
      await look(page, `lobby-${size.width}`);
    }
  } finally {
    // The run's server is scratch, but a later spec's lobby should not list
    // this cell's tables.
    for (const [id, who] of opened) await request.delete(`/api/games/${id}`, { headers: as(who) });
  }
  expect(watch.failures).toEqual([]);
});
```

```rust
/// `seed_cases.json` is whatever [`WireSeed`] says TODAY, and the client is held

/// and Rust's `str::trim` part ways really do get different verdicts from the
/// server, so a client rule written on the obvious trim fails `seedRule.test.ts`.
```

```rust
/// **What the new-table form checks a seed against, as the server reads one**
/// (M6.5c2, spec §2.2 "The seed"; plan Review Focus 2).
///
/// Not a payload any route serves — a CONTRACT, frozen as
/// [`site_space_words`] is and for its reason: the client has to decide
/// something itself. The form checks a typed seed AS IT IS TYPED
/// (`web/src/seedRule.ts`), which is a second statement of [`WireSeed`]'s rule
/// — `str::trim`, then `u64::from_str`: an optional `+`, ASCII digits, at most
/// 18446744073709551615. The client cannot call Rust, so the two are held
/// together here: `seedRule.test.ts` asserts `checkSeed` gives every verdict
/// in this file, and this file is refused when the rule moves.
///
/// **The inputs sit where a hand-written check would part ways with the
/// server**: leading zeros and a `+` it takes; a full-width or an Arabic-Indic
/// digit, an exponent, a sign, a separator and one past the top it refuses;
/// and TWO that split JavaScript's own `String.prototype.trim` from Rust's —
/// U+FEFF, which JavaScript strips and Rust does not, and U+0085, which Rust
/// strips and JavaScript does not (measured on both sides when this was
/// written). None is the walk's [`SETUP_SEED`], in either spelling: the
/// leakage pin scans this file like every other.
///
/// [`WireSeed`]: yokohama_web::tables::WireSeed
const SEED_INPUTS: &[&str] = &[
    "+007 ",
    " 7",
    "007",
    "\u{ff17}",
    "1e3",
    "-1",
    "18446744073709551616",
    "18446744073709551615",
    "",
    " ",
    "0",
    "+0",
    "-0",
    "+",
    "12 34",
    "\t42\n",
    "\u{a0}12\u{a0}",
    "\u{feff}12",
    "\u{85}12",
    "\u{3000}12\u{3000}",
    "0x10",
    "1_000",
    "12.0",
    "\u{663}",
    "00000000000000000000018446744073709551615",
    "99999999999999999999",
];

/// Each input with [`WireSeed`]'s own verdict — the create's `seed` field
/// deserialized from the STRING a browser sends, exactly as `NewGame` reads it.
///
/// [`WireSeed`]: yokohama_web::tables::WireSeed
fn seed_cases() -> Value {
    Value::Array(
        SEED_INPUTS
            .iter()
            .map(|raw| {
                let ok = serde_json::from_value::<yokohama_web::tables::WireSeed>(Value::String(
                    (*raw).to_string(),
                ))
                .is_ok();
                serde_json::json!({ "raw": raw, "ok": ok })
            })
            .collect(),
    )
}
```

- [ ] **Step 9: The rule, and its contract entry.** Create `web/src/seedRule.ts`:

```ts
// The seed the new-table form checks AS IT IS TYPED (M6.5c2, spec §2.2 "The
// seed"; R-6.5c2.8), by the server's own rule.
//
// **A second statement of `WireSeed`, and held to it.** The server reads a seed
// sent as text with `str::trim` and then `u64::from_str` (`tables.rs`,
// `WireSeed`'s `Deserialize`): an optional `+`, ASCII digits, at most
// 18446744073709551615. The form runs the same rule so a bad value explains
// itself in place instead of arriving as the create's 400 — and a copy of a rule
// is a thing that drifts, so `seedRule.test.ts` asserts this file's verdict on
// every input in `wire/seed_cases.json`, which is the server's own.
//
// **A seed is never a number here.** A `u64` does not survive a JavaScript
// number (`Number("18446744073709551557")` is 18446744073709552000), so the value
// stays text from the keystroke to the wire and the range is compared as a
// `BigInt`.

/** The largest seed there is: `u64::MAX`. */
const MAX = 18_446_744_073_709_551_615n;

/** The rule, in the words both refusals end with (mock 07). */
const RULE =
  "a seed is a whole number from 0 to 18446744073709551615. Leave it blank to have the server draw one.";

/**
 * `str::trim` as Rust reads it: the Unicode `White_Space` property off both ends.
 *
 * **Not `String.prototype.trim`**, which strips a different set — it removes
 * U+FEFF (not `White_Space`) and keeps U+0085 (which is). Measured both ways
 * when this was written, and pinned by the committed table's rows for exactly
 * those two characters.
 */
export const trimSeed = (raw: string): string =>
  raw.replace(/^\p{White_Space}+|\p{White_Space}+$/gu, "");

export type SeedVerdict = { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: string };

/** Whether the server would take `raw` as a seed, and why not where it would
 *  not. **A blank field is the FORM's question, not this one's**: blank means
 *  "the server draws one" and is never sent, while `WireSeed` refuses an empty
 *  string like any other non-number — so the table says `false` for `""` and
 *  the form never asks. */
export function checkSeed(raw: string): SeedVerdict {
  const digits = /^\+?([0-9]+)$/.exec(trimSeed(raw));
  if (digits === null) return { ok: false, reason: `Not a whole number: ${RULE}` };
  if (BigInt(digits[1]!) > MAX) return { ok: false, reason: `Too large: ${RULE}` };
  return { ok: true };
}
```

```ts
type SeedCase = { raw: string; ok: boolean };
const _seedCases: Widen<SeedCase[]> = seedCases;
```

```tsx
/** `drawSeat` is fair over every count the form offers: a byte at or past the
 *  largest multiple of `n` is drawn again rather than folded onto seat 0. */
describe("the draw", () => {
  it("draws again past the largest multiple of the count", () => {
    const bytes = [255, 254, 4];
    vi.spyOn(crypto, "getRandomValues").mockImplementation(((array: Uint8Array) => {
      array[0] = bytes.shift()!;
      return array;
    }) as typeof crypto.getRandomValues);
    // 256 % 3 is 1, so only 255 is past the last multiple: it is drawn again,
    // and 254 % 3 = 2 is the seat.
    expect(drawSeat(3)).toBe(2);
    expect(drawSeat(4)).toBe(0); // 4 % 4
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 13: The form.** Replace `web/src/NewGame.tsx` whole:

```tsx
// Setup (spec §5.3; M6.5c2 spec §2.2, R-6.5c2.8, mock 07): who sits where, who
// plays first, what the table is called, whether it wants a password — and,
// folded away for a fixture or a diagnostic, which seed.
//
// **TWO forms in one file, and they share only what is truly one thing.** The
// table form (`#/new`) asks everything a room asks; the form for a game on this
// device (`#/new/local`) asks only what a game against the bot can be asked —
// its name and who starts. They share the segmented control, the submit's guard
// and the create call.
//
// **"Your name" left both forms** (R-6.5c2.8): the lobby's corner owns it, and
// what a create sends as `display_name` is the name this browser already keeps,
// read when the form is sent. The form is about the table.

import { useRef, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import {
  api,
  ApiError,
  displayName,
  LOCAL_USER,
  useIdentityMode,
  type NewGameRequest,
  type SeatRequest,
} from "./api";
import { LobbyBand } from "./Band";
import { seatClass } from "./Cards";
import { VersionTag } from "./Chips";
import { normalizeName } from "./nameRule";
import { Refusal } from "./Refusal";
import { checkSeed, trimSeed } from "./seedRule";
import type { PlayerColor, TableView } from "./types";
import productionBot from "./wire/production_bot.json";

/** The seat colours, in the ENGINE's order. */
const COLORS = ["Red", "Blue", "Yellow", "Green"] as const;

/** The bot this build deals, by its short label (R-6.5c2.10) — read at BUILD
 *  time from the contract file `wire_fixtures` emits and refuses when stale, so
 *  the form asks the server nothing and states no second truth (spec §2.4). */
const BOT_LABEL = productionBot.label;

/** One seat row as the form holds it before it is a `SeatRequest`. `person`
 *  keeps its typed text while the row is switched away, so flipping a row back
 *  and forth loses nothing. */
type SeatRow = { kind: "me" | "person" | "bot" | "open"; person: string };

/** Who plays first: a seat, or a draw made when the form is sent. */
type First = number | "random";

/** The default seating for a count. **The bot sits at seat 1, and only at two
 *  players (R-P10)**; above two the other seats default to OPEN (spec §5.3). */
const defaultSeats = (players: number): SeatRow[] =>
  Array.from({ length: players }, (_, i) => ({
    kind: i === 0 ? ("me" as const) : players === 2 ? ("bot" as const) : ("open" as const),
    person: "",
  }));

/** A seat drawn over `n` from the browser's own generator, at the moment the
 *  form is SENT (R-6.5c2.8). **Rejection sampling**, so every seat is equally
 *  likely: a byte taken modulo three would favour seat 0 by one part in 85, so
 *  a byte at or past the largest multiple of `n` is drawn again. */
export function drawSeat(n: number): number {
  const byte = new Uint8Array(1);
  const limit = 256 - (256 % n);
  for (;;) {
    crypto.getRandomValues(byte);
    if (byte[0]! < limit) return byte[0]! % n;
  }
}

/** A few choices, one of them on: radio buttons drawn as segments (mock 07), so
 *  the arrow keys walk the group and a screen reader says "2 of 3" for free. */
function Segmented<T extends number | string>({
  legend,
  name,
  options,
  value,
  onChange,
}: {
  legend: string;
  name: string;
  options: readonly { value: T; label: string }[];
  value: T;
  onChange: (v: T) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <fieldset className="form-field">
      <legend>{legend}</legend>
      <div className="seg">
        {options.map((o) => (
          <label key={String(o.value)} className={o.value === value ? "on" : undefined}>
            <input
              type="radio"
              name={name}
              checked={o.value === value}
              onChange={() => onChange(o.value)}
            />
            {o.label}
          </label>
        ))}
      </div>
    </fieldset>
  );
}

/** The submit's guard, for both forms. **A ref decides whether the request
 *  happens; the state only disables the button** — React batches, so two clicks
 *  in one tick both read a `busy` STATE of false, and two `POST /api/games` are
 *  two different tables. */
function useSubmit() {
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const inFlight = useRef(false);
  const run = async (fn: () => Promise<void>) => {
    if (inFlight.current) return;
    inFlight.current = true;
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      setError(e instanceof ApiError ? e.message : String(e));
    } finally {
      inFlight.current = false;
      setBusy(false);
    }
  };
  return { busy, error, run };
}

/** The name this browser keeps, trimmed, or nothing — read when a form is
 *  SENT, so a name set in the lobby's corner a moment ago is the one used. */
const keptName = (): Partial<Pick<NewGameRequest, "display_name">> => {
  const shown = displayName()?.trim();
  return shown ? { display_name: shown } : {};
};

export function NewGame({
  me,
  onCreated,
  onCancel,
  who,
  local,
}: {
  /** Who this browser plays as, from the DOOR — never from storage: what a
   *  claimed header is worth is the server's answer at `/api/me`. */
  me: string;
  /** The table was opened; `App` takes it from here. Awaited inside the
   *  submit, so a refusal from `App`'s own two requests lands in this form. */
  onCreated: (table: TableView) => void | Promise<void>;
  /** Back out without opening anything: the lobby for the table form, the door
   *  for the local one (mock 07's Cancel). */
  onCancel: () => void;
  /** The band's corner, built by `App` (the identity corner, Task 11). The
   *  local form draws none — it is a game on this device (mock 07). */
  who?: ReactNode;
  /** Open the table in THIS BROWSER (M6.5b, R-6.5b.8): two seats, you and the
   *  bot, no password and no seed — `draw_seed` inside the module draws it. */
  local?: boolean;
}) {
  return local ? (
    <LocalForm onCreated={onCreated} onCancel={onCancel} />
  ) : (
    <TableForm me={me} onCreated={onCreated} onCancel={onCancel} who={who} />
  );
}

function TableForm({
  me,
  onCreated,
  onCancel,
  who,
}: {
  me: string;
  onCreated: (table: TableView) => void | Promise<void>;
  onCancel: () => void;
  who?: ReactNode;
}) {
  const [players, setPlayers] = useState(2);
  const [seats, setSeats] = useState<SeatRow[]>(() => defaultSeats(2));
  const [first, setFirst] = useState<First>(0);
  const [name, setName] = useState("");
  const [locked, setLocked] = useState(false);
  const [password, setPassword] = useState("");
  const [seedText, setSeedText] = useState("");
  const [advanced, setAdvanced] = useState(false);
  const { busy, error, run } = useSubmit();
  /** **A specific person is a NAME on an open door and an ADDRESS behind
   *  Access** (spec §2.1): the door's own name, from `/api/health`. */
  const byName = useIdentityMode() === "open";
  const colors = COLORS.slice(0, players) as PlayerColor[];

  /** Blank is "the server draws one" and is never sent; anything else is
   *  checked by the server's own rule as it is typed (spec §2.2). */
  const seedVerdict = trimSeed(seedText) === "" ? null : checkSeed(seedText);
  const seedError = seedVerdict !== null && !seedVerdict.ok ? seedVerdict.reason : null;

  /** Why a "specific person" row cannot be sent: `null` when it can, `""` when
   *  it is blank — held without a sentence, because nothing typed is not a
   *  mistake yet — and the key grammar's own reason otherwise (`nameRule.ts`). */
  const personError = (row: SeatRow): string | null => {
    if (row.kind !== "person") return null;
    if (row.person.trim() === "") return "";
    const n = normalizeName(row.person);
    return n.ok ? null : n.reason;
  };
  const held = seedError !== null || seats.some((r) => personError(r) !== null);

  /** **Rebuilt, not resized**: the bot is legal at two players only, so a seat
   *  list carried across a count change would strand a bot at three (R-P10).
   *  A first player the new count still has is kept. */
  const setCount = (n: number) => {
    setPlayers(n);
    setSeats(defaultSeats(n));
    setFirst((f) => (f === "random" || f < n ? f : 0));
  };
  const setRow = (i: number, patch: Partial<SeatRow>) =>
    setSeats((rows) => rows.map((r, n) => (n === i ? { ...r, ...patch } : r)));

  const body = (): NewGameRequest => {
    const seed = trimSeed(seedText);
    return {
      players,
      colors: [...colors],
      start_seat: first === "random" ? drawSeat(players) : first,
      // **Normalized here, because the server keys it so** (R-1.1; spec §2.1):
      // a seat bound under one spelling answers to that key alone.
      seats: seats.map((row): SeatRequest => {
        if (row.kind === "bot") return { bot: true };
        if (row.kind === "open") return { open: true };
        if (row.kind === "me") return { user: me };
        const n = normalizeName(row.person);
        return { user: n.ok ? n.key : row.person.trim() };
      }),
      // The seed is a STRING from the keystroke to the wire (`WireSeed`), and
      // blank is omitted: the board is an injective fingerprint of the seed, so
      // the server's own draw is the safe default.
      ...(seed ? { seed } : {}),
      ...(name.trim() ? { name: name.trim() } : {}),
      ...keptName(),
      // Only when ticked AND typed: a password field left blank under a ticked
      // box would lock a table nobody can join.
      ...(locked && password.trim() ? { password: password.trim() } : {}),
    };
  };

  /** A table with an open seat is not dealt when it is created, so "Deal" there
   *  would promise the set table and hand over a waiting room. */
  const opensSeats = seats.some((r) => r.kind === "open");

  return (
    <div className="band-screen">
      <LobbyBand crumbs={["Lobby", "New table"]} corner={who} />
      <div className="setup">
        {/* **Task 9's raised card**, and the title a level under the band's
            crumb: the band's last crumb is the page's `<h2>` and reads "New
            table" too (mock 07 draws both). */}
        <section className="raised-card form-card" aria-labelledby="new-table-title">
          <div className="card-band vp" aria-hidden="true" />
          <div className="card-in">
            <h3 id="new-table-title">New table</h3>

            {/* **Free text, and never an id** (R-2.4); the placeholder is the
                whole explanation (R-6.5c2.8: no subtext). */}
            <div className="form-field">
              <label htmlFor="name">Name</label>
              <input
                id="name"
                value={name}
                autoComplete="off"
                placeholder="ID shown in the lobby if left blank"
                onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)}
              />
            </div>

            <Segmented
              legend="Players"
              name="players"
              options={[2, 3, 4].map((n) => ({ value: n, label: String(n) }))}
              value={players}
              onChange={setCount}
            />

            <fieldset className="form-field">
              <legend>Seats</legend>
              {seats.map((row, i) => {
                const color = colors[i]!;
                const why = personError(row);
                return (
                  <div className="form-seat" key={color}>
                    <span className="color">
                      <span className={`seat-dot ${seatClass(color)}`} aria-hidden="true" />
                      {color}
                    </span>
                    <div className="pick">
                      <select
                        aria-label={`${color} seat`}
                        value={row.kind}
                        onChange={(e) => setRow(i, { kind: e.target.value as SeatRow["kind"] })}
                      >
                        <option value="me">You</option>
                        <option value="open">Open seat</option>
                        <option value="person">A specific person</option>
                        {players === 2 && <option value="bot">The bot</option>}
                      </select>
                      {row.kind === "bot" && <VersionTag label={BOT_LABEL} />}
                    </div>
                    {row.kind === "person" && (
                      <input
                        className="person"
                        aria-label={`${color} player's ${byName ? "name" : "address"}`}
                        type={byName ? "text" : "email"}
                        autoComplete="off"
                        placeholder={byName ? "their name" : "someone@example.com"}
                        value={row.person}
                        aria-invalid={why ? true : undefined}
                        aria-describedby={why ? `seat-${i}-error` : undefined}
                        onChange={(e) => setRow(i, { person: e.target.value })}
                      />
                    )}
                    {why ? (
                      <p className="field-error" id={`seat-${i}-error`}>
                        {why}
                      </p>
                    ) : null}
                  </div>
                );
              })}
              {/* R-P10 said where the choice is made, with the version the bot
                  plays as — shown, never chosen (R-6.5c2.10). */}
              <p className="seat-note">
                The bot <VersionTag label={BOT_LABEL} /> is offered at two players only: that is where
                it has been measured.
              </p>
            </fieldset>

            <Segmented<First>
              legend="First player"
              name="first"
              options={[
                ...colors.map((c, i) => ({ value: i as First, label: c })),
                { value: "random" as First, label: "Random" },
              ]}
              value={first}
              onChange={setFirst}
            />

            {/* **The checkbox carries the row's only label**, and the label
                says what the password guards: joining AND spectating. The box
                it reveals is asked about by its own name, with no placeholder
                (R-6.5c2.8). */}
            <div className="form-field">
              <label className="toggle">
                <input
                  type="checkbox"
                  checked={locked}
                  onChange={(e) => {
                    setLocked(e.target.checked);
                    // Cleared with the box: an unticked form cannot carry a
                    // word the player can no longer see.
                    if (!e.target.checked) setPassword("");
                  }}
                />
                <span className="switch-track" aria-hidden="true" />
                Ask for a password to join or spectate
              </label>
              {locked && (
                <input
                  className="password"
                  type="password"
                  aria-label="Table password"
                  autoComplete="new-password"
                  value={password}
                  onChange={(e) => setPassword(e.target.value)}
                />
              )}
            </div>

            {/* **Held open while the seed is refused**: a button held for a
                reason the player cannot see is a button that looks broken. */}
            <details
              className="fold"
              open={advanced || seedError !== null}
              onToggle={(e) => setAdvanced(e.currentTarget.open)}
            >
              <summary>Advanced</summary>
              <div className="form-field">
                <label htmlFor="seed">Seed</label>
                <input
                  id="seed"
                  value={seedText}
                  inputMode="numeric"
                  autoComplete="off"
                  spellCheck={false}
                  aria-invalid={seedError !== null ? true : undefined}
                  aria-describedby={seedError !== null ? "seed-error" : undefined}
                  onChange={(e) => setSeedText(e.target.value)}
                />
                {seedError !== null && (
                  <p className="field-error" id="seed-error">
                    {seedError}
                  </p>
                )}
              </div>
            </details>

            <div className="form-foot">
              <button type="button" className="quiet-link" onClick={onCancel}>
                Cancel
              </button>
              <button
                type="button"
                className="primary"
                disabled={busy || held}
                onClick={() =>
                  run(async () => {
                    await onCreated(await api.create(body()));
                  })
                }
              >
                {opensSeats ? "Open table" : "Deal"}
              </button>
            </div>
            {error && <Refusal sentence={error} />}
          </div>
        </section>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

function LocalForm({
  onCreated,
  onCancel,
}: {
  onCreated: (table: TableView) => void | Promise<void>;
  onCancel: () => void;
}) {
  const [name, setName] = useState("");
  const [first, setFirst] = useState<First>(0);
  const { busy, error, run } = useSubmit();

  const body = (): NewGameRequest => ({
    players: 2,
    colors: ["Red", "Blue"],
    start_seat: first === "random" ? drawSeat(2) : first,
    // **Seated by the MODULE's own address** (R-6.5b.1): `dispatch` answers as
    // `local@browser` for every local call, so a create naming anyone else
    // would open a table whose own player holds no seat. **No seed, ever**:
    // `draw_seed` inside the module draws it (spec §2.2 of M6.5b).
    seats: [{ user: LOCAL_USER }, { bot: true }],
    ...(name.trim() ? { name: name.trim() } : {}),
    ...keptName(),
  });

  return (
    <div className="band-screen">
      <LobbyBand crumbs={["On this device"]} corner={undefined} />
      <div className="setup">
        <section className="raised-card form-card local" aria-labelledby="new-local-title">
          <div className="card-band yen" aria-hidden="true" />
          <div className="card-in">
            {/* The tag beside the heading and not inside it, so the heading's
                name is the sentence and the version is a fact next to it. */}
            <div className="title-row">
              <h3 id="new-local-title">New game against the bot</h3>
              <VersionTag label={BOT_LABEL} />
            </div>
            <p className="lede">Two players: you and the bot.</p>

            <div className="form-field">
              <label htmlFor="name">Name</label>
              <input
                id="name"
                value={name}
                autoComplete="off"
                placeholder="Optional"
                onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)}
              />
            </div>

            {/* The seating is not a choice here, so it is not a control. */}
            <div className="form-field">
              <span className="field-label" id="local-seats">
                Seats
              </span>
              <ul className="form-seats" aria-labelledby="local-seats">
                <li className="form-seat">
                  <span className="color">
                    <span className={`seat-dot ${seatClass("Red")}`} aria-hidden="true" />
                    Red
                  </span>
                  <span>You</span>
                </li>
                <li className="form-seat">
                  <span className="color">
                    <span className={`seat-dot ${seatClass("Blue")}`} aria-hidden="true" />
                    Blue
                  </span>
                  <span>
                    The bot <VersionTag label={BOT_LABEL} />
                  </span>
                </li>
              </ul>
            </div>

            <Segmented<First>
              legend="First player"
              name="first"
              options={[
                { value: 0, label: "You" },
                { value: 1, label: "The bot" },
                { value: "random", label: "Random" },
              ]}
              value={first}
              onChange={setFirst}
            />

            <div className="form-foot">
              <button type="button" className="quiet-link" onClick={onCancel}>
                Cancel
              </button>
              <button
                type="button"
                className="primary yen"
                disabled={busy}
                onClick={() =>
                  run(async () => {
                    // **The host is the caller's INTENT** (R-6.5b.12): a create
                    // carries no id yet, so nothing in the path could route it.
                    await onCreated(await api.create(body(), "local"));
                  })
                }
              >
                Deal
              </button>
            </div>
            {error && <Refusal sentence={error} />}
          </div>
        </section>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```css
/* ---- the setup screens' shared frame (M6.5c2, spec §2.2) --------------------
 *
 * A screen with the lobby band across its top and its `.setup` column under it;
 * the column's own 3rem top margin was for a page with no header. */
.band-screen > .setup { margin-top: 1.5rem; }

/* ---- the two forms (M6.5c2, R-6.5c2.8; mock 07, mock 11) ---------------------
 *
 * Task 9's raised card (`.raised-card`, `.card-band.vp` / `.yen`, `.card-in`):
 * the table form's band is the VP blue its submit is, the local form's the yen
 * its Deal is (`button.primary.yen`). The form's own: its width, a roomier
 * inside, and its title — an `h3` under the band's `h2` crumb, drawn at a
 * title's size rather than `.setup h3`'s (`:901`), which it follows in the file
 * at the same specificity. */
.form-card { max-width: 35rem; margin: 0 auto; }
.form-card > .card-in { padding: 1.1rem 1.4rem 1.25rem; }
.form-card h3 { font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 600; margin: 0.1rem 0 0; }
.form-card .title-row { display: flex; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0.25rem; }
.form-card .lede { color: var(--fg-dim); font-size: 12.5px; margin: 0.25rem 0 0; }
.form-field { margin: 0.9rem 0 0; padding: 0; border: 0; min-width: 0; }
.form-field > label:not(.toggle), .form-field > legend, .form-field > .field-label {
  display: block; padding: 0; margin: 0 0 0.4rem;
  font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--fg-faint);
}
.form-card input:not([type="radio"]):not([type="checkbox"]), .form-card select {
  width: 100%; min-height: 2.15rem;
  background: var(--bg-sunken); color: var(--fg); border: 1px solid var(--line-bright);
  border-radius: var(--radius); padding: 0.45rem 0.65rem; font: inherit;
}
.form-card input::placeholder { color: var(--fg-faint); }
.form-card input[aria-invalid="true"] {
  border-color: var(--warn);
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in oklab, var(--warn) 18%, transparent);
}
.field-error { color: var(--warn); font-size: 11.5px; margin: 0.4rem 0 0; }

/* Segments: the radio IS the segment, transparent over its label, so a click
 * anywhere on the label lands on it and the arrow keys walk the group. */
.seg { display: inline-flex; flex-wrap: wrap; border: 1px solid var(--line-bright); border-radius: 5px; overflow: hidden; }
.seg label {
  position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center;
  padding: 0.38rem 0.95rem; color: var(--fg-dim); cursor: pointer;
  border-right: 1px solid var(--line-bright);
}
.seg label:last-child { border-right: 0; }
.seg label.on {
  color: var(--fg); font-weight: 700;
  background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--vp) 14%, var(--bg-raised));
  box-shadow: inset 0 -2px 0 var(--vp);
}
.seg input { position: absolute; inset: 0; margin: 0; opacity: 0; cursor: pointer; }
.seg label:has(input:focus-visible) { outline: 2px solid var(--vp); outline-offset: -2px; }

/* One seat: its colour, then who holds it. A person's field drops UNDER the
 * choice, so a phone never fits three controls on one line. */
.form-seat {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: 6rem minmax(0, 1fr); align-items: center;
  gap: 0.35rem 0.7rem; padding: 0.4rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);
}
.form-seat:last-of-type { border-bottom: 0; }
.form-seats { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; }
.form-seat .color { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.45rem; font-size: 12px; }
.form-seat .pick { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; min-width: 0; }
.form-seat .pick select { max-width: 16rem; }
.form-seat .person, .form-seat .field-error { grid-column: 2; }
.seat-note { color: var(--fg-faint); font-size: 11.5px; margin: 0.45rem 0 0; }

/* The password switch: a real checkbox under a drawn track and knob. `switch-track`,
 * never `track`, which is the dashboard's own unscoped flex row (`:633`). */
.toggle { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6rem; cursor: pointer; }
.toggle input { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; margin: 0; opacity: 0; }
.toggle .switch-track {
  flex: none; position: relative; width: 30px; height: 17px; border-radius: 99px;
  background: var(--line-bright); transition: background 0.15s;
}
.toggle .switch-track::after {
  content: ""; position: absolute; top: 2px; left: 2px; width: 13px; height: 13px;
  border-radius: 50%; background: var(--bg); transition: transform 0.15s;
}
.toggle input:checked + .switch-track { background: var(--vp); }
.toggle input:checked + .switch-track::after { transform: translateX(13px); }
.toggle input:focus-visible + .switch-track { outline: 2px solid var(--vp); outline-offset: 2px; }
.form-field .password { margin-top: 0.5rem; max-width: 19rem; }

/* The fold the seed lives in; its marker is drawn, so every engine draws one. */
.fold { margin-top: 1rem; padding-top: 0.7rem; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); }
.fold > summary { cursor: pointer; font-size: 12px; list-style: none; }
.fold > summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; }
.fold > summary::before { content: "\25B8\00a0"; color: var(--fg-faint); }
.fold[open] > summary::before { content: "\25BE\00a0"; }
.fold .form-field { margin-top: 0.6rem; }
.fold #seed { max-width: 23rem; }

/* The way out and the way on, on one line. */
.form-foot { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem; margin-top: 1.1rem; }
.quiet-link {
  background: none; border: 0; padding: 0; font: inherit; cursor: pointer;
  color: var(--fg-dim); text-decoration: underline;
  text-decoration-color: var(--line-bright); text-underline-offset: 3px;
}
.quiet-link:hover { color: var(--fg); }

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .toggle .switch-track, .toggle .switch-track::after { transition: none; }
}
/* A phone (mock 11): one column, and every control a thumb's size — 44 px, which
 * the browser suite's width cells read back. */
@media (max-width: 480px) {
  .band-screen > .setup { margin-top: 1rem; }
  .form-card > .card-in { padding: 1rem; }
  .form-card input:not([type="radio"]):not([type="checkbox"]), .form-card select,
  .form-foot button.primary, .seg label { min-height: 2.75rem; }
  .form-foot button.primary { flex: 1 1 auto; }
}
```

```ts
/**
 * Set what this browser calls itself — the name a seat it takes is labelled
 * with (M6.5c2, R-6.5c2.8). The forms and the join no longer ask for one — the
 * lobby's corner owns it — so a walk that reads a seat's label says, here, what
 * it is. The key is `api.ts`'s `DISPLAY_NAME_KEY`, spelled as a literal the way
 * `plays_a_whole_game` spells the claimed user's.
 */
export async function nameThisBrowser(page: Page, name: string): Promise<void> {
  await page.evaluate((n) => localStorage.setItem("yokohama.display_name", n), name);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 20: The forms' own width cells, and the seed refused in place (Review Focus 2).** Create
  `web/e2e/the_forms.spec.ts`:

```ts
// **The two setup forms, drawn by a real browser** (M6.5c2, spec §2.2 "The
// forms", "The seed", "The phone"; R-6.5c2.8; mock 07, mock 11).
//
// jsdom never loads `styles.css`, so what is asserted here is what only a
// stylesheet decides: nothing scrolls sideways at a phone's 390 px or at 1280,
// the control that sends the form is a thumb's size on the phone, and the
// seed's refusal is drawn INSIDE the open fold (Review Focus 2's other half —
// `seedRule.test.ts` holds the rule itself).
//
// Each cell writes a picture of the form to its own output directory: the
// headed look the spec asks for (§3) is a person comparing those with mock 07
// and mock 11, and the task's report says what differs.

import type { Page } from "@playwright/test";
import { expect, test } from "./sw";
import { haveBrowser } from "../playwright.config";
import { blame, newGameForm, readOverflow, watchForBreakage } from "./harness";

test.skip(!haveBrowser, "no Chromium — YOKOHAMA_WEB_E2E_OPTIONAL=1; this run tested NOTHING");

/** Lay the page out at `width`, and read nothing until the layout is DONE — a
 *  resize and a read in one tick can be answered from the pre-resize box. */
async function atWidth(page: Page, width: number): Promise<void> {
  await page.setViewportSize({ width, height: 844 });
  await page.evaluate(() => new Promise((r) => requestAnimationFrame(() => r(null))));
}

/** The page may not scroll sideways — the lane's recorded property. */
async function fits(page: Page, what: string, width: number): Promise<void> {
  const read = await readOverflow(page);
  expect(
    read.docScrollWidth - read.docClientWidth,
    `${what} scrolls sideways at ${width}px: ${blame(read)}`,
  ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0);
}

for (const width of [1280, 390] as const) {
  test(`the new-table form fits ${width} px at its widest, and refuses a bad seed in its fold`, async ({
    page,
  }, info) => {
    const watch = watchForBreakage(page);
    await newGameForm(page);
    await atWidth(page, width);
    // **The form at its WIDEST** — four seats, one of them a specific person
    // (whose field drops under the row), four colours and Random to start, the
    // password open and the fold open — because a width claim about the
    // narrowest form proves nothing about this one.
    await page.getByRole("group", { name: "Players" }).getByRole("radio", { name: "4", exact: true }).check();
    await page.getByRole("combobox", { name: "Green seat", exact: true }).selectOption("person");
    await page.getByLabel(/^Green player's (name|address)$/).fill("someone else");
    await page.getByLabel("Ask for a password to join or spectate", { exact: true }).check();
    await page.getByText("Advanced", { exact: true }).click();
    const seed = page.getByLabel("Seed", { exact: true });
    const submit = page.getByRole("button", { name: "Open table" });
    // Anti-vacuity: the controls this claim is about are really drawn.
    await expect(seed).toBeVisible();
    await expect(submit).toBeEnabled();

    // One past the top of a u64 (Review Focus 2): refused IN PLACE, the button held.
    await seed.fill("18446744073709551616");
    const fold = page.locator("details.fold");
    const refusal = fold.getByText(/^Too large: a seed is a whole number from 0 to 18446744073709551615\./);
    await expect(refusal).toBeVisible();
    await expect(seed).toHaveAttribute("aria-invalid", "true");
    await expect(submit).toBeDisabled();
    // **Inside the fold's own box**, which is what "in place" means on a
    // screen: a sentence the stylesheet put somewhere else sits beside nothing.
    const foldBox = (await fold.boundingBox())!;
    const sentenceBox = (await refusal.boundingBox())!;
    expect(sentenceBox.y).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(foldBox.y);
    expect(sentenceBox.y + sentenceBox.height).toBeLessThanOrEqual(foldBox.y + foldBox.height + 1);
    await fits(page, "the new-table form", width);
    if (width === 390) {
      const box = (await submit.boundingBox())!;
      expect(box.height, "the submit is a thumb's size on a phone").toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(44);
      expect(box.x + box.width, "the submit's right edge is on the screen").toBeLessThanOrEqual(390);
    }
    await page.screenshot({ path: info.outputPath(`new-table-${width}.png`), fullPage: true });

    // And a seed the SERVER takes — a `+`, leading zeros and a space — lets the
    // form go: the fold agrees with `WireSeed`, not with a stricter guess.
    await seed.fill("+007 ");
    await expect(refusal).toHaveCount(0);
    await expect(submit).toBeEnabled();
    expect(watch.failures).toEqual([]);
  });

  test(`the form for a game on this device fits ${width} px`, async ({ page }, info) => {
    const watch = watchForBreakage(page);
    // **No sign-in**: the local form needs no door (R-6.5b.8).
    await page.goto("/#/new/local");
    await atWidth(page, width);
    await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "New game against the bot", exact: true })).toBeVisible();
    const deal = page.getByRole("button", { name: "Deal" });
    await expect(deal).toBeEnabled();
    await page.getByRole("group", { name: "First player" }).getByRole("radio", { name: "Random", exact: true }).check();
    await fits(page, "the local form", width);
    if (width === 390) {
      const box = (await deal.boundingBox())!;
      expect(box.height, "Deal is a thumb's size on a phone").toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(44);
    }
    await page.screenshot({ path: info.outputPath(`new-local-${width}.png`), fullPage: true });
    expect(watch.failures).toEqual([]);
  });
}
```

```tsx
  const corner = (

            waiting for the lobby would find it on this screen. */}
        <LobbyBand crumbs={["Lobby", "Table"]} corner={corner} />
        <div className="setup open-table">
          {error ? <Refusal sentence={error} /> : <p className="muted">loading&hellip;</p>}
        </div>
      </div>

  const onlySeat = !seated && free.length === 1 ? free[0]! : null;

  const opener = table.seats.find((s) => s.kind === "human" && s.user === table.created_by);
  const owner = opener?.kind === "human" ? (opener.name ?? opener.user) : table.created_by;

  /** One seat, as its card says it (mock 08, 09). */
  const face = (s: SeatDoc, i: number) => {

    switch (s.kind) {
      case "open":
        if (seated) {
          return {
            color, caption, open: true, who: "Open seat",
            note: table.locked ? "anyone in the lobby, with the password" : "anyone in the lobby",
          };

        return {

              type="button"
              className="primary sit"

            >

            </button>

      // seat left open, so it is dealing from its create — and drawn anyway, so
      // a fourth kind of seat is a compile error here and not a blank card.
      case "bot":
        return { color, caption, who: "The bot" };
      case "human":
        return table.my_seats.includes(i)
          ? { color, caption, who: "You", note: s.name ?? s.user }
          : { color, caption, who: s.name ?? s.user, note: "seated" };
    }
  };

  const left = free.length === 1 ? "one seat left" : free.length === 2 ? "two seats left" : `${free.length} seats left`;
  const waiting = `Waiting for ${free.length} more ${free.length === 1 ? "player" : "players"}`;

  return (

        {!seated && table.locked && free.length > 0 && (

      </div>

/** "Invite people" (mock 08): the link, Copy, and — at a locked table — the
 *  reminder that the password travels separately. Worded for the person who
 *  SET it and for anyone else seated, who did not. */
function Invite({ url, locked, mine }: { url: string; locked: boolean; mine: boolean }) {
  const [copied, setCopied] = useState(false);
  return (
    <section className="invite" aria-labelledby="invite-caption">
      <h3 id="invite-caption" className="caption">
        Invite people
      </h3>
      <div className="row">
        {/* Read-only rather than a sentence, so it can be selected and copied by
            hand where the clipboard is refused — in every browser that has not
            granted it, and on a page served over plain HTTP. */}
        <input aria-label="Invite link" readOnly value={url} onFocus={(e) => e.currentTarget.select()} />
        <button
          type="button"
          className="ghost"
          onClick={() => {
            // **The rejection is swallowed, deliberately**: a refused clipboard
            // is a `pageerror` the browser gate counts, and the field beside
            // this holds the link either way.
            navigator.clipboard?.writeText(url).catch(() => {});
            setCopied(true);
          }}
        >
          {copied ? "Copied" : "Copy link"}
        </button>
      </div>
      {locked && (
        <p className="note">
          {mine ? "They'll need the password you set. Send it separately." : "They'll need the table's password."}
        </p>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}
```

```css
/* ---- waiting and joining (M6.5c2, R-6.5c2.9; mock 08, mock 09, mock 11) ------ */
/* The page's own title under the band: an `h3`, a level under the band's `h2`
 * crumb (Task 9), drawn at a title's size rather than `.setup h3`'s (`:901`). */
.setup h3.page-title { font-size: 1.9rem; font-weight: 600; margin: 0.2rem 0 0.3rem; }
/* A notice's title is a sentence, not a name: smaller, at every width (the
 * phone rule below is outranked). */
.setup .notice-card h3.page-title { font-size: 1.35rem; margin-top: 0; }
.open-table .table-status {
  display: flex; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.6rem;
  color: var(--fg-dim); margin: 0.3rem 0 1rem;
}
/* The three inputs these screens own, by name — never `.open-table input`,
 * which would also restyle the chat panel's own box on the same screen. */
.join-password input, .invite .row input, .spectate-box input {
  width: 100%; min-height: 2.15rem;
  background: var(--bg-sunken); color: var(--fg); border: 1px solid var(--line-bright);
  border-radius: var(--radius); padding: 0.45rem 0.65rem; font: inherit;
}
.join-password { max-width: 22rem; margin: 0 0 1rem; }
/* The seats: as many across as fit, one column on a phone. */
.seat-cards {
  list-style: none; margin: 0 0 1rem; padding: 0;
  display: grid; gap: 0.65rem; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(10.5rem, 1fr));
}
.open-table button.primary.join { display: block; margin: 0 0 1rem; }
.invite {
  background: var(--bg-raised); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px;
  padding: 0.85rem 1rem; margin: 0 0 1rem;
}
/* The panel's caption, which `.setup h3` would otherwise draw as a heading. */
.invite h3.caption {
  font-family: var(--mono); font-weight: 400; font-size: 10.5px;
  letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--fg-faint); margin: 0;
}
/* A whole URL in a row: the input may shrink below its content (`min-width: 0`)
 * and the button drops under it rather than off the edge (live review I-1). */
.invite .row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.5rem; margin-top: 0.5rem; }
.invite .row input { flex: 1 1 14rem; min-width: 0; }
.invite .note { color: var(--fg-faint); font-size: 11.5px; margin: 0.55rem 0 0; }
.open-table .open-table-controls { display: flex; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1rem; margin-top: 0.4rem; }
/* Abandon, the quieter danger (mock 08): outlined in the warning colour. */
.open-table .open-table-controls button.ghost.danger {
  color: var(--warn); border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--warn) 45%, transparent);
}
/* The unlock face and the lock screen: one card, one action. */
.spectate-box {
  display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-end; gap: 0.75rem;
  background: var(--bg-raised); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px;
  padding: 0.85rem 1rem; margin: 0 0 1rem;
}
.spectate-box .form-field { flex: 1 1 14rem; margin: 0; }
.unlock .title-row { display: flex; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.6rem; }
.notice-card {
  max-width: 35rem; margin: 0 auto;
  background: var(--bg-raised); border: 1px solid var(--line-bright); border-radius: 8px;
  padding: 1.1rem 1.4rem;
}
.notice-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1rem; margin-top: 0.9rem; }
@media (max-width: 480px) {
  .setup h3.page-title { font-size: 1.5rem; }
  .seat-cards { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
  .open-table button.primary.join, .spectate-box button.primary { width: 100%; }
  .open-table button.primary.join, .seat-cards button.sit, .spectate-box button.primary,
  .join-password input, .invite .row input, .spectate-box input { min-height: 2.75rem; }
}
```

4. the screen for a save that no longer rebuilds (`App.tsx:1427-1429`), local by construction.

Under `VITE_MULTIPLAYER=false` each leads to the DOOR, where this browser's games are listed, and says "On this
device", the local screens' own crumb (mock 07). A build that serves a lobby keeps all four exactly as they are:
the spec's rule is about the single-player build, and the cells that press "Lobby" on these screens today
(`App.test.tsx:3648` among them) are the anti-vacuity partners.

**Why Remove on a foreign row is not the cross-rev Remove** (spec §2.4: "the plan confirms Remove and export work on a
table the module refuses to open"):
- **Export works because it reads documents and never rebuilds.** `BackUpOne` → `backupOne` → `localPair` + `readPair`
  (`backup.ts:317-327`). "Save game file" → `recordText` → `localPair` (`api.ts:769-785`). The Worker's `pair` arm
  reads the module's store and IndexedDB, and `live_handle` is never reached.
- **Remove cannot be `forgetUnplayable`**, whose unfenced IndexedDB delete (`backup.ts:503-511`) is right for a
  cross-rev row. That row is this browser's own compatibility NOTE, read straight from IndexedDB (`listUnplayable`). A
  foreign row is the module's LISTING: every tab's Worker loaded the pair at its boot (`worker.ts:151-165`), so deleting
  the stored pair behind the Worker's back would leave the row listed until the next rebuild.
- **So it takes the module's own delete, which works on a game `live_handle` refuses.** The layer's `delete` reads the
  table and the record's event count and never rebuilds (`tables.rs:1664-1700`; spec §2.4). The Worker commits a
  delete only for a game this tab HOLDS (`worker.ts:195-217`, the `deletePair` generation fence), so the hold comes
  first and is given back after: P-6's own reason for keeping Abandon on a game's screen, met here by taking the hold.
- **Task 4 owns the layer half of this confirmation**: a `DELETE` on a not-over foreign game answers 204 through
  `api::dispatch` (its "every game route refuses" list must not include `delete`). This task's cells prove the page
  takes that path and not the database shortcut.

```tsx
            {/* **NOT `local`, deliberately** (spec §4: "Abandon still works"):
                `local` means "send this game to the archive first", and the
                archive would refuse a save that no longer rebuilds. A server
                table's own delete archives it (R-6.5a.11). */}
            {mayAbandon && (
              <Abandon
                table={broken.table}
                onDone={() => (local ? toDoor() : toLobby())}
                onError={setError}
              />
            )}
            <button
              type="button"
              className="ghost"
              onClick={() => (local ? leave(localExit.to) : toLobby())}
            >
              {local ? localExit.label : "Lobby"}
            </button>
          </div>
          {error && <Refusal sentence={error} />}
        </div>
      );
    }
```

```ts
// ---- a game the MODULE refuses to open (M6.5c2, spec §2.4) ----------------
//
// **Remove takes the module's fenced delete, never this database directly.** A
// cross-rev row is this browser's own compatibility note and `forgetUnplayable`
// removes it straight from IndexedDB; a foreign row is the module's LISTING,
// loaded into every tab's Worker at its boot, so a delete behind the Worker's
// back would leave the row listed. The layer's delete never rebuilds (it reads
// the table and the record's event count), which is why it works on a game
// `live_handle` refuses; the Worker commits it only for a game this tab holds.

      .posted.map((p) => (p.kind === "call" ? `${p.method} ${p.path}` : p.kind))
      .filter((s) => s === "hold" || s === "release" || s.startsWith("DELETE"));

    expect(steps()).toEqual(["hold", `DELETE /api/games/${ID}`, "release"]);
  });
```

  In `web/src/backup.ts`, add `hold` and `release` to the `./local/client` import (`:47`),
  `import { api } from "./api";`, and directly below `forgetUnplayable` (`:503-511`):

```ts
/**
 * Remove a game the MODULE refuses to open — not over, dealt a bot this build
 * does not run (M6.5c2, spec §2.4) — through the module's own FENCED delete.
 *
 * **Not [`forgetUnplayable`]'s unfenced path, and the difference is where the
 * row comes from.** A cross-rev row is this browser's own compatibility note,
 * read straight from IndexedDB; a foreign row is the module's LISTING — every
 * tab's Worker loaded the pair at its boot — so deleting the stored pair behind
 * the Worker's back would leave the row listed until the next rebuild. The
 * layer's `delete` reads the table and the record's event count and never
 * rebuilds (spec §2.4), which is why it works on a game `live_handle` refuses;
 * the Worker commits a delete only for a game this tab HOLDS, so the hold comes
 * first and is given back after — on every way out.
 */
export async function removeForeign(id: string): Promise<void> {
  if (!(await hold(id))) {
    throw new Error("this game is open in another tab — close it there, then remove it");
  }
  try {
    await api.remove(id);
  } finally {
    await release(id);
  }
}
```

  - `Unplayable` (`:300-345`) becomes:

```tsx
export function Unplayable({
  reload = 0,
  foreign = [],
  onRemoved,
}: {
  reload?: number;
  /** Games the LISTING says this build's bot cannot continue (M6.5c2, spec
   *  §2.4): not over, dealt a bot this build does not run. Listed beside the
   *  cross-rev rows, the pattern R-6.5b2.12 set, and removed through the
   *  module's own fenced delete ([`removeForeign`]) — their row is the
   *  module's listing, not a note in this browser's database. */
  foreign?: readonly TableView[];
  /** A foreign row was removed: the host re-reads its listing. */
  onRemoved?: () => void;
}): React.ReactNode {
  const [rows, setRows] = useState<UnplayableGame[] | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  /** A Remove that did not happen — said under the list, not in place of it:
   *  the rows are still there, and the reason is about one of them. */
  const [removeError, setRemoveError] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const read = useCallback(() => {
    listUnplayable().then(setRows, (e: unknown) => setError(sentenceOf(e)));
  }, []);
  useEffect(() => read(), [read, reload]);

  const forget = async (id: string) => {
    try {
      await forgetUnplayable(id);
      read();
    } catch (e) {
      setError(sentenceOf(e));
    }
  };
  const removeRefused = async (id: string) => {
    setRemoveError(null);
    try {
      await removeForeign(id);
      onRemoved?.();
    } catch (e) {
      setRemoveError(sentenceOf(e));
    }
  };

  // **Wrapped, not the bare exception** (review M-10).
  if (error !== null)
    return <p className="error">the games that will not open could not be read &mdash; {error}</p>;
  const cross = rows ?? [];
  if (cross.length === 0 && foreign.length === 0) return null;
  return (
    <div className="unplayable">
      <h4>Will not open here</h4>
      <ul>
        {foreign.map((t) => (
          <li key={t.id}>
            <span className="restore-id">{t.name ?? t.id}</span>{" "}
            <span className="meta">{foreignWords(t)}</span> <BackUpOne id={t.id} />
            <Forget id={t.id} onForget={removeRefused} />
          </li>
        ))}
        {cross.map((g) => (
          <li key={g.id}>
            <span className="restore-id">{g.id}</span>{" "}
            <span className="meta">
              {g.note.reason ||
                (g.note.semantics_rev === null
                  ? "this build does not read it"
                  : `saved at semantics rev ${g.note.semantics_rev}`)}
            </span>{" "}
            <BackUpOne id={g.id} />
            <Forget id={g.id} onForget={forget} />
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      {removeError !== null && <p className="error">{removeError}</p>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: The probe.** In `web/src/api.ts`, `bounded` (`:285-294`) becomes:

```ts
/** `p`, or a rejection once `ms` has passed.
 *
 *  A race rather than a catch, for the reason [`BOUND_MS`] gives. **The timer
 *  is cleared the moment `p` settles** (M6.5c2): the signal's probe is bounded
 *  too, inside a hook whose cells count what is left armed, and a bound whose
 *  timer outlived its read would stand there as a rung nobody scheduled. */
export const bounded = <T,>(p: Promise<T>, ms: number): Promise<T> =>
  new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error("timed out")), ms);
    p.then(
      (v) => {
        clearTimeout(timer);
        resolve(v);
      },
      (e: unknown) => {
        clearTimeout(timer);
        reject(e);
      },
    );
  });
```

```ts
// ---- M6.5c2: the record's `run` through every browser save path (spec §2.4) --
//
// **Every save names what produced it** (R-6.5c2.10): the record's `run` block
// — which bot sat where, at which version and knobs, with its stream seed —
// and since M6.5c2 the host it was played on (`run.run_id`, stamped by the
// module: Task 5's pin). This is the PAGE's half: the three places a browser
// keeps or hands over a record — this database, "Save game file" and the
// backup envelope — carry `run` byte for byte. They can, because nothing on
// the page parses a record (`backup.ts`'s header); these cells are what says
// so for `run` in particular, whose two u64s a JavaScript number rounds.
describe("the record's run block through every save path", () => {
  /** The committed record's `run` block, as text — `run` is its last key. */
  const RUN = RECORD_TEXT.slice(RECORD_TEXT.indexOf('"run": {'), RECORD_TEXT.lastIndexOf("\n}"));

  it("is the premise: a run block whose two u64s no JavaScript number holds", () => {
    expect(RUN).toContain('"agent_seed": 10851594032870736878');
    expect(RUN).toContain('"weights": 6957643967275421640');
    expect(String(Number("10851594032870736878"))).not.toBe("10851594032870736878");
    // So a parse and a re-serialize on ANY path would change the bytes.
    expect(JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(RECORD_TEXT), null, 2)).not.toBe(RECORD_TEXT);
  });

  it("survives this browser's database byte for byte", async () => {
    await putPair("local-run", RECORD_TEXT, tableFor("local-run"));
    const back = await readBack("local-run");
    expect(back.record).toBe(RECORD_TEXT);
    expect(back.record).toContain(RUN);
  });

  // "Save game file" hands `api.recordText`'s string to a Blob untouched
  // (`App.tsx`'s `saveGameFile`; `App.test.tsx`'s local Save game file cell
  // reads the Blob back). This is the string's own source.
  it("survives Save game file: the text the download is made of is the stored text", async () => {
    await putPair("local-run", RECORD_TEXT, tableFor("local-run"));
    expect(await api.recordText("local-run")).toBe(RECORD_TEXT);
  });

  it("survives a backup and a restore onto a fresh device, byte for byte", async () => {
    await putPair("local-run", RECORD_TEXT, tableFor("local-run"));
    const envelope = await backupOne("local-run");
    // The envelope carries the record as a JSON STRING: parsing the FILE hands
    // back the record's exact text, never a parsed record.
    expect((JSON.parse(envelope) as Envelope).games[0]!.record).toBe(RECORD_TEXT);
    // A fresh device: a new database, and a new Worker.
    globalThis.indexedDB = new IDBFactory();
    resetLocalHostForTests();
    stubWorker();
    await restorePairs(envelope);
    const back = await readBack("local-run");
    expect(back.record).toBe(RECORD_TEXT);
    expect(back.record).toContain(RUN);
  });
});
```

**Why the objects read the door's OWN header** (the spec: the shell "forwards the caller's claimed name as
`X-Yokohama-Claimed-User`"):
- An object hands the module a raw `user` string, and the module's `identity_of` puts it under the header the door's
  mode reads. So the header between the shell and an object is the shell's own convention.
- Reading it by door (`forwardedCaller`) buys one thing: if the Worker and an object ever disagreed about the door,
  a claim would reach NO caller, rather than be read by the `worker` mode as a verified identity.
- Every client `x-yokohama-*` header is still stripped, so the objects receive only the header the Worker set.

```rust
        let r = identity_inner(None);

    /// last accepted one set stands. Mutants: a default door; any other string

        assert_eq!(err, r#"YOKOHAMA_WEB_IDENTITY must be worker or open — got "cf-access""#);

        assert!(err.contains("YOKOHAMA_WEB_ARCHIVE"), "{err}");
        let r = dispatch_inner(Some("ben"), "GET", "/api/me", "", None, b"");
        assert_eq!(r.body, r#"{"mode":"open","user":"ben"}"#, "every refused init changed nothing");
    }

    /// Spec §2.1 rule 4, at BOTH doors: a value no header can carry never
    /// reaches `resolve` as itself. Its TRIM is judged as a header carrying it
    /// would be — by `resolve`, in the door's mode, so the mode rule keeps ONE
    /// site — and a control character no trim removes is the key grammar's

        let absent = identity_inner(None);

            assert_eq!((r.status, r.body.as_str()), (401, want.as_str()), "{door}");
```
