```rust
//! **`init`'s configuration** (spec §2.2, §3.1): the JSON the shell builds from
//! the Worker's variables, parsed and refused HERE — so a bad VALUE is refused
//! at `init` naming its variable, the Worker's form of the NAS refusing to
//! start. A configuration of the wrong SHAPE names no variable: JSON that is
//! not an OBJECT is refused in this crate's own sentence, which names the six
//! keys ([`parse`]); text that is not JSON, an object with a key it does not
//! have or MISSING the door, and a value of the wrong JSON type, such as
//! `{"chat_keep": 500}` for the string `"500"`, in serde's words. The shell
//! always builds the object, with every value a string or `null`
//! (`worker/src/config.ts`'s `moduleConfig`, whose `shellConfig` refuses a
//! variable that is not a string, and a door that is not named, first: the
//! orchestrator's ruling E3; M6.5c2, spec §2.1), so no deployment reaches those.

use serde::Deserialize;
use yokohama_web::chat::ChatConfig;
use yokohama_web::identity::{IdentityMode, User};

/// The door's variable (M6.5c2, spec §2.1; R-6.5c2.5): `worker` or `open`,
/// with no default.
pub(crate) const IDENTITY_VAR: &str = "YOKOHAMA_WEB_IDENTITY";

/// The archive switch's variable (spec §3.1): `r2` or `off`.
pub(crate) const ARCHIVE_VAR: &str = "YOKOHAMA_WEB_ARCHIVE";

/// The six keys the shell sends, and no others: an unknown key is a
/// misspelling in the shell, refused rather than ignored, and a missing
/// `identity` is refused too — the door has no default. Read ONLY from the
/// object form ([`parse`]).
#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct InitConfig {
    /// The door (M6.5c2, spec §2.1), as `shellConfig` read it.
    identity: String,
    archive: String,
    /// The Archive object's address (spec §2.6), and `null` on every other
    /// object. Read only under `r2`, where it is the receipt archive's
    /// caller.
    caller: Option<String>,
    // The three chat variables, raw — `null` for a variable the Worker does not
    // set, which the layer's parser reads as its default.
    lobby_chat: Option<String>,
    chat_keep: Option<String>,
    chat_text: Option<String>,
}

/// What `init` builds the layer with.
pub(crate) struct Config {
    pub(crate) door: Door,
    pub(crate) chat: ChatConfig,
    pub(crate) archive: Switch,
}

/// Which door this Worker has (M6.5c2, spec §2.1; R-6.5c2.5), fixed at `init`
/// with the rest of the configuration: every object builds its module from its
/// OWN configuration, so one deployment is one door everywhere. Two names move
/// with it (review R2.2-m2): the layer's mode a caller is resolved under
/// ([`Door::mode`]), and the door's name on the wire ([`Door::wire_name`]).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Door {
    /// Cloudflare Access, verified by the shell, which hands the objects the
    /// caller it verified — a person's assertion, or the dev door's claim under
    /// the credential. This repository's configuration.
    Worker,
    /// No identity service (R-6.5c2.3): the name a caller claims is who they
    /// are. The shell holds a claim only to what a header can carry; the
    /// layer's key grammar judges the rest.
    Open,
}

impl Door {
    /// The layer's identity mode for this door.
    pub(crate) fn mode(self) -> IdentityMode {
        match self {
            Self::Worker => IdentityMode::Worker,
            Self::Open => IdentityMode::Open,
        }
    }

    /// The door's name on the wire — `/api/me`'s `mode`, `/api/health`'s
    /// `identity` — in the layer's own words: `cf-access` under `worker`,
    /// because the door a client is behind is Cloudflare Access (the name
    /// `web/src/types.ts` and the client's `useIdentityMode` have read since
    /// M6.5c), and `open` under `open`.
    pub(crate) fn wire_name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Worker => IdentityMode::CfAccess.name(),
            Self::Open => IdentityMode::Open.name(),
        }
    }
}

/// The archive switch (spec §2.6).
pub(crate) enum Switch {
    /// `off`: `NoArchive`, and every path takes the layer's own off-branch.
    Off,
    /// `r2`: the receipt archive, with the Archive object's address — the
    /// caller whose saves this instance files — or `None` on any other object.
    R2 { caller: Option<String> },
}

/// The configuration `init` builds the layer with.
///
/// **The door first** (M6.5c2, spec §2.1): exactly `worker` or `open`, refused
/// naming its variable otherwise.
///
/// The chat values go through the layer's own `ChatConfig::from_env_values`,
/// whose refusals already name their variables — the NAS's names, parser and
/// defaults, never a copy.
///
/// **Under `r2` the caller is NORMALIZED by the layer's own `User::parse`**,
/// the parse that normalizes every sender, and refused if it is no key. The
/// receipt archive reads it whole for spec §2.6's `test/` root, which must read
/// `Red@T.TEST` as the `red@t.test` a sender of that name normalizes to. Under
/// `off` nothing reads it, and it is not checked.
///
/// **The object form only** (R1's L-3): serde's derived `Deserialize` also
/// reads a struct from a positional ARRAY, a form `deny_unknown_fields` does
/// not govern, so anything but an object is refused before serde reads it —
/// the rule this crate keeps for a create body, the picker row and a
/// receipt's outcome. The refusal echoes nothing, since the configuration
/// carries the Archive object's address.
pub(crate) fn parse(config: &str) -> Result<Config, String> {
    let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(config)
        .map_err(|e| format!("the module's init configuration does not parse: {e}"))?;
    if !value.is_object() {
        return Err("the module's init configuration is the object of its six keys — \
                    identity, archive, caller, lobby_chat, chat_keep and chat_text"
            .to_string());
    }
    let c: InitConfig = serde_json::from_value(value)
        .map_err(|e| format!("the module's init configuration does not parse: {e}"))?;
    let door = match c.identity.as_str() {
        "worker" => Door::Worker,
        "open" => Door::Open,
        v => return Err(format!("{IDENTITY_VAR} must be worker or open — got {v:?}")),
    };
    let archive = match c.archive.as_str() {
        "off" => Switch::Off,
        "r2" => Switch::R2 { caller: c.caller.as_deref().map(normalized).transpose()? },
        v => return Err(format!("{ARCHIVE_VAR} must be r2 or off — got {v:?}")),
    };
    let chat =
        ChatConfig::from_env_values(c.lobby_chat.as_deref(), c.chat_keep.as_deref(), c.chat_text.as_deref())?;
    Ok(Config { door, chat, archive })
}

/// The archive caller as the layer normalizes an address.
fn normalized(raw: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    User::parse(raw)
        .map(|user| user.as_str().to_string())
        .map_err(|e| format!("the archive's caller must be an address: {e}"))
}
```

```rust
/// Who the caller is, by the door's ONE header (spec §2.3; M6.5c2, spec §2.1):
/// the value the shell hands over goes into a header map under the header the
/// door's mode reads — `X-Yokohama-User` under `worker`,
/// `X-Yokohama-Claimed-User` under `open` — and is read by the layer's own
/// `identity::resolve` in that mode, with its key grammar and its mode rule:
/// under `worker` an identity must have the email shape and a plain name
/// reads as absent; under `open` any key the grammar accepts is a caller.
/// `anonymous`, like an absent or blank value, is no caller, and a refusal is
/// the layer's own sentence.
///
/// A value no header can carry — a control character other than a tab —
/// never reaches `resolve` as itself (spec §2.1 rule 4). Its TRIM is judged as
/// a header carrying it would be, by `resolve` in the same mode, so the mode
/// rule keeps ONE site; a value no trim makes carriable holds a control
/// character inside it, which the key grammar refuses (`User::parse`'s
/// sentence). The shell never forwards such a value (`address` in
/// `worker/src/identity.ts`); the cells keep this path in step.
pub fn identity_of(user: Option<&str>) -> Result<User, String> {
    let mode = door().mode();
    let mut headers = http::HeaderMap::new();
    if let Some(raw) = user {
        let value = match http::HeaderValue::from_str(raw) {
            Ok(value) => value,
            Err(_) => match http::HeaderValue::from_str(raw.trim()) {
                Ok(trimmed) => trimmed,
                Err(_) => return User::parse(raw),
            },
        };
        headers.insert(mode.header(), value);
    }
    resolve(mode, &headers)
}
```

```ts
/** An `Env` with `vars` set and, when asked, the bucket bound — at the WORKER
```

```ts
 * trimmed, then matched exactly. `cf-access` is the NAS's door, not this
 * host's: here the shell verifies Access itself, which is `worker`.

function door(raw: string | null): Door {
  const value = raw === null ? null : raw.trim();
  if (value === "worker" || value === "open") return value;
  return refuse(
    value === null
      ? "YOKOHAMA_WEB_IDENTITY must be worker or open — it is not set, and there is no default: a door is a deployment decision"
```

```ts
/**
 * **An open-door claim** (M6.5c2, spec §2.1): the raw name a caller sent —
 * `handle` picks the carrier, the header on a `fetch` and the `claimed`
 * parameter on an upgrade — judged by `address`: RAW by `forwardable` first,
 * so a percent-decoded parameter holding a character no header can carry is
 * no caller, rather than a `headers.set` that throws into the platform's plain
 * 500 (review R2.2-m3); then trimmed and ASCII-lowercased (the Kelvin lesson).
 * The shell never judges a name beyond what a header can carry: the layer's
 * key grammar does, in the objects. A blank or absent claim is no one.
 *
 * Space runs are NOT collapsed here — that is the key grammar's, and there is
 * one. So a hand-typed `ben   castle` names the Archive object
 * `archive:ben   castle` where the client's own `ben castle` names another; the
 * two hold nothing of their own and file under one key, because the module
 * normalizes both, so the only cost is a second object.
 */
export function claimedIdentity(raw: string | null): Identity {
  const name = raw === null ? undefined : address(raw);
  return name === undefined ? { kind: "none" } : { kind: "claimed", name };
}

/** The value an identity is forwarded as, and names its archive object by —
 *  a person's or the dev door's address, or an open-door claim — or
 *  `undefined` for no one (M6.5c2). */
export function callerName(identity: Identity): string | undefined {
  switch (identity.kind) {
    case "person":
    case "dev":
      return identity.email;
    case "claimed":
      return identity.name;
    case "none":
      return undefined;
  }
}
```

```ts
import { cloudflareTest } from "@cloudflare/vitest-plugin";
import { configDefaults, defineConfig } from "vitest/config";

// **The POOL** (spec §5.2): Cloudflare's Workers Vitest integration,
// `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin` 1.2.3, whose entry is the `cloudflareTest()`
// Vite plugin. Every cell runs INSIDE workerd, against the Worker a pool
// configuration describes — never `wrangler.jsonc`, which is production's.
//
// **Two projects, one per door** (M6.5c2, spec §2.1; review R2.2-M2). Every
// object builds its configuration from its OWN constructor's `env` — the
// configuration file's — so a cell's env override at `handle` moves the
// Worker's door and never an object's, and one project cannot prove both:
// - `worker`, over `wrangler.test.jsonc` (`YOKOHAMA_WEB_IDENTITY=worker`,
//   production's door): every `test/**/*.test.ts` but `test/open/`;
// - `open`, over `wrangler.open.test.jsonc` (`YOKOHAMA_WEB_IDENTITY=open`):
//   `test/open/**/*.test.ts`.
// Each project runs its own workerd, with its own storage and bucket: pool
// fact 5 holds per project as it holds per file. `npm test` runs both, and
// `npx vitest run --project open` one. Vitest 4 removed the workspace file, so
// a workspace IS `test.projects` (measured with vitest 4.1.11).
//
// It runs over the BUILT module under `gen/` and rebuilds nothing: after a
// change to `crates/yokohama-worker`, `npm run build:module:debug` comes FIRST,
// or the pool tests the module as it was. The debug build is the one the pool
// needs — its trap cells call `debug_trap`, which a release build does not
// export.
//
// `npm run test:scripts` (`vitest.scripts.config.ts`) runs the node half; the
// globs do not overlap (the orchestrator's ruling I-31).
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    projects: [
      {
        plugins: [cloudflareTest({ wrangler: { configPath: "./wrangler.test.jsonc" } })],
        test: { name: "worker", include: ["test/**/*.test.ts"], exclude: [...configDefaults.exclude, "test/open/**"] },
      },
      {
        plugins: [cloudflareTest({ wrangler: { configPath: "./wrangler.open.test.jsonc" } })],
        test: { name: "open", include: ["test/open/**/*.test.ts"] },
      },
    ],
  },
});
```

`worker/test/open/door.test.ts`, new. It holds Task 17's cells; Task 18 adds a describe to it.

```ts
import { createExecutionContext, runInDurableObject } from "cloudflare:test";
import { env } from "cloudflare:workers";
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import compiled from "../../gen/yokohama_worker_bg.wasm";
import { createModule } from "../../gen/factory.js";
import { Archive } from "../../src/archive";
import * as configModule from "../../src/config";
import type { Env } from "../../src/env";
import { House } from "../../src/house";
import type { KeySource } from "../../src/identity";
import { handle } from "../../src/index";
import { readReply } from "../../src/module";
import { HOUSE_NAME } from "../../src/slot";
import { Table } from "../../src/table";
import { settle, tableStub } from "../helpers";

// **The open door, end to end** (M6.5c2, spec §2.1; R-6.5c2.3, R-6.5c2.5) —
// the pool's `open` project, over `wrangler.open.test.jsonc`. The Worker and
// every object read `YOKOHAMA_WEB_IDENTITY=open` from their OWN configuration,
// which is why this is a project and not a cell's env override (review
// R2.2-M2). Every request goes through `handle`, as the Worker's own `fetch`
// does, so what reaches an object is what the door forwards.
//
// Storage, the house and the bucket are per FILE and per project (pool fact
// 5): every cell uses ids and names of its own.

const ORIGIN = "https://yokohama.test";
const JSON_TYPE = { "content-type": "application/json" };
const UPGRADE = { Upgrade: "websocket" };

/** How long a cell waits for a message it EXPECTS (the orchestrator's ruling
 *  R-10: nothing waits out a timer to show that something did not arrive). */
const WAIT_MS = 2_000;

/** A key source that fails the request that asks it: under the open door the
 *  Worker reads no Access assertion, so no key is ever wanted. */
const NO_KEYS: KeySource = async () => {
  throw new Error("the open door asked for Access's keys");
};

interface Sent {
  method?: string;
  headers?: Record<string, string>;
  body?: BodyInit | null;
  /** The claimed name, as `X-Yokohama-Claimed-User`: a fetch's carrier. */
  claim?: string;
  env?: Env;
  keys?: KeySource;
}

interface Answer {
  status: number;
  text: string;
  webSocket: WebSocket | null;
}

/** One request through the Worker's `handle`, answered whole. An upgrade's
 *  socket is handed back unread. */
async function through(path: string, sent: Sent = {}): Promise<Answer> {
  const headers = new Headers(sent.headers);
  if (sent.claim !== undefined) headers.set("X-Yokohama-Claimed-User", sent.claim);
  const req = new Request(ORIGIN + path, { method: sent.method ?? "GET", headers, body: sent.body ?? null });
  const res = await handle(req, sent.env ?? env, createExecutionContext(), sent.keys ?? NO_KEYS);
  const webSocket = res.webSocket;
  return { status: res.status, text: webSocket ? "" : await res.text(), webSocket };
}

/** `path` with `name` as the upgrade's `claimed` parameter, encoded as the
 *  client encodes it (`URLSearchParams`, `web/src/ws.ts`). */
function claimedAt(path: string, name: string): string {
  const url = new URL(path, ORIGIN);
  url.searchParams.set("claimed", name);
  return url.pathname + url.search;
}

/** A socket through the Worker, accepted, with every message kept. */
async function socket(res: Answer): Promise<{ ws: WebSocket; until(n: number): Promise<string[]> }> {
  const ws = res.webSocket;
  if (ws === null) throw new Error(`the upgrade was answered ${res.status}, unupgraded: ${res.text}`);
  ws.accept();
  const messages: string[] = [];
  const waiting = new Set<() => void>();
  ws.addEventListener("message", (e) => {
    messages.push(typeof e.data === "string" ? e.data : "<binary>");
    for (const w of [...waiting]) w();
  });
  return {
    ws,
    until: (n) =>
      new Promise<string[]>((resolve, reject) => {
        const check = () => {
          if (messages.length < n) return;
          clearTimeout(timer);
          waiting.delete(check);
          resolve([...messages]);
        };
        const timer = setTimeout(() => {
          waiting.delete(check);
          reject(new Error(`${n} messages awaited; arrived: ${JSON.stringify(messages)}`));
        }, WAIT_MS);
        waiting.add(check);
        check();
      }),
  };
}

/** Which objects `f`'s requests reached, and what each was handed: a spy on
 *  each class's `fetch`, on the PROTOTYPE (pool fact 1), calling through. */
async function reaching<T>(f: () => Promise<T>): Promise<{ result: T; table: Request[]; house: Request[]; archive: Request[] }> {
  const table = vi.spyOn(Table.prototype, "fetch");
  const house = vi.spyOn(House.prototype, "fetch");
  const archive = vi.spyOn(Archive.prototype, "fetch");
  try {
    const result = await f();
    return {
      result,
      table: table.mock.calls.map(([r]) => r),
      house: house.mock.calls.map(([r]) => r),
      archive: archive.mock.calls.map(([r]) => r),
    };
  } finally {
    table.mockRestore();
    house.mockRestore();
    archive.mockRestore();
  }
}

/** The `x-yokohama-*` headers an object was handed: the names it trusts. */
function yokohamaHeaders(req: Request): Record<string, string> {
  return Object.fromEntries([...req.headers].filter(([name]) => name.startsWith("x-yokohama-")));
}

/** The layer's own answer to no caller at this door: a fresh module in this
 *  project's configuration, asked `identity` with none. */
function noCaller(): string {
  const mod = createModule(compiled);
  mod.init(configModule.moduleConfig(env, null));
  return readReply(mod.identity(undefined)).body;
}

describe("the open door (M6.5c2, spec §2.1)", () => {
  // Mutants: the claim not read (user null); the claim forwarded as
  // `X-Yokohama-User`, which an open object does not read (user null, and the
  // headers show it); an assertion read at the open door (a key asked for);
  // a forged `x-yokohama-*` header let through.
  it("a claim by the header on a fetch is the caller, with no assertion read; the objects are handed it under its own name", async () => {
    const asked: boolean[] = [];
    const keys: KeySource = async (refresh) => {
      asked.push(refresh);
      throw new Error("the open door asked for Access's keys");
    };
    const forged = { "x-yokohama-user": "evil@x.test", "x-yokohama-operator": "evil@x.test", "x-yokohama-future": "evil@x.test" };
    const me = await reaching(() =>
      through("/api/me", { claim: "  Ben ", headers: { ...forged, "Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion": "a.b.c" }, keys }),
    );
    expect(me.result.text).toBe('{"mode":"open","user":"ben"}');
    expect(me.house.map(yokohamaHeaders), "the claim under its own name, and nothing forged").toEqual([
      { "x-yokohama-claimed-user": "ben" },
    ]);
    expect(asked, "no key asked for: the open door reads no assertion").toEqual([]);
    expect((await through("/api/me")).text, "no claim: no one").toBe('{"mode":"open","user":null}');
    expect((JSON.parse((await through("/api/health")).text) as { identity: string }).identity).toBe("open");
  });

  // **(Review Focus 1)** An address with a `+` and a name with a space, carried
  // on the upgrade as the client carries them: `URLSearchParams` encodes the
  // parameter (`web/src/ws.ts`, whose own cell pins the client's half), and
  // the Worker reads it back decoded. The socket's caller is exactly the
  // fetch caller: at a PLAYING table each socket's first frame IS that
  // caller's own `…/events` reading — seat 0 is to move and seat 1 is not, so
  // the two readings differ and each socket is told apart by the frame it is
  // sent. Mutants: the parameter read raw off `url.search` (`a%2Bb%40x.test`,
  // which is no caller); decoded with `decodeURIComponent` (`ben+castle`, which
  // the key grammar refuses); a `+` turned into a space (`a b@x.test`, no
  // caller); the parameter never read (the upgrade answered 401).
  it("(Review Focus 1) a + in an address and a space in a name reach a table's socket exactly as the fetch caller", async () => {
    const id = "rf1-open";
    const [plus, spaced] = ["a+b@x.test", "ben castle"];
    const create = {
      id,
      players: 2,
      colors: ["Red", "Blue"],
      start_seat: 0,
      seed: 20260831,
      seats: [{ user: plus }, { user: spaced }],
    };
    const created = await through("/api/games", { method: "POST", claim: plus, headers: JSON_TYPE, body: JSON.stringify(create) });
    expect(created.status, created.text).toBe(201);
    for (const [who, seat] of [
      [plus, 0],
      [spaced, 1],
    ] as const) {
      const kept = await through(`/api/games/${id}/keep`, { method: "POST", claim: who, headers: JSON_TYPE, body: JSON.stringify({ seat, card: 1 }) });
      expect(kept.status, `${who} keeps: ${kept.text}`).toBe(200);
    }
    const reading = async (who: string) => {
      const res = await through(`/api/games/${id}/events`, { claim: who });
      expect(res.status, `${who}: ${res.text}`).toBe(200);
      return res.text;
    };
    const readings = { [plus]: await reading(plus), [spaced]: await reading(spaced) };
    expect(readings[plus], "premise: seat 0 is to move and seat 1 is not, so the two readings differ").not.toBe(readings[spaced]);
    for (const [who, query] of [
      [plus, "?claimed=a%2Bb%40x.test"],
      [spaced, "?claimed=ben+castle"],
    ] as const) {
      const path = claimedAt(`/api/games/${id}/stream`, who);
      expect(path.endsWith(query), `premise: the client's own encoding — ${path}`).toBe(true);
      const tab = await socket(await through(path, { headers: UPGRADE }));
      expect(await tab.until(1), who).toEqual([`{"event":"signal","data":${readings[who]}}`]);
      tab.ws.close(1000, "done");
    }
    await settle(tableStub(id));
  });

  // Review R2.2-m3: the parameter is percent-DECODED, so it can hold any
  // character — and `headers.set` THROWS on a value a header cannot carry,
  // which, before any `try` in `handle`, would be the platform's plain 500.
  // Judged RAW first (`claimedIdentity`), such a claim is no caller, and the
  // house answers as the layer answers no one. Mutants: the claim forwarded
  // unjudged (the call rejects, or an identity header reaches the house);
  // normalized before it is judged (`Kevin` becomes the caller `kevin`).
  it("a claimed parameter no header can carry is no caller — the layer's own answer, never a platform 500", async () => {
    const body = noCaller();
    for (const raw of ["Kevin", " ben", "ben\r", "ben\u0000", "rené"]) {
      const res = await reaching(() => through(claimedAt("/api/stream", raw), { headers: UPGRADE }));
      expect([res.result.status, res.result.webSocket, res.result.text], JSON.stringify(raw)).toEqual([401, null, body]);
      expect(res.house.map(yokohamaHeaders), `${JSON.stringify(raw)}: no identity header`).toEqual([{}]);
    }
    // The anti-vacuity partner: a name a header CAN carry is admitted, as itself.
    const tab = await socket(await through(claimedAt("/api/stream", "kevin"), { headers: UPGRADE }));
    const attached = await runInDurableObject(env.HOUSE.get(env.HOUSE.idFromName(HOUSE_NAME)), (_o, state) =>
      state.getWebSockets("lobby").map((ws) => ws.deserializeAttachment() as { user?: string }),
    );
    expect(attached).toContainEqual({ user: "kevin" });
    tab.ws.close(1000, "done");
  });

  // Spec §2.1: "on upgrades only". ONE carrier per request kind, as R-1.2 has
  // each mode read one header. Mutants: the parameter read on a fetch; the
  // header read on an upgrade.
  it("the claim rides ONE carrier per request: the header on a fetch, the parameter on an upgrade", async () => {
    expect((await through("/api/me", { claim: "ben" })).text).toBe('{"mode":"open","user":"ben"}');
    const tab = await socket(await through(claimedAt("/api/stream", "ben"), { headers: UPGRADE }));
    tab.ws.close(1000, "done");
    expect((await through("/api/me?claimed=ben")).text, "a fetch's parameter is no claim").toBe('{"mode":"open","user":null}');
    const refused = await through("/api/stream", { claim: "ben", headers: UPGRADE });
    expect([refused.status, refused.webSocket], "an upgrade's header is no claim").toEqual([401, null]);
  });
});
```

```ts
/**
 * The caller an object was handed (the plan's internal headers; M6.5c2, spec
 * §2.1): the ONE header its door names, and no other — `X-Yokohama-User`, a
 * caller the Worker verified, under `worker`; `X-Yokohama-Claimed-User`, a name
 * a caller claimed, under `open`. The Worker strips every client
 * `x-yokohama-*` header and sets its door's alone, so the two agree while the
 * Worker and the object read one configuration — and were they ever to
 * disagree, a claim would reach no caller rather than pass as a verified one.
 * With a configuration the shell refuses there is no door and no caller: the
 * object answers that refusal's 500 before it reads one.
 */
export function forwardedCaller(headers: Headers, config: ShellConfig | { error: string }): string | undefined {
  if ("error" in config) return undefined;
  return headers.get(config.door === "open" ? CLAIMED_USER_HEADER : USER_HEADER) ?? undefined;
}
```

```ts
/** The identity a WebSocket UPGRADE carries, as query parameters — `{}` where
 *  there is nothing to send (M6.5c2, spec §2.1).
 *
 *  **A browser puts no header on an upgrade** (`new WebSocket(url)`, `ws.ts`),
 *  so under the OPEN door the stored name rides the upgrade's URL as
 *  `claimed=`, and the Worker reads it there, on upgrades only. It is the value
 *  `identityHeaders` sends on every fetch — one stored name, one statement of
 *  it — and nothing under any other door: behind Access the edge's own session
 *  is the identity, and a name left from an open door would only be a stale
 *  one in a URL. `ws.ts` encodes it with `URLSearchParams`, so a `+` travels as
 *  `%2B` and never becomes a space (Review Focus 1). */
export function identityParams(): Record<string, string> {
  const who = claimedUser();
  return who && identityMode() === "open" ? { claimed: who } : {};
}
```

```ts
/**
 * What the open door refuses beside it (M6.5c2, spec §2.1; review R2.2-M1),
 * naming BOTH variables — the Worker's form of refusing to start:
 * - an operator list: a claimed name is never an operator's rights. It is a
 *   SECRET, which the deploy guard cannot see (it reads the committed
 *   configurations), so the refusal is here, at run time, and never echoes the
 *   list (R3's M-6);
 * - the dev door on: it is the `worker` door's test instrument, and under
 *   `open` a claim needs no credential. The guard refuses this pair in `vars`
 *   too.
 * `DEV_DOOR_CLIENT_ID` is ignored under `open`, never refused.
 */
function openDoorRefusals(c: ShellConfig): void {
  if (c.door !== "open") return;
  if (c.admins !== null) {
    refuse(
      "YOKOHAMA_WEB_ADMINS is set beside YOKOHAMA_WEB_IDENTITY=open — a claimed name is never an operator: " +
        "delete the operator list (wrangler secret delete YOKOHAMA_WEB_ADMINS), or deploy the worker door",
    );
  }
  if (c.devDoor) {
    refuse(
      "YOKOHAMA_DEV_DOOR=on beside YOKOHAMA_WEB_IDENTITY=open — the dev door is the worker door's test instrument, " +
        "and under open a claim needs no credential: set YOKOHAMA_DEV_DOOR to off, or deploy the worker door",
    );
  }
}
```

- `:30-49` become:

```ts
/**
 * The gate's verdict on a request to `/api/admin` or below (spec §2.9):
 *
 * - `off`: under the OPEN door, for every caller (M6.5c2, spec §2.1; review
 *   R2.2-M1) — a claimed name is never an operator's rights, and `shellConfig`
 *   refuses an operator list beside `open`, but the gate reads the door first
 *   rather than lean on that refusal — and with `YOKOHAMA_WEB_ADMINS` absent.
 *   The routes are then unrouted `/api/*`: the house's `dispatch`, which
 *   answers the layer's own 404;
 * - `operator`: a PERSON — an Access assertion that names an address — whose
 *   address the list holds. Both are trimmed and ASCII-lowercased as the
 *   layer's `User::parse` reads an address (`resolveIdentity`, `shellConfig`),
 *   so they compare as the layer would;
 * - `refused`: anyone else — a person not listed, no one, an identity reached
 *   through the dev door, which NEVER counts, even when the address it claims
 *   is on the list, and a claimed name.
 */
export type Gate = { kind: "off" } | { kind: "refused" } | { kind: "operator"; email: string };

export function operatorGate(door: Door, admins: string[] | null, identity: Identity): Gate {
  if (door === "open" || admins === null) return { kind: "off" };
  if (identity.kind === "person" && admins.includes(identity.email)) return { kind: "operator", email: identity.email };
  return { kind: "refused" };
}
```

```rust
/// Whether `address` is a TEST identity's (spec §2.6; M6.5c2, review R2.2-m4):
/// an EMAIL in the reserved `.test` domain. Every address this reads is a key
/// the layer's `User::parse` wrote — a table's `created_by`, or the caller
/// `init` normalized — and a plain name never holds an `@` (the key grammar),
/// so a plain name is never one, whatever it ends in: under the open door
/// `a.test` is a legal name, and the `test/` prefix EXPIRES after 30 days
/// (R-6.5c2.12).
fn is_test_identity(address: &str) -> bool {
    address.contains('@') && address.ends_with(TEST_DOMAIN)
}
```

- the code, replacing `ABSENT`'s loop in `configFailures`, `operatorList`, `objectBlocks` and the two pool reads:

```js
/** The two doors (M6.5c2, spec §2.1), and what the guard says of each. */
const DOORS = {
  worker: "Cloudflare Access, verified by the shell",
  open: "no identity service: anyone who reaches the Worker plays under any name",
};

/** The door `value`'s top-level `vars` names, trimmed as the shell reads it —
 *  `undefined` for none. The deploy is the top level's, so an environment's
 *  `vars` name no door here. */
function doorOf(value) {
  const vars = value.vars;
  const raw = vars !== null && typeof vars === "object" && !Array.isArray(vars) ? vars.YOKOHAMA_WEB_IDENTITY : undefined;
  return typeof raw === "string" ? raw.trim() : raw;
}

/** Check 3, over `wrangler.jsonc`: the door, and its rules. */
function doorRules(value, failures) {
  const door = doorOf(value);
  if (door === undefined) {
    failures.push("wrangler.jsonc names no door — its vars must set YOKOHAMA_WEB_IDENTITY to worker or open, and there is no default");
  } else if (typeof door !== "string" || !Object.hasOwn(DOORS, door)) {
    failures.push(`wrangler.jsonc's YOKOHAMA_WEB_IDENTITY must be worker or open — got ${JSON.stringify(door)}`);
  }
  for (const [key, why] of Object.entries(ABSENT)) {
    // An open door has no Access application for a workers.dev URL to go around.
    if (key === "workers_dev" && door === "open") continue;
    if (value[key] !== false) {
      failures.push(`wrangler.jsonc must set "${key}": false — got ${JSON.stringify(value[key]) ?? "nothing"}; ${why}`);
    }
  }
  const vars = value.vars !== null && typeof value.vars === "object" ? value.vars : {};
  if (door === "worker") {
    for (const name of ["ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN", "ACCESS_AUD"]) {
      if (typeof vars[name] !== "string" || vars[name].trim() === "") {
        failures.push(`wrangler.jsonc's vars must set ${name} under the worker door — without it no assertion is verified, and every caller is no one`);
      }
    }
  }
  if (door === "open" && typeof vars.YOKOHAMA_DEV_DOOR === "string" && vars.YOKOHAMA_DEV_DOOR.trim().toLowerCase() === "on") {
    failures.push(
      "wrangler.jsonc's vars set YOKOHAMA_DEV_DOOR=on beside YOKOHAMA_WEB_IDENTITY=open — the dev door is the worker door's test instrument, and the Worker refuses the pair",
    );
  }
}

/** What check 7 refuses among production's `vars`: the SECRETS. */
const SECRETS = {
  YOKOHAMA_WEB_ADMINS: "the operator list is a secret (wrangler secret put), never a committed value",
  DEV_DOOR_CLIENT_ID: "the dev door's client id is a secret (wrangler secret put), never a committed value",
};

/** Check 7, over `wrangler.jsonc`: every `vars` block, the top level's and
 *  each environment's, read for the secrets' KEYS. */
function secretsInVars(value, failures) {
  const blocks = [["vars", value.vars]];
  if (value.env !== null && typeof value.env === "object" && !Array.isArray(value.env)) {
    for (const [name, env] of Object.entries(value.env)) {
      if (env !== null && typeof env === "object") blocks.push([`env.${name}.vars`, env.vars]);
    }
  }
  for (const [where, vars] of blocks) {
    if (vars === null || typeof vars !== "object") continue;
    for (const [key, why] of Object.entries(SECRETS)) {
      if (Object.hasOwn(vars, key)) failures.push(`wrangler.jsonc's ${where} name ${key} — ${why}`);
    }
  }
}

/** The pool's configurations, one per door (M6.5c2): each is held to spec
 *  §2.3's assets block and to production's object blocks. */
const POOLS = ["wrangler.test.jsonc", "wrangler.open.test.jsonc"];

/** Check 6, over production and each pool file that parsed. A block production
 *  lacks is named once; a block a pool lacks is that pool's. */
function objectBlocks(production, pools, failures) {
  for (const [key, what] of Object.entries(OBJECT_BLOCKS)) {
    const missing = [["wrangler.jsonc", production], ...pools].filter(([, config]) => config.value[key] === undefined);
    for (const [name] of missing) failures.push(`${name} has no ${key} block — spec §3.1 ${what}`);
    if (missing.length > 0) continue;
    const p = canonical(production.value[key]);
    for (const [name, pool] of pools) {
      const t = canonical(pool.value[key]);
      if (p !== t) {
        failures.push(`${name}'s ${key} differs from wrangler.jsonc's — the pool would test what production does not ship: ${t} against ${p}`);
      }
    }
  }
}

/** The line the guard prints about the door `wrangler.jsonc` names (R-6.5c2.5),
 *  passed or refused — or `undefined` when it names none check 3 knows, which
 *  check 3 refuses. */
export function doorLine(root) {
  const production = readConfig(root, "wrangler.jsonc", []);
  const door = production === undefined ? undefined : doorOf(production.value);
  return typeof door === "string" && Object.hasOwn(DOORS, door) ? `deploy-guard: the door is ${door} — ${DOORS[door]}` : undefined;
}

/** Checks 3 to 7: the ones that need no build. */
export function configFailures(root) {
  const failures = [];
  const production = readConfig(root, "wrangler.jsonc", failures);
  if (production) {
    doorRules(production.value, failures);
    if (production.text.includes("YOKOHAMA_WEB_TEST_CLOCK")) {
      failures.push("wrangler.jsonc names YOKOHAMA_WEB_TEST_CLOCK — the test clock is set in wrangler.test.jsonc and nowhere else");
    }
    assetsBlock("wrangler.jsonc", production.value, failures);
    secretsInVars(production.value, failures);
  }
  const pools = [];
  for (const name of POOLS) {
    const pool = readConfig(root, name, failures);
    if (pool) {
      assetsBlock(name, pool.value, failures);
      pools.push([name, pool]);
    }
  }
  if (production) objectBlocks(production, pools, failures);
  return failures;
}
```

**Confirmed (review o2):**
- `deliverArchive` keys each upload in flight by its plan's key (`table.ts:476-481`).
- A plan's key is a SHA-256 over its record's and its table's texts (`receipt.rs:229-231`).

**Why a conflict whose stamp does not land is FINAL.** Routing the conflict through `stamp_archive` and then reading
the answer with today's `stampArm` would make another game's record `{"stamped": false, "over": true}`. That is
`retry`, and it would retry hourly for ever. `settledArm` keeps every conflict final except the one the layer stamped
(R-6.5c2.11: "on the Worker the conflict stays final and the table stays stranded until the operator's `?force`").

```ts
// upload and the stamp leave TOGETHER is `settledArm`'s. A conflict the stamp
// landed on — the layer found an earlier completion of this same game at the

// `stampArm` (another game's `{stamped: false, over: true}` retried hourly for
// ever); a conflict completed without its stamp; a landed upload's failed
// stamp not retried.
describe("what an upload and its stamp leave together (R-6.5c2.11)", () => {
  const conflict: Outcome = { outcome: "conflict", detail: PLAN.record_key, held: OTHER_SEED };
  it("completes a conflict the stamp landed on, and leaves every other conflict final", () => {
    expect(settledArm(conflict, { stamped: true, over: true })).toBe("stamped");
    for (const stamp of [{ stamped: false, over: true }, { stamped: false, over: false }, undefined]) {
      expect(settledArm(conflict, stamp), JSON.stringify(stamp)).toBe("final");

      expect(settledArm(outcome, { stamped: false, over: false }), outcome.outcome).toBe("no-longer-over");
      expect(settledArm(outcome, { stamped: false, over: true }), outcome.outcome).toBe("retry");
      expect(settledArm(outcome, undefined), outcome.outcome).toBe("retry");
    }
  });
```

```ts
 *  logs it (`logOutcome` names the detail alone). */
export type Outcome = { outcome: "landed" | "identical" | "conflict" | "failed"; detail: string; held?: string };
```

- `executePlan` (`:109-129`) becomes the function below. In its doc (`:89-108`), step 1 reads "…these very bytes are
  `identical`, other bytes a `conflict` carrying them — either way nothing is written…", and step 3 "…other bytes a
  `conflict`, carrying them.".

```ts
export async function executePlan(bucket: Bucket, plan: Plan): Promise<Outcome> {
  const at = (outcome: "landed" | "identical"): Outcome => ({ outcome, detail: plan.record_key });
  // What the key holds, against this plan's record — as TEXT: a conflict hands
  // the held text on, for the module to compare (R-6.5c2.11).
  const against = (held: string): Outcome =>
    held === plan.record ? at("identical") : { outcome: "conflict", detail: plan.record_key, held };
  try {
    const held = await textAt(bucket, plan.record_key);
    if (held !== null) return against(held);
    await bucket.put(plan.table_key, plan.table);
    const created = await bucket.put(plan.record_key, plan.record, { onlyIf: new Headers({ "If-None-Match": "*" }) });
    if (created !== null) return at("landed");
    const raced = await textAt(bucket, plan.record_key);
    if (raced === null) {
      // The create was refused because the key held a record, and the key
      // now holds none: only a delete in between could do that, and nothing
      // this shell runs deletes an archived key. Whatever did, the pair is
      // not known to be whole, so the upload is retried as a failure.
      return { outcome: "failed", detail: `${plan.record_key} refused a create as present, then read as absent` };
    }
    return against(raced);
  } catch (e) {
    return { outcome: "failed", detail: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e) };
  }
}
```

```ts
/**
 * What an owed save's upload and its stamp leave TOGETHER (M6.5c2,
 * R-6.5c2.11): a `conflict` the stamp LANDED on — the archive held an earlier
 * completion of this same game, which the layer compared in Rust — is
 * `stamped`, the save complete; a conflict it did not land on is `final`,
 * whatever the stamp answered — as the M6.5c spec §2.6 ruled every conflict:
 * nothing owed, and nothing retried, since another game's record (which only a
 * caller-chosen id can reach) no retry can clear. Every other outcome is
 * `stampArm`'s, and a stamp that answered no 200 is retried.
 */
export function settledArm(outcome: Outcome, stamp: Stamp | undefined): "stamped" | "no-longer-over" | "retry" | "final" {
  if (outcome.outcome === "conflict") return stamp?.stamped ? "stamped" : "final";
  return stamp === undefined ? "retry" : stampArm(stamp);
}
```

`worker/test/gates.ts`, after `heldPuts` (`:207-219`):

```ts
/**
 * Two uploads' puts, each held at a gate of its OWN — the M6.5c2 refinish
 * race's: the FIRST put to arrive waits at `openFirst`'s gate, the SECOND at
 * `openSecond`'s, and every later put goes straight through. An upload's first
 * put is its table's (`executePlan`), so two overlapping uploads are released
 * one at a time: open the first, and its record put follows its table's
 * through; then the second. Gates made in the cell's own context, as
 * `heldPuts`'s are. `arrived()` counts the puts that have reached the bucket.
 */
export function heldInTurn(): { through: PutThrough; arrived(): number; openFirst(): void; openSecond(): void; openAll(): void } {
  const [first, second] = [gate(), gate()];
  let arrived = 0;
  return {
    through: async (real, key, value, options) => {
      const turn = arrived++;
      if (turn === 0) await first.opened;
      else if (turn === 1) await second.opened;
      return real.put(key, value, options);
    },
    arrived: () => arrived,
    openFirst: () => first.open(),
    openSecond: () => second.open(),
    openAll: () => {
      first.open();
      second.open();
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
/**
 * The walk's last two moves, from the decision two undos reach at the
 * one-person table — measured by the plan: `1` opens the President's retreat,
 * `0` recovers no assistant from the Bank, `confirm` retreats, and `1` ends the
 * additional-action phase, the game over with the walk's own record. `1` for
 * one assistant instead is a DIFFERENT end of the same game: another record.
 */
const ORIGINAL_END = ["1", "0", "confirm", "1"] as const;
const DIFFERENT_END = ["1", "1", "confirm", "1"] as const;

/** `lines` played in order through `input`, each held to `play`'s premise;
 *  answers the last play. */
async function playAll(
  input: (line: string) => Promise<Response>,
  play: (res: Response) => Promise<Play>,
  lines: readonly string[],
): Promise<Play> {
  let last: Play | undefined;
  for (const line of lines) last = await play(await input(line));
  return last!;
}
```

```ts
import type { Exports } from "../gen/factory.js";
import type { Instance, Replied } from "./module";
import { log } from "./respond";

/**
 * **One guarded module call, as a table object makes it** (spec §2.4
 * "Traps"; Task 13's review, m4) — split out of `table.ts` at M6.5c2 (spec
 * §2.7), where the request's own call (`Table.call`), the receipt loop's two
 * dispatches (`Saves.deleting`, `Saves.redispatch`) and an owed save's stamp
 * (`Saves.stamp`) each wrote the same pattern out: a stage name, ONE
 * `guarded`, the layer's documents read back, and a `trap` line naming the
 * stage the trap met. It is written here once.
 */

/** The table object's trap 500, host-written (spec §2.4, §4). */
export const TRAP = "the table's engine stopped — try again";

/** The layer's documents a table object stores, in the order the wake loads
 *  them (spec §2.4). The fourth `docs` kind, `picker`, is the host's own. */
export const LAYER_DOCS = ["record", "table", "chat"] as const;
export type LayerDoc = (typeof LAYER_DOCS)[number];

/** A module call's reply, and the reading its clock was pinned to (the plan's
 *  ruling P-2). */
export interface Pinned {
  reply: Replied;
  at: number;
}

/** A call's pinned reply, and each layer document read back out of the module
 *  after it — `undefined` for one the module does not hold. The map is empty
 *  where the store refuses the id (`readLayerDocs`). */
export interface Called extends Pinned {
  docs: Map<LayerDoc, string | undefined>;
}

/**
 * `run` over the module under ONE `Instance.guarded`, then the layer's three
 * documents read back out of it — so a trap in any step drops the module and
 * nothing the call did is committed: a move a trapped call made was never
 * acknowledged. The documents are read before anything else is computed from
 * the module (the orchestrator's ruling I-42).
 *
 * `first` is the stage `run` starts in, and `run` names each later one through
 * `stage`; after `run` returns the stage is `read`. A trap is logged
 * `trap {id, call: <the stage it met>, error}` and answers `undefined`, for
 * the caller to answer in its own way — the trap 500, or an owed save kept
 * for its retry. Anything else `run` throws reaches the caller unchanged, as
 * `guarded`'s does.
 */
export function guardedCall<T extends Pinned>(
  instance: Instance,
  id: string,
  first: string,
  run: (mod: Exports, stage: (name: string) => void) => T,
): (T & { docs: Map<LayerDoc, string | undefined> }) | undefined {
  let stage = first;
  const done = instance.guarded((mod) => {
    const ran = run(mod, (name) => {
      stage = name;
    });
    stage = "read";
    return { ...ran, docs: readLayerDocs(mod, id) };
  });
  if ("trapped" in done) {
    log("trap", { id, call: stage, error: done.trapped });
    return undefined;
  }
  return done.ok;
}
```

`table.ts`, which imports them:

`Table.call` (today `:1270-1289`) becomes:

```ts
  private call(incoming: Incoming, instance: Instance): Called | Response {
    const { id, transport } = incoming;
    const first = incoming.create ? "create" : transport === undefined ? "dispatch" : "events";
    const called = guardedCall(instance, id, first, (mod) =>
      this.pinned(mod, (m) =>
        incoming.create
          ? m.create(incoming.user, incoming.body, id, incoming.contentType)
          : transport === undefined
            ? m.dispatch(incoming.user, incoming.method, incoming.path, incoming.query, incoming.contentType, incoming.body)
            : m.events(id, incoming.user, transport === "events" ? incoming.query : ""),
      ),
    );
    return called ?? respond(500, errorBody(TRAP));
  }
```

Keep its doc (`:1257-1269`). Its first sentence names "ONE `Instance.guarded`", which is now inside
`guardedCall`, so it reads true as written.

```ts
/**
 * **What the slot's half asks of the table object it serves** (spec §2.5,
 * §2.7). It keeps nothing of the object but the pushes in flight: everything
 * else is read through here at the moment it is needed — `env` included,
 * because a cell REPLACES the live object's `env` to fail a push
 * (`failPushes`, `test/gates.ts`), and a binding kept at construction would
 * push past it.
 */
export interface DeliveryHost {
  /** The object's name, `ctx.id.name`: `undefined` for an object reached by
   *  none. */
  name(): string | undefined;
  /** The object's SQLite, `ctx.storage.sql`. */
  sql(): SqlStorage;
  /** The house's stub, made from the object's `env` as it is at the call. */
  house(): DurableObjectStub<House>;
  /** A module instance of its own, for ONE `house_copy` (`copyOf`), configured
   *  from the object's `env` as it is at the call. */
  scratch(): Instance;
  /** The object's configuration, as `shellConfig` read it. */
  config(): ShellConfig | { error: string };
  /** The table's ONE write batch, the alarm beside it (`Table.batch`). */
  batch(writes: (sql: SqlStorage) => void, alarm?: number | null): void;
  /** `meta.marker`, or `undefined` when none stands. */
  markerOf(sql: SqlStorage): Marker | undefined;
  /** An owed save's retry, while one is owed and the archive is on
   *  (`Saves.archiveRung`). */
  archiveRung(sql: SqlStorage): number | undefined;
  /** A standing marker's end, or the table's expiry (`Table.deadlines`). */
  deadlines(sql: SqlStorage): number | undefined;
  /** The object ends (`Table.end`): its REMOVAL acknowledged. */
  end(marker: Marker | undefined): Promise<void>;
}
```

```ts
  private stamp(id: string, instance: Instance, owed: ArchiveOwed, outcome: Outcome): Called | undefined {
    return guardedCall(instance, id, "receipt", (mod, stage) => {
      mod.receipt(owed.plan.key, JSON.stringify(outcome));
      stage("stamp_archive");
      return { reply: pinnedTo(mod, owed.reading, (m) => m.stamp_archive(id)), at: owed.reading };
    });
  }
```

```ts
  private redispatch(
    id: string,
    instance: Instance,
    first: Called,
    plan: Plan,
    outcome: Outcome,
    f: (mod: Exports) => Reply,
    call: string,
  ): Called | Response {
    const again = guardedCall(instance, id, "receipt", (mod, stage) => {
      mod.receipt(plan.key, JSON.stringify(outcome));
      stage(call);
      return { reply: pinnedTo(mod, first.at, f), at: first.at };
    });
    if (again === undefined) return respond(500, errorBody(TRAP));
    return { ...again, reply: { ...again.reply, bumps: [...first.reply.bumps, ...again.reply.bumps] } };
  }
```

```ts
  constructor(ctx: DurableObjectState, env: Env) {
    super(ctx, env);
    // Nothing is written here: the first write batch creates the tables.
    this.config = shellConfig(env);
    // The two halves read this object through their hosts, at the moment they
    // need it: `env` above all, which a cell REPLACES on the live object
    // (`failPushes`, `swapBucket`), so neither half keeps a binding of its own.
    // And every call to `deliverSlot` and `sendFrames` goes through THIS
    // object's method, which a cell's spy on the prototype counts.
    this.delivery = new Delivery({
      name: () => this.ctx.id.name,
      sql: () => this.ctx.storage.sql,
      house: () => this.env.HOUSE.get(this.env.HOUSE.idFromName(HOUSE_NAME)),
      scratch: () => new Instance(moduleConfig(this.env, null)),
      config: () => this.config,
      batch: (writes, alarm) => this.batch(writes, alarm),
      markerOf: (sql) => markerOf(sql),
      archiveRung: (sql) => this.saves.archiveRung(sql),
      deadlines: (sql) => this.deadlines(sql),
      end: (marker) => this.end(marker),
    });
    this.saves = new Saves({
      name: () => this.ctx.id.name,
      sql: () => this.ctx.storage.sql,
      config: () => this.config,
      bucket: () => this.env.ARCHIVE as R2Bucket,
      instance: () => (this.instance ??= new Instance(moduleConfig(this.env, null))),
      batch: (writes, alarm) => this.batch(writes, alarm),
      wake: (id, instance, config, traps) => this.wake(id, instance, config, traps),
      commit: (id, called, parts, archive, ending) => this.commit(id, called, parts, archive, ending),
      sendFrames: (id, bumps) => this.sendFrames(id, bumps),
      deliverSlot: () => this.deliverSlot(),
      dueBesidesArchive: (sql) => this.dueBesidesArchive(sql),
      reading: () => this.reading(),
    });
    // The client's keep-alive (spec §2.7): every `ping` a socket sends is
    // answered `pong` by the platform, and never reaches `webSocketMessage`.
    ctx.setWebSocketAutoResponse(new WebSocketRequestResponsePair("ping", "pong"));
  }

  /**
   * **The slot's ONE delivery routine** (spec §2.5), on the object: every

   * it runs is `Delivery.deliverSlot`.
   */
  deliverSlot(): Promise<void> {

  }
```

### Task 21: One read of the documents per request; one time unit in the operator's listing; Task 14's L-8 and L-4 (spec §2.7; M6.5c close §6.2; handover §4.6)

**What changes, and why.**
- **One read per request (F-4).** `readDocs` runs at four sites. Today's lines:
  - `table.ts:441`, `recopy`, now `Delivery.recopy`;
  - `:867`, `deleting`, now `Saves.deleting`;
  - `:1226`, `wake`;
  - `:1489`, `commit`.

  A request runs up to three of them. MEASURED at the base, with a spy on `readDocs` filtered to the table's
  own storage: a warm `GET` 1, a cold `GET` 2, a cold abandon that saves first 3, and the alarm's expiry 3.
  Each request path now reads ONCE, right after `ready`, and hands the one read to its wake, its receipt loop
  and its batch. An owed save's settling does the same in its own synchronous turn.
- **Why one read is enough.** Nothing writes a document between the read and the batch:
  - `answer` runs in one synchronous turn;
  - `abandon` and `expire` await only inside `blockConcurrencyWhile`. Cloudflare's rule for it (quoted in
    the abandon's own doc): "all events that were not explicitly initiated as part of the callback itself
    will be blocked", so an earlier request's upload cannot settle into the table mid-loop.
- **L-8 closes with the thread.** `deleting` read every document only to ask whether a record is stored
  (`gameOf(reading, stored.has("record"))`). It now reads nothing of its own: better than the one-row query
  L-8 proposed.
- **One time unit.** The operator's listing carries `created_at` and `archived_at` in the layer's unix
  SECONDS, and `last_active` in the shell's MILLISECONDS (deployment 17 read `1790224338` beside
  `1790224338723`). The listing becomes all SECONDS: `last_active` is cut to whole seconds where the listing
  is built. Why seconds:
  - two of the three fields are the layer's, and every time the API carries is seconds;
  - an operator reads `last_active` against `created_at`;
  - the slot KEEPS milliseconds — the shell's own time base, as the two-time-bases rule says — so nothing
    stored changes.

  The listing is HOST-ONLY: no `web/src/wire/` file carries it, no client reads it, and the live replay only
  forces. So no corpus moves.

```ts
import { evictDurableObject, runDurableObjectAlarm, runInDurableObject } from "cloudflare:test";
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import * as storageModule from "../src/storage";
import type { Table } from "../src/table";
import { backdate, call, DAY_MS, logsDuring, RED, seedPlaying, settle } from "./helpers";

// **One read of the documents per request** (F-4; spec §2.7; the M6.5c
// close §6.2). The three documents — the record's whole text among them —
// were read by the wake of a fresh module, by the receipt loop of a delete
// through the layer, and by the batch's comparison: up to three times a
// request. Each path now reads once and hands the read on.
//
// ONE file, and its ids are its own (pool fact 5).

/**
 * Every `readDocs` call made on `stub`'s OWN storage while `f` runs — counted
 * by a spy at MODULE scope (`archiveOff`'s technique in `helpers.ts`), which
 * calls through, and filtered to the table's `SqlStorage`: the house answers
 * in the same isolate and reads its own documents through the same function.
 * The storage is the live instance's, taken AFTER any eviction the cell made,
 * so it is the one the request reads.
 */
async function readsDuring(stub: DurableObjectStub<Table>, f: () => Promise<unknown>): Promise<number> {
  let own: SqlStorage | undefined;
  await runInDurableObject(stub, (_t, state) => {
    own = state.storage.sql;
  });
  const spy = vi.spyOn(storageModule, "readDocs");
  try {
    await f();
    return spy.mock.calls.filter(([sql]) => sql === own).length;
  } finally {
    spy.mockRestore();
  }
}

describe("one read of the documents per request (F-4; spec §2.7)", () => {
  // The guard: a warm request read them once before this cycle too (the
  // batch's comparison), and still does.
  it("a warm request reads the documents once", async () => {
    const stub = await seedPlaying("reads-warm");
    expect(await readsDuring(stub, () => call(stub, RED, "GET", "/api/games/reads-warm/events"))).toBe(1);
  });

  // MEASURED at the base: 2 — the wake loading the fresh module, then the
  // batch. Mutant: the wake reads its own.
  it("a cold request — the wake loads a fresh module — reads them once", async () => {
    const stub = await seedPlaying("reads-cold");
    await evictDurableObject(stub);
    expect(await readsDuring(stub, () => call(stub, RED, "GET", "/api/games/reads-cold/events"))).toBe(1);
  });

  // MEASURED at the base: 3 — the wake, the receipt loop (which read every
  // document to ask whether a record is stored: Task 14's L-8) and the batch.
  // The creator's abandon of a started game owes its save, so the loop
  // uploads to this file's bucket and dispatches again. Mutants: `deleting`
  // reads its own (L-8 back); the batch reads its own.
  it("a cold abandon that saves first reads them once: the wake, the receipt loop and the batch share it", async () => {
    const stub = await seedPlaying("reads-abandon");
    await evictDurableObject(stub);
    const reads = await readsDuring(stub, () =>
      logsDuring(async () => {
        const res = await call(stub, RED, "DELETE", "/api/games/reads-abandon");
        expect(res.status, "premise: the creator's abandon of a started game, its save made").toBe(204);
        await settle(stub);
      }),
    );
    expect(reads).toBe(1);
  });

  // MEASURED at the base: 3 — the alarm's copy step, then the expiry's
  // receipt loop and batch. The alarm is no request: its copy step and its
  // expiry are two synchronous turns, one read each.
  it("the alarm's expiry reads them twice: once for its copy step, once for the expiry", async () => {
    const stub = await seedPlaying("reads-expiry");
    await backdate(stub, Date.now() - 91 * DAY_MS);
    const reads = await readsDuring(stub, () =>
      logsDuring(async () => {
        expect(await runDurableObjectAlarm(stub), "premise: an alarm stood, and ran").toBe(true);
        await settle(stub);
      }),
    );
    expect(reads).toBe(2);
  });
});
```

```ts
  /**
   * The object ends (spec §2.4 step 6; spec §2.9's force): its module dropped,
   * and `deleteAll()`, which at this compatibility date deletes its alarm too.
   * Logged:
   *
   * - `marker-ended` when it ends a marker;
   * - `forced` when an operator's force made the REMOVAL — `force`'s batch
   *   flags it (`meta.forced`), and its immediate path passes `forced`;
   * - `removal-ended` for a REMOVAL neither wrote (Task 14's L-4): one the code
   *   before the marker wrote (deployments 14–16), or a force by the code
   *   before the flag (17–20), acknowledged since. Every delete through the
   *   layer writes its marker in the batch that writes its REMOVAL, so no code
   *   since writes such a removal, and every `forced` line has its `operator`
   *   line.
   *
   * An owed save it drops is logged `archive-owed-dropped` first, once
   * `deleteAll()` has dropped it — only a force's immediate path meets one
   * here, since a delete's batch and a force's clear it — so a force logs the
   * two in ONE order on both its paths.
   */
  private async end(marker: Marker | undefined, forced = false): Promise<void> {
    const id = this.ctx.id.name;
    const sql = this.ctx.storage.sql;
    const owed = archiveOwedOf(sql);
    const flagged = forced || getMeta(sql, "forced") !== undefined;
    this.instance?.drop();
    await this.ctx.storage.deleteAll();
    if (owed !== undefined) log("archive-owed-dropped", { id, record_key: owed.plan.record_key, attempt: owed.attempt });
    if (marker !== undefined) log("marker-ended", { id, reason: marker.reason, at: marker.at, kept: marker.kept });
    else if (flagged) log("forced", { id });
    else log("removal-ended", { id });
  }
```

the slot's own four …", add ", then flags the REMOVAL as a force's (`forced`)".

- [ ] **Step 10 (RULED — A-3): the memo.** In `storage.ts`, replace `hasTables` (today `:48-57`) with:

```ts
/**
 * The objects whose two tables are KNOWN to exist (F-4's rows read; A-3):
 * once `hasTables` has found them, it answers from here. `sqlite_master` is
 * scanned whole, and `hasTables` runs inside every `getMeta` and `readDocs` —
 * MEASURED at M6.5c2's base, 30 of a warm request's 32 rows read. Only
 * `deleteAll()` drops the tables, and its one caller forgets them
 * (`forgetTables`, from `Table.end`). Keyed by the object's `SqlStorage`,
 * which a new instance — after an eviction or a reset — gets anew; a table
 * NOT found is never remembered, so tables a batch creates are found by the
 * next read.
 */
const known = new WeakSet<SqlStorage>();

/** Whether the first write batch has run. Both tables are created by one
 *  `ensureTables`, inside one transaction, so it asks for both. It names them:
 *  `sqlite_master` also lists the platform's own `_cf_METADATA` once an alarm
 *  has been set. Answered from `known` once they are found. */
export function hasTables(sql: SqlStorage): boolean {
  if (known.has(sql)) return true;
  const { n } = sql
    .exec<{ n: number }>("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name IN ('docs', 'meta')")
    .one();
  if (n === 2) known.add(sql);
  return n === 2;
}

/** The tables forgotten, once `deleteAll()` has dropped them (`Table.end`): a
 *  straggling acknowledgement, a force's answer and a later create then read
 *  them absent. */
export function forgetTables(sql: SqlStorage): void {
  known.delete(sql);
}
```

### Task 22: The module's structural invariants — the picker's rule on every call, the scrub fenced all the way down, one plan per call, the restatements imported, the figures in one place (spec §2.6, §2.7; R1's cleanup debts 1–4 and 6)

Five debts, each made STRUCTURAL: after this task the compiler or a cell holds each, where before a comment or
a fact about how one instance is used held it.

1. **The picker's rule on every call** (R1's debt 1). Three exports reach `Games::handle` outside
   `picker::around`, and a handle one of them REBUILDS pumps an owed bot move and persists it:
   - `events_inner`;
   - `stamp_archive_inner`;
   - `expire_inner`'s arm with no creator.

   That is a record change, and no list is cleared for it. It is safe today only because a list implies a
   resident handle, and one instance holds one table.

   **Decision: clear the list whenever the record changes, at the ONE drain every layer call already passes
   through (`from_the_layer`). Not: route them through `around`.** The evidence:
   - `around` is keyed by a REQUEST: it reads the path (`game_of`) and, after a 200 `…/input`, the body
     (`line_of`). These three calls have neither, and routing them through it means inventing a request.
   - `around`'s rule for a record change is also the WRONG one for them. After a line that changed the record
     and left a picker open, `around` marks the entry `Dropped` (`after_input`'s last arm), because the SAME
     `Repl` still has that picker open. A call that is no dispatch changes a record only through a rebuild,
     whose new `Repl` starts with its picker CLOSED, so its whole entry must go, a `Dropped` one included.
   - So `from_the_layer` takes a `Scope` naming which rule applies, and no call can reach `Games` without
     naming one:
     - `Scope::Dispatch` — `around` applies the rule inside the call;
     - `Scope::Table(id)` — the record is watched across the call.
   - Of the three, `expire_inner`'s no-creator arm cannot change a record at all: its `handle` answers `Err`
     for a table that is gone or unreadable, or answers a RESIDENT handle, which is never rebuilt. It takes
     `Scope::Table` all the same, so the rule holds without that fact.

   **The residual, named:** a rebuild at the SAME record — no pump — leaves a stale list the record rule cannot
   see. It is unreachable: nothing in this host evicts a resident handle. `Games` evicts only on a conflicting
   write, and a `MemStore` with one writer has none. Only a handle identity (an entry tied to the `Arc` it was
   built on) would close it. That is not taken: the spec offers the two record-based options, and this one is
   the record's.
2. **The scrub's fence all the way down** (R1's debt 2). `scrub` (`house.rs:100-123`) names every field of
   `TableDoc` and `Lock`. It now names every field of each `SeatDoc` variant, of `TurnMirror`, and of its
   `bot: Option<BotDescriptor>` (Task 3). So a field added at any depth — a per-seat secret, a bot's
   `agent_seed` — fails to COMPILE here, and whoever adds it decides whether the house may hold it.
   MEASURED in a scratch crate of the same shapes, under clippy `-D warnings`:
   - the fence passes as one exhaustive `match` (a nested `if let` trips `clippy::collapsible_match`);
   - a field added to `BotDescriptor`, `TurnMirror` or `SeatDoc::Human` fails with E0027, "pattern does not
     mention field";
   - a new `SeatDoc` variant fails with E0004.
3. **One plan per call** (R1's debt 3). `ReceiptArchive.pending` (`receipt.rs:86-88`) keeps only the LAST
   deferred plan, dropping an earlier one without a word.

   **Decision: a second deferred plan of ANOTHER key in one call is refused (the first kept), rather than
   `pending` becoming a list.** The evidence: the shell carries ONE plan per reply at three sites:
   - `Reply.archive` is one plan's JSON, parsed by `parsePlan`;
   - `meta.archive_owed` holds one plan;
   - the receipt loop (`Saves.deleting`) uploads and re-dispatches one.

   A list would move all three, and `archive_owed`'s stored format, for a case no layer site reaches (R1: the
   layer's `delete` reads the stored record without building a handle, and `archive_over_retry`'s two puts
   are one plan). A refusal keeps the contract, makes the case LOUD at its own site, and a second put of the
   SAME plan still defers one.
4. **The restatements imported** (R1's debt 4; spec §2.6). The five items Task 7 made the layer export replace
   the module's copies (A-4's names):
   - the error body (`api::error_body`), Task 4's third arm among it;

   - the house frame (`signal::house_frame`);
   - the clock (`games::HostClock`);
   - the platform scan (`platform::calls_in`, over `platform::CALLS`).

   The frame's source-TEXT pin already retired in Task 7, which repointed the cell to the export. Once

5. **The figures in one place** (R1's debt 6). `copyOf`'s doc (in `delivery.ts` since Task 20; today

   - it reads 121,001 data bytes and a 122,381-byte data section;

```rust
    fn a_call_that_is_no_dispatch_clears_a_picker_whose_record_its_rebuild_changed() {

        let dir = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../worker/test/fixtures");
        let stored_table = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("owed-pump.table.json")).expect("the committed fixture");

            })

        // spelled out in place (MEASURED under the lint gate).

        let calls: [(&str, Call); 2] =
            [("events", || events_inner("owed", Some(RED), "")), ("stamp_archive", || stamp_archive_inner("owed"))];
        for (what, call) in calls {
            for (kind, entry, want) in [("a list", stale(), Some("[]")), ("a dropped picker", super::Picker::Dropped, None)] {
                fresh("owed", &stored_table, &owed);
                super::with_pickers(|pickers| pickers.insert("owed".to_string(), entry));
                let r = call();
                assert_eq!(

                assert_eq!(r.picker.as_deref(), want, "{what}, {kind}: a list's row is deleted, and no row that never was");
                assert!(super::with_pickers(|pickers| !pickers.contains_key("owed")), "{what}, {kind}: the entry is gone");
```

```rust
    #[test]
    fn a_second_deferred_plan_in_one_call_is_refused_and_the_first_is_carried() {

        init_inner(&r2(None)).unwrap();
        let archive = super::RECEIPTS.lock().unwrap().clone().expect("the receipt archive, under r2");
        let table = |id: &str| json!({ "created_by": RED, "id": id }).to_string();
        let failed_with = |r: &Result<yokohama_web::archive::PutOutcome, PutError>, sentence: &str| {
            matches!(r, Err(PutError::Failed(said)) if said.as_str() == sentence)
        };
        let first = archive.put("", Why::Over, "one", r#"{"r":1}"#, &table("one"));
        assert!(failed_with(&first, super::DEFERRED), "{first:?}");
        let again = archive.put("", Why::Over, "one", r#"{"r":1}"#, &table("one"));
        assert!(failed_with(&again, super::DEFERRED), "the same plan again is still one plan: {again:?}");
        let second = archive.put("", Why::Over, "two", r#"{"r":2}"#, &table("two"));
        assert!(failed_with(&second, super::SECOND_PLAN), "{second:?}");
        let drained: Value = serde_json::from_str(&super::drain_plan().expect("a plan is carried")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(drained["record_key"], "test/rev7/over/one.json", "the FIRST plan is the one the reply carries");
```

```rust
/// Which of spec §2.4's picker rules a call into the layer answers to (R1's
/// cleanup debt 1). [`from_the_layer`] takes one with every call, so no call
/// reaches `Games` without its rule named.
pub(crate) enum Scope<'a> {
    /// A dispatch: `picker::around`, INSIDE the call, applies the rule — the
    /// input rule after a 200 `…/input`, and a changed record's clear after
    /// any other dispatch at or below `/api/games/{id}`.
    Dispatch,
    /// Any other call on the game `id` names — `events`, `stamp_archive`,
    /// `expire`'s arm with no creator, `restore_picker`: `id`'s record is
    /// watched across the call, and a change clears `id`'s picker
    /// (`picker::watching`). Such a call changes a record only by REBUILDING
    /// the handle, whose owed bot pump is the one move it can make, and a
    /// rebuilt `Repl` starts with its picker closed — so the whole entry goes,
    /// a `Dropped` one included.
    Table(&'a str),
}
```

`from_the_layer` becomes:

```rust
pub(crate) fn from_the_layer(
    scope: Scope<'_>,
    call: impl FnOnce(&Games) -> (u16, String, Option<String>),
) -> ReplyData {
    let guard = GAMES.lock().expect("the host's games");
    let games = guard.as_ref().expect("init() before any call into the layer");
    let (status, body, picker) = match scope {
        Scope::Dispatch => call(games),
        Scope::Table(id) => {
            let ((status, body, picker), cleared) = picker::watching(games, id, || call(games));
            (status, body, picker.or(cleared))
        }
    };
    ReplyData { status, body, bumps: drain_bumps(), archive: receipt::drain_plan(), picker, dropped: None, logs: drain_logs() }
}
```

`logs: drain_logs()` is Task 6's field, kept as Task 6 wrote it. If Task 6's commit spells the drain otherwise,
keep that spelling. Its doc (`:459-473`) gains a paragraph after its first:

```rust
/// **Spec §2.4's picker rule rides every call** (R1's cleanup debt 1):
/// `scope` names it — [`Scope::Dispatch`] where `around` applies it inside the
/// call, [`Scope::Table`] for any other call on a game, whose record is watched
/// here. A call's own `Reply.picker` wins over the watch's: `restore_picker`
/// answers its own.
```

```rust
/// Spec §2.4's rule for a changed record, stated once for [`around`] and
/// [`watching`]: `id`'s entry removed, and `"[]"` when it held a list, whose
/// row the shell then deletes.
fn clear_if(changed: bool, id: &str) -> Option<String> {
    if !changed {
        return None;
    }
    with_pickers(|pickers| pickers.remove(id)).and_then(cleared)
}

/// The rule for a call that is no dispatch ([`crate::Scope::Table`]; R1's
/// cleanup debt 1): `id`'s record read before and after `call`, and on a
/// change the entry cleared. `events`, `stamp_archive` and `expire`'s arm with
/// no creator reach `Games::handle` outside [`around`], and a handle one of
/// them rebuilds pumps an owed bot move and persists it — the one way such a
/// call changes a record — so the picker it served is closed. Nothing today
/// leaves an entry whose handle is gone, since one instance holds one table;
/// the rule now holds without that fact.
pub(crate) fn watching<T>(games: &Games, id: &str, call: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> (T, Option<String>) {
    let before = record_of(games, id);
    let out = call();
    let changed = record_of(games, id) != before;
    (out, clear_if(changed, id))
}
```

```rust
/// The clock: the layer's `HostClock` (M6.5c2, spec §2.6; R1's cleanup debt
/// 4) — frozen while pinned, else live — where this host carried its own copy
/// of the browser host's three statics.
///
/// Live is `Date.now()` on the target and the clock's own tick everywhere else
/// — the crate's own cells and the workspace lint gate compile for the host,
/// and `js_sys::Date::now` there is a stub that panics.
///
/// **[`set_clock`] is its only writer.** [`init`] rebuilds everything else
/// this crate holds and leaves the clock as it was: the plan's ruling P-2 has
/// the shell pin a reading before every call that can reach the layer's
/// clock.
static CLOCK: HostClock = HostClock::new();

fn now() -> u64 {
    CLOCK.now(|| {
        #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
        {
            (js_sys::Date::now() / 1000.0) as u64
        }
        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
        {
            CLOCK.tick()
        }
    })
}

/// Pin the clock to `seconds`, or pass `undefined` for the live clock — and get
/// back what it replaced (`undefined` = live), so a caller that pins a reading
/// for one call can restore a test configuration's frozen clock after it (spec
/// §2.6). Whole seconds: a fraction is dropped, as the live arm drops it — the
/// `f64` is this export's, and the layer's clock keeps whole seconds.
#[wasm_bindgen]
pub fn set_clock(seconds: Option<f64>) -> Option<f64> {
    CLOCK.set(seconds.map(|s| s as u64)).map(|s| s as f64)
}
```

```rust
    /// **The crate's own scan** (spec §5.1): this is host code, and its ONLY
    /// platform call is the clock. Every `src/*.rs` of this crate is read by
    /// the layer's own `platform::calls_in` — the hosts' scan over the eight
    /// patterns (`platform::CALLS`), which stops at a file's first column-0
    /// `#[cfg(test)]` (M6.5c2, spec §2.6; R1's cleanup debt 4).
    ///
    /// Three anti-vacuity partners, and they are this host's own: the layer's
    /// scan must find a call where there is one; this one must have looked at
    /// a file; and the one allowed call must be in CODE rather than in prose —
    /// a doc comment naming `js_sys::Date::now` would otherwise keep this cell
    /// green over a crate that had stopped making the call at all.
    #[test]
    fn this_host_makes_no_platform_call_but_the_clock() {
        assert!(
            !yokohama_web::platform::calls_in("probe.rs", "use std::fs;\n").is_empty(),
            "anti-vacuity: the layer's scan finds a call where there is one",
        );
        let src = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("src");
        let mut escaped: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        let mut scanned = 0usize;
        let mut clock_in_code = false;
        for entry in std::fs::read_dir(&src).expect("src is readable") {
            let path = entry.expect("an entry").path();
            if path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) != Some("rs") {
                continue;
            }
            let name = path.file_name().unwrap().to_str().unwrap().to_string();
            let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).expect("readable");
            scanned += 1;
            escaped.extend(yokohama_web::platform::calls_in(&name, &text));
            // The partner reads the lines `calls_in` reads: those above the
            // file's first column-0 `#[cfg(test)]`.
            let lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect();
            let end = lines.iter().position(|l| *l == "#[cfg(test)]").unwrap_or(lines.len());
            clock_in_code |= lines[..end]
                .iter()
                .any(|line| !line.trim_start().starts_with("//") && line.contains("js_sys::Date::now"));
        }
        assert!(escaped.is_empty(), "platform calls in the host crate: {escaped:#?}");
        assert!(scanned > 0, "anti-vacuity: the scan read no file");
        assert!(clock_in_code, "anti-vacuity: the one allowed platform call is CODE, not prose");
    }
```

  `1e16fe27` — the working tree's `worker/gen/`, whose `source.json` stamp equals `sourceDigest` over HEAD's
  sources: `{"bytes":1221719,"pages":18,"segments":168,"dataBytes":121296,"dataSection":122677,"gzip9":476412}`.

```js
// **The Worker module's figures, read off its own sections** (R1's cleanup
// debt 6; spec §2.7): what the root `Cargo.toml`'s `release-wasm` comment
// records for this module, re-read by one command so the reading never
// becomes a sentence nobody can check (M6.5b2's false sentence 6). Run after
// `npm run build:module`, the release build:
//
//   node scripts/module-figures.mjs gen/yokohama_worker_bg.wasm
//
// It prints the module's bytes and its `gzip -9` size, the pages its linear
// memory starts at — which every instance pays, a table object's second
// instance for one house copy (`copyOf`, `src/delivery.ts`) among them — and
// its data: the segments, their bytes, and the data section's encoded size.

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import { gzipSync } from "node:zlib";

/** The figures of the module `input` holds (WebAssembly core spec, binary
 *  format §5.5): its size, its one memory's initial pages, and its data
 *  segments' count and bytes and the data section's size. */
export function moduleFigures(input) {
  const b = input instanceof Uint8Array ? input : new Uint8Array(input);
  if (b.length < 8 || b[0] !== 0x00 || b[1] !== 0x61 || b[2] !== 0x73 || b[3] !== 0x6d) {
    throw new Error("not a WebAssembly module: it does not open with \\0asm");
  }
  let at = 8;
  const u32 = () => {
    let value = 0;
    let shift = 0;
    let byte;
    do {
      if (at >= b.length) throw new Error("a LEB128 number runs past the module's end");
      byte = b[at++];
      value += (byte & 0x7f) * 2 ** shift;
      shift += 7;
    } while (byte & 0x80);
    return value;
  };
  // An active segment's offset: ONE constant and `end`. Its immediate is
  // skipped by its LEB128 continuation bits, never by looking for 0x0b, which
  // an immediate may hold (offset 11 is the byte 0x0b).
  const offset = () => {
    const op = b[at++];
    if (op !== 0x41 && op !== 0x42) throw new Error(`a data segment's offset is not an i32 or i64 constant (opcode 0x${op.toString(16)})`);
    while (b[at++] & 0x80);
    if (b[at++] !== 0x0b) throw new Error("a data segment's offset is not a single constant");
  };
  const figures = { bytes: b.length, pages: null, segments: 0, dataBytes: 0, dataSection: 0 };
  while (at < b.length) {
    const id = b[at++];
    const size = u32();
    const end = at + size;
    if (id === 5) {
      if (u32() !== 1) throw new Error("the module declares more than one memory");
      const flags = u32();
      figures.pages = u32();
      if (flags & 1) u32();
    } else if (id === 11) {
      figures.dataSection = size;
      figures.segments = u32();
      for (let i = 0; i < figures.segments; i++) {
        const mode = u32();
        if (mode === 2) u32();
        if (mode !== 1) offset();
        const length = u32();
        figures.dataBytes += length;
        at += length;
      }
    }
    at = end;
  }
  if (figures.pages === null) throw new Error("the module declares no memory");
  return figures;
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) {
  if (process.argv.length !== 3) {
    console.error("usage: node scripts/module-figures.mjs <module.wasm>");
    process.exit(2);
  }
  const bytes = readFileSync(process.argv[2]);
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ ...moduleFigures(bytes), gzip9: gzipSync(bytes, { level: 9 }).length }));
}
```
